jobs.objective:
Write Burrow, one protocol for Squeekchain on Ethereum Sepolia where a Squeek NFT can be collateral, a marketplace and a Uniswap v4 hook both pay their fees to the same vault, and bonding sells discounted shares for assets the treasury keeps. Foundry, unit tests plus Sepolia fork tests, and a deployment script the operator runs. Do not deploy from the job.

The vault share token is named Burrow SQK, symbol bSQK, 18 decimals. Holding bSQK is the single way to earn from everything: loan interest, marketplace fees and swap fees all arrive as SQK into the vault and raise the share price. There is no rebase and no second staking contract.

LIVE ADDRESSES, every one verified by calling it; pass them to constructors, never hardcode. SQK 0x5501e1fa81be1c3f49225fa7668da0245d07db60, ERC20 with EIP-2612 permit, 18 decimals. Squeek NFT 0xcb98349c134ab983da5bfd80527dfe2552bdb70f, ERC721, 9987 minted. Squeekchain staking 0x4b67b739dfd832f4eac67a7aa3bc244fb74cea4f exposing deposit(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), withdraw(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), claim(address recipient), setClaimRecipient(address), claimable(address) view, basePower(address account, uint8 collection) view, accountPower(address) view, stakeOf(address) view, stake(uint256), unstake(uint256 amount, uint256 maxFee, uint64 deadline) returns (uint256 net), quoteUnstake(address,uint256) view, exitPolicy() view returning (uint16 minBps, uint16 maxBps, uint16 saturationBps, uint8 windowDays, uint256 pressureFloor), live value (200, 6000, 2000, 7, 21000000e18). Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0xE03A1074c86CFeDd5C142C4F04F1a1536e203543, PositionManager 0x429ba70129df741B2Ca2a85BC3A2a3328e5c09b4, Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3. The public Squeekchain docs are stale for this deployment: their claimable(uint8,uint256[]) and position(uint8,uint256) selectors revert here, so call no signature this objective has not listed.

1. BurrowValuer. creditLine(uint256[] tokenIds) view returns the SQK a borrower may owe, equal to summed NFT power times pricePerPower times ltvBps over 10000. Power per level comes from a table set at construction matching the published policy 1000, 3000, 7000, 15000, 31000, 63000 and upward. There is no NFT market on this chain so pricePerPower is governed and is the main attack surface: the owner may move it only through a two day timelock, by at most 20 percent per change, inside a hard band fixed at construction. ltvBps capped at 6000. Events on proposal and execution with old and new values.

2. BurrowVault, ERC20 bSQK, the lending core and the single fee sink.
Lenders: deposit(uint256 assets) mints shares against totalAssets, which is idle SQK plus principal outstanding plus accrued interest. withdraw(uint256 shares) burns and pays from idle SQK, with a clear custom error when utilisation leaves none.
Borrowers: openPosition(uint256[] tokenIds) pulls NFTs with safeTransferFrom, records each level, then calls staking.deposit and staking.setClaimRecipient so the collateral keeps earning for the vault. borrow(uint256 amount) requires debt plus amount at or below the valuer line. repay, repayAll and closePosition, which calls staking.withdraw and returns the NFTs once debt is zero. Interest is a fixed per second rate set at construction, capped at 50 percent a year, accrued on every touch.
Self repaying loans, the heart of this: sweepRewards() calls staking.claim for the vault and applies what arrives first to accrued interest, pro rata by each position's escrowed power, then to principal. While the hamster runs, the loans shrink by themselves. Anyone may call it.
Liquidation: when debt exceeds the line, liquidate(address borrower) lets anyone repay the debt and take the NFTs, with liquidationBonusBps capped at 1500, surplus recorded for the borrower. Liquidation reverts within one hour of a price change so governance cannot harvest borrowers.
Fee sink: donate(uint256 amount) pulls SQK and raises the share price without minting. The marketplace and the hook call it. Nothing else is needed to pay stakers.
Bonding: bond(address asset, uint256 amountOrId, uint256 minShares) accepts a Squeek NFT or a v4 SQK pool position, values an NFT through the valuer and a position through its SQK principal, mints bSQK worth that value plus bondDiscountBps capped at 2000, vesting linearly over bondVestingDays, claimable with claimBond(). Bonded assets stay in the treasury; bonded NFTs are staked so they earn.

3. BurrowMarket. list(uint256 tokenId, uint256 price), cancel, buy with SQK pulled from the buyer, and a Dutch auction used for liquidated NFTs that decays linearly from a premium to a floor over a fixed window. Every sale takes feeBps, capped at 500, and forwards it with vault.donate. Sellers are paid the rest in the same transaction.

4. BurrowHook, a Uniswap v4 hook for the SQK pool, built on BaseHook from v4-periphery against the PoolManager above. Permissions: afterSwap and afterSwapReturnDelta only, declared in getHookPermissions. In afterSwap, when the output currency is SQK, skim hookFeeBps capped at 100 of the output, take it from the PoolManager with poolManager.take, and forward it with vault.donate; when SQK is not the output currency, take nothing. A v4 hook only works if its address carries its permission bits, so the deployment script must mine a CREATE2 salt with HookMiner and deploy through the deterministic deployer, and a test must assert the deployed address has exactly the declared flags.

RULES. Solidity 0.8.26, OpenZeppelin for ERC20, ERC721Holder, SafeERC20, ReentrancyGuard and Ownable2Step, v4-core and v4-periphery for the hook. Every value moving external function nonReentrant, checks effects interactions. Custom errors only. Token id arrays capped at 32, strictly ascending, no duplicates. The owner has no path to user assets: the only powers are pausing new borrows, the timelocked price, and parameters inside their hard caps.

TESTS. Unit tests on a mock staking contract mirroring the real one: share price never falls on deposit or withdraw, borrow refused above the line, interest accrual, sweepRewards cutting debt, liquidation one wei either side of the boundary, the timelock rejecting early or oversized moves, the post move liquidation freeze, bond vesting and discount caps, marketplace fee routing into the share price, hook flags matching its address, and every custom error. Fork tests with vm.createSelectFork pinned to a Sepolia block, deal for SQK, vm.prank on a real Squeek holder, proving against the real deployed staking and NFT contracts a full round trip: escrow, still earning, borrow, sweep, repay, close. Invariants: total assets never fall except on withdrawal, and summed debt never exceeds summed credit lines. Ship script/Deploy.s.sol reading the live addresses and parameters from environment variables, mining the hook salt, deploying all four and wiring them, plus a README with every address, every assumption, the unaudited testnet only warning, and the exact forge commands.

jobs.objective: Launch two contracts in this repository on Robinhood Chain, in this order, without changing their logic. 1) src/ConditionalsV2.sol:ConditionalsV2, constructor (address owner = $owner, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IIntake intake = 0xa43e6f75ee006411f79ac1c84120606c2330de82, address oracleSigner = 0x5598aa9146215bc13eb26f2c692ad1461fd32982, address feeRecipient = 0x63bcf2d1483c7628d7d53704ff9c8199dc28d907). 2) src/ConditionalsZap.sol:ConditionalsZap, constructor (ConditionalsV2 conditionals = $contract:ConditionalsV2, IPoolManager poolManager = 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IERC20 usdg = 0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168). Neither constructor makes external calls. ConditionalsV2 is a conditional prediction market in IMD settled by the IdentityMD oracle. A market asks 'if CONDITION, will OUTCOME?' with four outcomes (index 2*world+side). A share of the outcome that happens pays 1 IMD. The creator deposits two 0.5 IMD oracle questions plus a neutral seed of b ln 4 that funds an LMSR maker (0.5 to 100 IMD b, Solady expWad and lnWad, log-sum-exp, rounding margins that keep makerBalance >= C(q) >= every q[i]); the seed is the creator's maximum loss. Until closeTime: stakeConditional (and stakeFor, paid by the caller and credited to an account) mints a complete set, sells the opposite side to the maker and buys more of the chosen side, so the stake is paid in its world on its side and refunded in the other world; buy, sell and exit trade with the maker with slippage bounds. Every maker trade pays 2%: half accrues to the creator in owed, 67/200 is sent to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD because IMD reverts on transfers to zero, and the rest accrues to feeRecipient in owed. When the maker is short of every outcome it turns those complete sets back into IMD (_absorb). The oracle flow is unchanged from Conditionals v1, IMD launch 2278, audited: after resolveTime anyone calls requestResolution, the contract pays the Intake with requestWithFailure for oracle.request@oracle-1 questions (panel 5, quorum 4, bool, panel evidence, window pinned to one Ethereum block, block.number - 10, since block.number on Robinhood Chain is the Ethereum block number) and stores keccak256 of each canonical question document. onOracleResult (selector 0x510379c7) accepts an answer only from the Intake for its own pending request, with the stored questionHash, answerType bool, panelSize and quorum at least the market's, agreed >= quorum, not expired, and an EIP-712 signature (domain IdentityMD Oracle, version 2) from the market's oracle signer. onFailure (0x5a0df71e) only clears the ask. Settlement pays 1 IMD per share of the outcome that happened and gives the creator the maker's residual and unspent budget. With no usable answer 30 days after resolveTime anyone can void: accounts get their net IMD in back excluding fees, pro rata if short, and the creator is paid last. The owner can only propose an oracle configuration for future markets behind a 3 day delay and set the fee recipient; it cannot touch trades, answers or open markets. No token, no proxy, no pause. ConditionalsZap has no owner and holds nothing between calls. stakeWithEth and stakeWithUsdg swap exact input through two hookless Uniswap v4 pools (USDG to ETH, fee 500, spacing 10; ETH to IMD, fee 10000, spacing 100) inside one PoolManager unlock, revert on a partial fill or below the caller's minImd, and call stakeFor for the caller. All positions, exits and payouts are in IMD in ConditionalsV2. ConditionalsV2's runtime is close to the 24,576 byte limit with optimizer_runs 1, so any fix must keep it under. legacy/ holds the deployed v1 for reference and is not built. The test suite (unit, fuzz, invariant, oracle conformance vector and a live-API question-hash vector; fork tests with FORK_ROBINHOOD=1) must keep passing.

Squeek Dome — IMD Job Brief
Full spec: https://github.com/0xtakoyaki22/squeek-dome
Goal: one-page, non-custodial Squeek holder + Keeper workbench on Sepolia. Any visitor can crank; an owner can batch-claim and merge. Real transactions only.
Scope: Sepolia only, chain 11155111 / 0xaa36a7, testnet assets have no value. No new contract, staking, or minting (minting paused). Use only exact values below. Reads via https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com, so page works before wallet connects. window.ethereum only for connect, chain switch, eth_sendTransaction.
Contracts
SqueekCore V3: 0x74665dAecA35A2303e767E76a2FF1FB6F93e119f
SqueekMining V6: 0x3beE588fC20dE788Bac17d33b41Da7346cb27EC4
SqueekNFT: 0x0eAF3E0d40A0a8E5a6Ac030b2459E9FB0B7905c6
DotGrid: 0x2dC7661D172fEf0FC900E0aD0f4ffCE68E8bfD75 (via tokenURI only)
Collection always 0. REWARD_PER_BLOCK Sepolia is 5,600 SQK (6,900 is launch). Block height = cumulativeBlockUnits / 1,000,000,000 (= blockHeight in Core.state()).
Exact functions
SqueekMining:
checkpoint() — permissionless, pays Sepolia gas, no reward. Call checkpointStatus() first.
checkpointStatus() returns (bool corePaused, uint64 nextRound, bool roundSettled)
state() returns 13 fields in this order: (uint256 minted, paid, totalWeight, rewardIndex, uint64 closedThroughBlock, lastActivationRound, uint256 weightActivationCursor, weightActivationCount, bool bootstrapped, uint64 processedThroughRound, closedCumulativeWork, uint96 closedCumulativeBlockUnits, uint32 closedWorkPerThousandBlocks). Pending = count - cursor. Query weightActivation only for cursor .. min(count, cursor+32)-1; if cursor==count, query none.
weightActivation(uint256 index) returns (uint64 round, uint192 addedWeight)
position(uint8, uint256) returns (uint64 activeWeight, pendingWeight, uint40 pendingRound, uint48 nextMergeBlock, uint8 level, uint256 lastIndex, accruedScaled). Level 0 = burned/unminted, no revert. pendingRound != 0 = cannot merge. accruedScaled is SQK x 2^128, NOT 18-decimal SQK — use claimable() for unclaimed SQK.
claimable(uint8, uint256[]) returns uint256, 18-decimal SQK claim would pay now. There is NO function called previewClaim. It needs 1-32 IDs, strictly ascending, no duplicates, but does NOT check ownership.
claim(uint8, uint256[]) — owner only, 1-32 IDs, strictly ascending, no duplicates, else InvalidClaim. Fraction stays on lowest ID.
merge(uint8, survivorId, donorId) — owner only, both owned by caller, distinct, same level 1-9 (max 10), pendingRound == 0, nextMergeBlock <= SqueekCore blockHeight. Donor burned permanently. Survivor +1 level, keeps ID/image and both credits.
SqueekCore state() returns 8 fields in this order: (uint64 settledThroughRound, cumulativeWork, uint96 cumulativeBlockUnits, uint64 blockHeight, uint96 blockProgress, uint32 workPerThousandBlocks, uint256 authorizationNonce, bool paused). Use settledThroughRound as frontier, blockHeight for merge checks. Do NOT use a version with workPerThousandBlocks before blockHeight, or genesis/lastSettlement timestamps — not in CoreState.
SqueekNFT: ownerOf(uint256), tokenURI(uint256). NOT ERC721Enumerable: tokenOfOwnerByIndex does NOT exist, never call it. Images: tokenURI -> decode base64 JSON -> render image field (inline SVG) as isolated image, never inject into markup. ownerOf/tokenURI REVERT for burned/unminted IDs — scans must catch reverts and skip, not crash.
IDs and ownership
Load IDs by: (a) user-typed IDs or RPC scan 1..30 via ownerOf, skipping reverts, (b) 1-click "Load Live Sepolia Sample Holder" scanning ownerOf 1..20 until an address owns >=2 live Squeeks, then scanning its IDs, (c) OPTIONAL API api.squeekchain.com/v1/owners/{address}/squeeks — unconfirmed, never depend on it.
STRICT: API is display only. Never take ID, amount, owner or eligibility from API into a transaction. Re-verify every candidate via RPC: ownerOf, position, claimable. Operators CANNOT claim/merge — only direct ownerOf can.
Panels (one top bar, one shared state)
Panel 1 — Keeper Crank (works with 0 Squeeks): show checkpointStatus + Mining state (processedThroughRound, totalWeight, minted, paid, pending count) + up to 32 waiting activations, vs settledThroughRound. Buttons: "Simulate Checkpoint (eth_call)" showing OK or exact decoded revert; "Crank Checkpoint (Send Tx)" only when corePaused==false and roundSettled==true. When roundSettled==false, keep Simulate active and state sending now would revert and waste gas — never present force-send as success. After receipt, link tx hash and re-read status/state. No manual roundSettled toggle — state only from RPC.
Panel 2 — Batch Claimer: connected wallet OR pasted/sample holder in Inspect Mode (Send only if connected wallet owns every selected ID). Table: ID, thumbnail, level, activeWeight, pending round, nextMergeBlock, unclaimed SQK from claimable(0,[id]). Select 1-32, auto-sort ascending, dedupe, reject level 0 / unowned. Show batch claimable(0,sortedIds), highlight lowest ID keeping fraction, simulate, then send claim(0,sortedIds).
Panel 3 — Merge Arena: only eligible pairs (distinct, same level, pendingRound==0 both, nextMergeBlock<=blockHeight both). Side-by-side images, level, activeWeight, combined unclaimed SQK. Swap toggle must instantly re-render BOTH cards, SQK amounts, combined total, and modal IDs; a swap changing only hidden dialog values is a FAIL. "Prepare Merge" opens a blocking modal naming BOTH IDs: "Token #DONOR will be BURNED PERMANENTLY and cannot be restored. Token #SURVIVOR will advance one level, keep its ID/image, and inherit both credits." Only after a confirmation checkbox, simulate, then send merge(0,survivorId,donorId).
Transaction wiring
Check eth_chainId == 0xaa36a7, switch if wrong. Real eth_call to Mining, then eth_sendTransaction with from, to=Mining, data, value 0x0. Wait for receipt, link https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/{hash}. No setTimeout fakes. Decode reverts with Mining errors (RoundNotSettled, CorePaused, InvalidClaim, InvalidPosition, InvalidMerge, Unauthorized); if undecodable, fall back to checkpointStatus, never raw hex alone.
Acceptance (all must pass): 1. Real calldata + eth_call + chain check + eth_sendTransaction, no mocks. 2. Unconnected Inspect Mode via public RPC, incl. 1-click sample holder. 3. 0-Squeek wallet can simulate Panel 1 and, when roundSettled, send checkpoint(). 4. Out-of-order claim IDs auto-sort; duplicates/unowned blocked. 5. Merge cannot send without burn modal naming both IDs. 6. Desktop + mobile; at 375px top bar wraps, no truncation/scroll to buttons.
Out of scope: custom contract, staking, minting, prediction markets, games, leaderboards, bots, music, art, simulator-only buttons.

Produce ONE test edition of Open Interest's daily crypto-discourse brief through the paper's full pipeline: three independent drafts, one selection, one adversarial review. The edition spec that every draft must follow in full:

Produce today's TEST EDITION of a daily crypto-discourse brief. Plain text
only, under 900 words total. This is a drafting rehearsal: quality of voice
and sourcing is the entire point.

FIRST: fetch and obey the house style guide at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/style-guide.html
Its rules are binding: declarative sentences, numbers with context, no banned
words (delve, landscape, game-changer, seamless, robust, unlock, tapestry,
paradigm, "it's worth noting", "ever-evolving", emoji), at most one em dash
in the whole edition, absolute dates only, no financial advice.

SOURCES: open platforms only (Farcaster, research blogs, Mirror, Substack,
governance forums, GitHub; X only via open mirrors). Prefer the last 24-48
hours. A claim that cannot be verified against an open-platform source is
cut, and the cut is noted in METHOD. When sources conflict on a figure,
prefer the primary source; otherwise state the range and attribute both.
Cite with the full source URL in square brackets; for these plain-text test
editions this overrides the style guide's numbered-citation example.

STRUCTURE (exactly):
LEAD: a headline (short declarative sentence ending in a full stop), a
2-sentence deck, then 150-250 words. Every factual claim carries a source
URL in brackets.
ALSO TODAY: exactly three items: category tag, one-sentence headline with
full stop, 2-3 sentence summary, at least one source URL each.
READING LIST: 3-5 links, each with a 1-line reason.
METHOD: one closing paragraph: sources swept, hours covered, any items cut
for failed verification and any claims resting on secondary sources.

ACCEPTANCE: the structure above, complete; every claim sourced; under 900
words; no banned words; headlines are declarative sentences with full stops;
absolute dates only (no 'this week', 'yesterday', 'the weekend'); at most
one em dash in the whole edition.

CONTINUITY: before drafting, fetch https://openinterest-ai.github.io/paper/rehearsal.html and the prior test editions linked there. Do NOT lead with a story a prior edition led with unless a material NEW development happened after that edition published; an ongoing story without a new development may appear only in ALSO TODAY, and only with the new angle stated.

jobs.objective:
# Squeek Sprouts — IMD objective (paste into explorer.imd.fun/launch)

Build "Squeek Sprouts": a single-page, static, browser idle-farming game for Squeekchain where crops grow ONLY from the real wheel work of Squeektoshi, the hamster that powers Squeekchain. It is a game people play and come back to, not a dashboard.

## Core idea
- The player owns a 3x3 pixel-art garden. Each crop needs a fixed amount of "wheel work" (wheel passes counted by Squeekchain) to ripen.
- Growth = currentCumulativeWork - workWhenPlanted. When the hamster naps, the garden sleeps (night scene). When he runs, it grows, even while the player is away (idle game).
- Harvesting while the hamster is running is a "fresh harvest": 2x crumbs and a 15% chance of a GOLDEN crop worth 5x.

## Live data (public, CORS-enabled, no key)
- Poll `GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status` every 15 s.
  - `measurement.cumulativeWorkUnits` (string number): the growth counter.
  - `measurement.counterEpoch`: if it changes, or the counter goes down, rebase every planted crop so it keeps the progress it had (planted = newWork - (lastWork - planted)).
  - `measurement.coreStatus` (`SPINNING` | `IDLE`), `rpmMilli` (/1000 = RPM), `speedMmPerSecond`, `distanceMm`, `freshness` (`online` or stale; if not online show "signal stale, garden paused" and do not count it as running).
  - `builder.projected.blockHeight`: show as Squeek block height.
- Optional fallback: if the API fails twice, switch to a clearly labelled DEMO wheel (simulated naps/runs, separate save slot) so the page never looks broken.

## Economy (keep these numbers)
| Crop | Work to ripen | Seed cost | Sells for | Unlocks after crumbs earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheel Radish | 40 | free | 6 | 0 |
| Zoomie Carrot | 120 | 8 | 20 | 30 |
| Round Pumpkin | 400 | 30 | 70 | 150 |
| Rim Sunflower | 1000 | 90 | 190 | 500 |
| Moon Melon | 3000 | 260 | 600 | 1500 |
- Start with 10 crumbs and 3 open plots. Plots 4–9 cost 25, 60, 120, 250, 500, 1000 crumbs.
- Save state in localStorage (wrap in try/catch). A "Reset garden" button needs two taps (no confirm() dialogs).

## Screens and feel
- Left panel: a pixel-art canvas of Squeektoshi on his wheel. The wheel spins at a speed scaled from the live RPM; the hamster bobs when running and sleeps with "zzz" under a moon when idle. Below it: status pill (RUNNING · GROWING / NAPPING · GARDEN SLEEPS / STALE / DEMO), work counter, RPM, speed (m/s), distance (km), block height, and "work grown here".
- Main panel: seed shed (each seed shows its pixel sprite, cost, work needed, price, or lock state), the 3x3 garden (tap empty plot = plant selected seed, tap growing plot = shows work left, tap ripe plot = harvest, tap locked plot = buy), progress bars, a glowing border on ripe crops.
- Garden journal: timestamped log of ripe crops, harvests, golden crops, unlocks, counter restarts.
- All crop sprites are drawn on canvas in code (4 growth stages each, distinct ripe shapes: radish, carrot, pumpkin, sunflower, crescent-marked moon melon). No emoji, no stock images. Fonts: Silkscreen + VT323 from Google Fonts. Warm dark palette (soil browns, leaf greens, gold accent).
- Must work on phones (garden stays 3 columns, panels stack).

## Stretch (only if cheap and safe)
- "Sign in with wallet" via a signed message (no gas, no approvals) to show the player's short address on a local high-score card. Never request transactions or token approvals.

## Delivery
- Pure static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no backend, no private keys, no transactions.
- Host on IPFS/ENS and deliver the code to GitHub. README explains the data source and the growth/rebase math.
- Footer: "Reads Squeekchain's public API. No wallet, no gas, nothing is signed."

Revision to the existing website only. Do not redeploy or modify the contract, its address, the ABI or the deployment config (imd-deployment.json). Keep all current behaviour, layout, styling and data reads unchanged.

1. RENAME. The project is now called "Squeek's First Road Trip" (replacing "Hamster Road Trip"). Update it everywhere visible: page title, loading text, header wordmark, hero and section text, help text, meta and Open Graph/Twitter titles and descriptions, the share image (share.svg), favicon labels, README and docs. PROJECT
Hamster Road Trip is a community game. The real Squeekchain hamster's wheel distance moves a marker across a world map, starting at Miami Beach, Florida. The community votes on where the hamster travels next. The hamster does the walking and the community chooses the route.

HOW THE GAME WORKS
1. The game runs in 24-hour epochs. During an epoch, each wallet votes once for one destination from a fixed list of 64 destinations (ids 0 to 63).
2. When an epoch ends, the destination with the most votes wins (ties go to the lowest id) and is added to the end of the route queue.
3. The marker travels to the first destination in the queue, then the next, and so on. Progress is driven only by the hamster: distance travelled = real wheel km x SCALE, where SCALE is one config value (default 100) shown on screen.
4. If the queue is empty or the wheel is idle, the hamster rests (sleeping animation and a short story line) and waits.
5. Arriving at a stop shows a postcard: place name, a one-line fun fact and a pixel-art icon. Every arrival is added to a trip log.
6. A Navigator leaderboard ranks wallets by how many of their votes matched winning destinations.

Constructor takes epochSeconds (86400) and destinationCount (64). vote(destinationId): one vote per wallet per epoch, rejects ids out of range. finalize(epoch): callable by anyone once the epoch has ended, records the winner once. Repair the existing delivery from job a5886b35-7174-42da-9056-421ecd5001df. Base: https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-2725-stratoks-restore-wallet at 4671102884260ac798821bd32bfad7f462aacf7f. Preserve the current Expanse world and walletless viewing. This is source, frontend preview and owner-run backend delivery; do not access or deploy to production.

1. RECOVERABLE SESSION CHECKS
shared/visitor-auth-client.js currently destroys a valid session and queues logout on any refresh error. Retain the credential on 429, 5xx, offline and timeout, show a temporary unverified/unavailable state, and retry with bounded backoff/jitter and Retry-After support. Only an authoritative invalid-session response ends that session. Never represent an unconfirmed session as freshly verified. Explicit logout and account/network/provider/world changes must still clear obsolete auth immediately and revoke safely. Prevent stale responses and duplicate refreshes; preserve retry/cancel flows.

2. PROXY-AWARE RATE LIMITS
The server keys all visitors on the Caddy connection IP; about 30 tabs exhaust the shared 60/min bucket. Add explicit owner-configured trusted proxies and correct client address extraction ONLY through that trust boundary. Ignore forged forwarded headers from untrusted peers; document Caddy header sanitization and private backend binding. Separate bounded challenge/verify abuse limits from authenticated session polling. Keep global/body/concurrency limits. Test 50 verified sessions behind a trusted proxy polling at the shipped cadence while another visitor signs in; no false expiration or unfair shared-IP lockout.

3. BOUNDED PROFILES AND SESSIONS WITHOUT PERMANENT LOCKOUT
Throwaway addresses currently fill the durable 10,000-profile store forever; one signer can consume all 2,000 sessions. Add a documented bounded retention/admission policy that recovers at capacity, with per-peer/time signup controls and expiry/eviction of inactive records as appropriate. Do not promise Sybil-proof identity. Preserve retained profiles atomically across restart and disclose retention. Bound active sessions per address and origin; new sessions cannot monopolize capacity. Test small configured limits, many distinct disposable signers, repeated one-signer sessions, expiry and restart recovery. Never silently erase world or resident memory.

4. SIGNED MESSAGE AND CANCELLATION
Validate world identity against the actual server's structured format, not an assumed UUID (existing world IDs may be world-20260101-0). Reject control characters/newlines and malformed fields in world/domain/origin/URI before opening a wallet prompt; reconstruct and verify the exact server-issued message. Keep address/chain/origin/world/nonce/expiry binding and replay protection. Publicly displayed nonce must not be a revocation credential for an established session. Use a separate unpredictable cancellation secret or an equivalently secure design to cancel late verification without introducing account-switch races. test cancellation before/during/after verification and wrong-secret/origin attempts.

5. REPRODUCIBLE DEPLOYMENT
Fix Docker COPY ownership/permissions so USER node can read modules even from umask 077 checkouts. Run import checks as that runtime user; retain shared/ modules. Provide correct Expanse Caddy/compose routing on 8788, including /api/auth/*, /api/expanse/* and static assets; remove legacy 8787 guidance. Explicit AUTH_URI/origin configuration, private profile volume, backup and rollback instructions. Build AND start linux/arm64 image on native ARM or documented emulation; probe health/config and disposable-signer login/logout.

6. UI AND REGRESSIONS
Remove repeated unavailable-backend copy and duplicate screen-reader status announcements. Preserve EIP-6963 provider choice, legacy fallback, current HUD, inspector, camera and mobile controls. Separate wallet connection from server authentication. No approvals, transfers, contracts, paid gameplay or new token. Preserve population, identities, brain weights, goals, signals, terrain, schema and live configuration. Demo must remain clearly labelled.

DELIVER AND PROVE
Add regression tests reproducing each defect before the fix and passing after. Run existing backend/client/typecheck/build suites and real HTTP crypto tests. Exercise browser login/logout, transient failures, account/network switch races, 320/390px mobile layout and anonymous viewing with disposable signers; distinguish simulated providers from actual extensions/devices. Verify copied-world load/save/restart without changing simulation behavior. Publish updated source and static preview, API/setup/rollback docs, raw test evidence and a finding-to-fix matrix with commit/file/test references. List unresolved issues explicitly; accepted task status alone is not evidence they are fixed.

jobs.objective:
Build and publish "Squeek Pouch", an original, playable single-page browser arcade game for Squeekchain (the hamster-powered proof-of-work toychain on Ethereum Sepolia, chainId 11155111). This is for the Squeekchain Genesis Code lane: a real game whose gameplay is driven by Squeekchain's live data, not a dashboard or landing page. English UI.

GAMEPLAY
- The player is a hamster on the ground at the bottom of the screen. Seeds fall from the top. Move left/right (drag/touch on mobile, arrow keys or A/D on desktop) to catch them in the cheek pouches.
- Sunflower seed = +1 to the pouch. Golden "SQK" seed = +5. Pouch capacity 15; the hamster's cheeks visibly swell as the pouch fills and its movement speed drops by up to 55% when full.
- Falling pebbles: touching one costs 1 life (3 lives) and spills all unbanked seeds in the pouch.
- Banking: run to the burrow at the left edge (or press a "Burrow" button / Space to auto-run home) to bank the pouch into the score. Only banked seeds count. This creates a risk/reward loop: bank often and safe, or carry a fat pouch for a bigger boosted deposit.
- Rounds last 90 seconds; difficulty (fall speed, pebble rate) ramps over the round. Game over at 0 lives or time up. Show final banked score and a local best score (localStorage only). "Play again" button.

LIVE SQUEEKCHAIN INTEGRATION (required, core to gameplay)
- Data source: GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status (public, CORS enabled). Poll every 5 seconds from the browser. Do not invent other endpoints; verify field names against the live response.
- Fields used: measurement.coreStatus ("IDLE" | "ACTIVE" | "COUNTER_FAULT"), measurement.rpmMilli (wheel rpm x 1000), measurement.freshness ("online" | "stale"), measurement.observedAt, measurement.staleAfterSeconds, measurement.provenance, measurement.distanceMm; builder.projected.blockHeight and builder.projected.blockProgress (progress toward the next Squeek block, in units of 1,000,000,000 = 100%; fall back to builder.anchor if projected is missing).
- Wheel Boost: while the real hamster Squeektoshi is ACTIVE and data is fresh, every bank deposit is multiplied by min(3, 1 + rpm/40). Idle = x1. While ACTIVE, seeds also spawn about 25% faster and fall about 15% faster.
- Block Storm: if builder.projected.blockHeight increases while a round is in progress (a real Squeek block was mined), trigger a 6-second "Block Storm" in which mostly golden SQK seeds rain down quickly with few pebbles, with a banner "REAL BLOCK #<height> MINED!".
- Visuals tied to data: a large background hamster wheel rotates at the real rpm; scene is warm/lit when the hamster is running and a night palette when idle.
- Live status panel above the game: running/resting state with a colored dot, current rpm, Squeek block height, % of next block mined with a progress bar, current wheel boost, and a line naming the data source.
- Fallback: if the API fails twice in a row, switch to a simulated wheel and clearly label it "Offline demo - SIMULATED data, not real" in the status panel. Never present simulated data as real. Resume live data automatically when the API recovers. Stale data (freshness "stale" or older than staleAfterSeconds) counts as idle and is labeled stale.

LOOK
- Cozy arcade style: dark purple night background (#1b1430), warm orange accent (#ffb43b), cream text, rounded friendly font, big tappable buttons. On-screen text is short and playful (title, rules, HUD: banked score, pouch x/15, lives, timer).

CONSTRAINTS
- Static site only (HTML/CSS/JS, may be built with Vite + TypeScript), no backend, no server, no accounts.
- No wallet connection, no signatures, no tokens, no wagering, no payments, no analytics or tracking, no collection of user data. Points only. Only the local best score is stored in localStorage.
- Mobile-first and responsive (iPhone Safari and desktop Chrome), touch-action none on the canvas, no page scrolling while playing. Canvas rendering with devicePixelRatio scaling. Cute hand-drawn-style hamster drawn in code (no copyrighted assets).
- Title screen explains the rules and the live-data mechanics in 3 short paragraphs, and states "Points only - no wallet, no tokens".
- Footer: "Built for Squeekchain - live data from api.squeekchain.com" with a link to https://squeekchain.com.

DELIVERABLES
- Hosted static site on IPFS, plus source code and a README explaining gameplay, exactly which Squeekchain API fields are used and how, the fallback behaviour, and how to run locally.
- Tests: unit tests for the boost formula, block-progress parsing, block-height-increase detection (including no trigger on first load and no duplicate trigger for the same height), stale/offline fallback switching and labeling, and banking/pebble/pouch-capacity rules. A headless browser check that the page loads with no console errors.

jobs.objective:
STRATOKS — LIVING WORLD BEHAVIOR AND VISUAL REPAIR

BASE: https://github.com/kilicsln/stratoks at d0ee752960b66ac04c8f36964e195d9409d97bfb. Extend this exact source, including its verified wallet fixes. Deliver integrated code, original usable art, a static website preview and owner-run backend package. Do not deploy to production. No new token, contracts or paid gameplay.

PROBLEM: The current world is carpeted with identical log sprites, repeated huts and rigid terrain. Residents' meaningful decisions are hard to observe. Target a richly illustrated isometric living world, not a landing page, decorative screenshot or a few looping occupations. Keep the original yellow sprout-headed STRATOKS species; no rabbits or copied TV/game assets.

1. DIAGNOSE AND REPAIR RESOURCE CLUTTER
Trace resource production, consumption, storage, persistence and rendering. Establish whether logs represent real stocks, rendering duplication or runaway production; report evidence. Fix the actual causes. Bound visual density through quantity-aware piles, storage representations and zoom-dependent aggregation; retain exact selectable quantities. Do not delete stocks, hide bugs, reset the world or stop legitimate production merely to make screenshots attractive. If surplus accumulation is real, add demand/storage-aware decisions and meaningful existing construction/repair/tool consumption, not arbitrary invisible sinks. Test resource accounting and long-run growth.

2. MEANINGFUL AUTONOMOUS ACTIVITY
Extend the existing needs, memory, goals and brain. Implement and demonstrate three connected activity chains: acquire/transport/store/use materials for tool or shelter repair; acquire/prepare/share food according to hunger and local stocks; explore for a needed resource and return or settle when resources and shelter permit. Fishing is only one example. Decisions must depend on local perception, needs, costs and remembered outcomes, with interruption/replanning when conditions change. Do not assign an endless fixed occupation to each resident. Use bounded per-resident work and record decision evidence. Preserve existing learning; show its actual contribution without claiming consciousness, full fly-brain emulation or invented language. Use real state-derived icons/activity descriptions rather than fabricated thoughts. Keep births, scarcity and deaths systemic.

3. WORLD ART AND GEOGRAPHY
Provide coherent original game-ready assets with consistent perspective and lighting. Improve organic shoreline transitions, terrain edges, vegetation, rocks, water and depth, retaining navigable topology. Distinguish forest/grassland, desert, islands and cold regions already supported by the world; preserve exploration and chunk streaming. Avoid checkerboard biome borders and repeating wall-like tile edges. Render structure function, condition, construction stage and climate visibly; vary existing huts/workplaces/storage without inventing fake functioning buildings. Never move resources or residents merely for composition. Animate actual carrying, working, resting and helping states with appropriate props and direction; bind visuals to simulation events, not random decorative loops. Include asset sources, licenses and atlas manifests.

4. PROFESSIONAL WORLD-FIRST INTERFACE
Replace the oversized 'A world taking root' card with a compact contextual control. Use an unobtrusive dark forest/charcoal HUD, warm gold accents, disciplined typography and consistent icons. Keep most of the screen available for the world. Provide compact status, resident goal/action/need inspector, legible minimap, search/follow and camera reset/zoom. Move tick/polling/debug details into diagnostics. No marketing cards or large overlays. Preserve wallet provider choice, verified sessions, logout/retry and walletless viewing. Support 390px mobile and 1440px desktop without covering critical controls.

5. PRESERVATION AND ACCEPTANCE
Keep world identity, resident identities, memories, learned weights, inventory and visitor profiles. Any necessary schema migration must be explicit, tested on a copy, and backed up; no reseeding. Do not require private data or credentials. Use a representative persisted schema-5 fixture with 300+ residents and accumulated resources; state clearly that it is a fixture. Verify load/save/restart and pre/post-migration invariants. Run existing tests, typecheck/build and wallet regressions. Demonstrate all three activity chains in multi-seed unattended runs; publish events, frequencies, failures and durations, not hand-triggered animations alone. Measure tick time, memory and browser frame times; no unsupported 60fps claims. Supply before/after browser captures at multiple zoom levels, crowded settlements and contrasting biomes. Independently review accounting, behavior evidence and visual integration. Publish source/commit, preview, test evidence, setup/rollback notes and unresolved limitations. A mockup or unchanged map under new menus is not completion.

jobs.objective:
Project goal:
A funny, chaotic endless-runner game featuring a customizable hamster (Squeektoshi style). Players dress up their hamster with absurd, meme-y, and slightly 恶趣味 accessories, then run on the wheel collecting points while dodging obstacles. Real Squeekchain data from Sepolia influences the game. High scores must be submitted and displayed via an on-chain leaderboard.

Core Requirements:
- Read real data from SqueekCore on Sepolia: 0x74665dAecA35A2303e767E76a2FF1FB6F93e119f
  Or use https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/core (and related endpoints) for blockHeight, progress, settled work, etc.
- Display current Squeek block height, round progress, and a live “hamster spinning” indicator.
- Fully playable in browser (no login needed to play). Mobile-friendly if possible.
- Clean, cute-but-chaotic visual style. Use simple Canvas, SVG, or CSS animations.
- Include a clear README explaining the game, how it uses real Squeekchain data, customization, the on-chain leaderboard, and that this is a community project for the Squeekchain / Buildooooor badge.

Gameplay:
- Endless scrolling wheel/path.
- Player controls: left/right move or jump (keyboard + click/tap).
- Collectibles (seeds, SQK coins, random funny items) that give points.
- Obstacles that end the run or knock the hamster off.
- Score multiplier or temporary boost when a real new Squeek block is completed.
- Funny hit effects and visual feedback.
- After a run ends, player can submit their score on-chain with a short nickname.

Customization (must have, make it funny and 恶趣味):
Before starting a run, player can equip the hamster with:
- Headwear (choose one): Sunglasses (墨镜), Pressure cooker (高压锅) on head, Traffic cone, Banana peel hat, Dunce cap, Tiny crown, VR headset
- Handheld item (choose one): Sword, Toy gun / water gun, Toilet brush (厕所刷), Toilet plunger (吸马桶的), Giant spoon, Rubber chicken, Selfie stick, Lightsaber (simple visual)
- Optional extra (choose one): Mustache, Cape, Tiny rocket backpack, Googly eyes overlay

The equipped items must be visibly rendered on the hamster during the run. Different combinations can give tiny funny score bonuses or visual effects.

On-chain Leaderboard (mandatory):
- Deploy a simple smart contract on Sepolia testnet that stores high scores.
- Players connect wallet and submit score + nickname after a run.
- Contract should store at least the top scores (e.g. top 50 or top 100) with nickname, score, and player address.
- Frontend must display a public leaderboard that reads directly from the contract (anyone can view it without connecting a wallet).
- Use Foundry for the contract, include basic tests, and deploy it on Sepolia.
- Provide the deployed contract address in the README and frontend.

Tech & Delivery:
- Frontend: static single-page site (HTML + CSS + JS + Canvas) or simple React/Next.js. Wallet connection for score submission only.
- Contract: Foundry + Solidity on Sepolia.
- Provide the live site link and deployed contract address after build.
- Keep it an MVP: fun, playable, and clearly tied to Squeekchain data. Not a full commercial game.

Make the whole thing silly, chaotic, and shareable. The more absurd the hamster looks, the better.

versions.objective:
Write Burrow, one protocol for Squeekchain on Ethereum Sepolia where a Squeek NFT can be collateral, a marketplace and a Uniswap v4 hook both pay their fees to the same vault, and bonding sells discounted shares for assets the treasury keeps. Foundry, unit tests plus Sepolia fork tests, and a deployment script the operator runs. Do not deploy from the job.

The vault share token is named Burrow SQK, symbol bSQK, 18 decimals. Holding bSQK is the single way to earn from everything: loan interest, marketplace fees and swap fees all arrive as SQK into the vault and raise the share price. There is no rebase and no second staking contract.

LIVE ADDRESSES, every one verified by calling it; pass them to constructors, never hardcode. SQK 0x5501e1fa81be1c3f49225fa7668da0245d07db60, ERC20 with EIP-2612 permit, 18 decimals. Squeek NFT 0xcb98349c134ab983da5bfd80527dfe2552bdb70f, ERC721, 9987 minted. Squeekchain staking 0x4b67b739dfd832f4eac67a7aa3bc244fb74cea4f exposing deposit(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), withdraw(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), claim(address recipient), setClaimRecipient(address), claimable(address) view, basePower(address account, uint8 collection) view, accountPower(address) view, stakeOf(address) view, stake(uint256), unstake(uint256 amount, uint256 maxFee, uint64 deadline) returns (uint256 net), quoteUnstake(address,uint256) view, exitPolicy() view returning (uint16 minBps, uint16 maxBps, uint16 saturationBps, uint8 windowDays, uint256 pressureFloor), live value (200, 6000, 2000, 7, 21000000e18). Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0xE03A1074c86CFeDd5C142C4F04F1a1536e203543, PositionManager 0x429ba70129df741B2Ca2a85BC3A2a3328e5c09b4, Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3. The public Squeekchain docs are stale for this deployment: their claimable(uint8,uint256[]) and position(uint8,uint256) selectors revert here, so call no signature this objective has not listed.

1. BurrowValuer. creditLine(uint256[] tokenIds) view returns the SQK a borrower may owe, equal to summed NFT power times pricePerPower times ltvBps over 10000. Power per level comes from a table set at construction matching the published policy 1000, 3000, 7000, 15000, 31000, 63000 and upward. There is no NFT market on this chain so pricePerPower is governed and is the main attack surface: the owner may move it only through a two day timelock, by at most 20 percent per change, inside a hard band fixed at construction. ltvBps capped at 6000. Events on proposal and execution with old and new values.

2. BurrowVault, ERC20 bSQK, the lending core and the single fee sink.
Lenders: deposit(uint256 assets) mints shares against totalAssets, which is idle SQK plus principal outstanding plus accrued interest. withdraw(uint256 shares) burns and pays from idle SQK, with a clear custom error when utilisation leaves none.
Borrowers: openPosition(uint256[] tokenIds) pulls NFTs with safeTransferFrom, records each level, then calls staking.deposit and staking.setClaimRecipient so the collateral keeps earning for the vault. borrow(uint256 amount) requires debt plus amount at or below the valuer line. repay, repayAll and closePosition, which calls staking.withdraw and returns the NFTs once debt is zero. Interest is a fixed per second rate set at construction, capped at 50 percent a year, accrued on every touch.
Self repaying loans, the heart of this: sweepRewards() calls staking.claim for the vault and applies what arrives first to accrued interest, pro rata by each position's escrowed power, then to principal. While the hamster runs, the loans shrink by themselves. Anyone may call it.
Liquidation: when debt exceeds the line, liquidate(address borrower) lets anyone repay the debt and take the NFTs, with liquidationBonusBps capped at 1500, surplus recorded for the borrower. Liquidation reverts within one hour of a price change so governance cannot harvest borrowers.
Fee sink: donate(uint256 amount) pulls SQK and raises the share price without minting. The marketplace and the hook call it. Nothing else is needed to pay stakers.
Bonding: bond(address asset, uint256 amountOrId, uint256 minShares) accepts a Squeek NFT or a v4 SQK pool position, values an NFT through the valuer and a position through its SQK principal, mints bSQK worth that value plus bondDiscountBps capped at 2000, vesting linearly over bondVestingDays, claimable with claimBond(). Bonded assets stay in the treasury; bonded NFTs are staked so they earn.

3. BurrowMarket. list(uint256 tokenId, uint256 price), cancel, buy with SQK pulled from the buyer, and a Dutch auction used for liquidated NFTs that decays linearly from a premium to a floor over a fixed window. Every sale takes feeBps, capped at 500, and forwards it with vault.donate. Sellers are paid the rest in the same transaction.

4. BurrowHook, a Uniswap v4 hook for the SQK pool, built on BaseHook from v4-periphery against the PoolManager above. Permissions: afterSwap and afterSwapReturnDelta only, declared in getHookPermissions. In afterSwap, when the output currency is SQK, skim hookFeeBps capped at 100 of the output, take it from the PoolManager with poolManager.take, and forward it with vault.donate; when SQK is not the output currency, take nothing. A v4 hook only works if its address carries its permission bits, so the deployment script must mine a CREATE2 salt with HookMiner and deploy through the deterministic deployer, and a test must assert the deployed address has exactly the declared flags.

RULES. Solidity 0.8.26, OpenZeppelin for ERC20, ERC721Holder, SafeERC20, ReentrancyGuard and Ownable2Step, v4-core and v4-periphery for the hook. Every value moving external function nonReentrant, checks effects interactions. Custom errors only. Token id arrays capped at 32, strictly ascending, no duplicates. The owner has no path to user assets: the only powers are pausing new borrows, the timelocked price, and parameters inside their hard caps.

TESTS. Unit tests on a mock staking contract mirroring the real one: share price never falls on deposit or withdraw, borrow refused above the line, interest accrual, sweepRewards cutting debt, liquidation one wei either side of the boundary, the timelock rejecting early or oversized moves, the post move liquidation freeze, bond vesting and discount caps, marketplace fee routing into the share price, hook flags matching its address, and every custom error. Fork tests with vm.createSelectFork pinned to a Sepolia block, deal for SQK, vm.prank on a real Squeek holder, proving against the real deployed staking and NFT contracts a full round trip: escrow, still earning, borrow, sweep, repay, close. Invariants: total assets never fall except on withdrawal, and summed debt never exceeds summed credit lines. Ship script/Deploy.s.sol reading the live addresses and parameters from environment variables, mining the hook salt, deploying all four and wiring them, plus a README with every address, every assumption, the unaudited testnet only warning, and the exact forge commands.

versions.objective:
Deliverables: (1) a smart contract on Sepolia, (2) a website, (3) the full source code of both published on GitHub in a public repository, (4) the website hosted on IPFS.

PROJECT
Hamster Road Trip is a community game. The real Squeekchain hamster's wheel distance moves a marker across a world map, starting at Miami Beach, Florida. The community votes on where the hamster travels next. The hamster does the walking and the community chooses the route.

HOW THE GAME WORKS
1. The game runs in 24-hour epochs. During an epoch, each wallet votes once for one destination from a fixed list of 64 destinations (ids 0 to 63).
2. When an epoch ends, the destination with the most votes wins (ties go to the lowest id) and is added to the end of the route queue.
3. The marker travels to the first destination in the queue, then the next, and so on. Progress is driven only by the hamster: distance travelled = real wheel km x SCALE, where SCALE is one config value (default 100) shown on screen.
4. If the queue is empty or the wheel is idle, the hamster rests (sleeping animation and a short story line) and waits.
5. Arriving at a stop shows a postcard: place name, a one-line fun fact and a pixel-art icon. Every arrival is added to a trip log.
6. A Navigator leaderboard ranks wallets by how many of their votes matched winning destinations.

CONTRACT: RoadTripVotes (Sepolia)
Constructor takes epochSeconds (86400) and destinationCount (64). vote(destinationId): one vote per wallet per epoch, rejects ids out of range. finalize(epoch): callable by anyone once the epoch has ended, records the winner once. Views: currentEpoch, votesFor(epoch, id), winnerOf(epoch), hasVoted(epoch, wallet). Events for votes and finalization. No owner, admin, upgrade path, token or payments. Foundry tests, and an independent review of the contract before deployment.

WEBSITE (static, no backend)
- Reads the deployed contract address and ABI from the deployment config.
- Distance is read in the browser from the public Squeekchain API (https://docs.squeekchain.com/developers/api/). Confirm exact endpoints from those docs and do not guess. The solid marker uses settled work only. Optionally show a faint ghost marker for provisional progress. Handle API failures gracefully.
- Map: Leaflet or MapLibre with an open tile provider (not the openstreetmap.org tile servers), with attribution shown. Routes come from a free open routing service and are cached in the browser. Where no road route exists (oceans), draw a great-circle arc with a ship or plane icon.
- Destinations: 64 family-friendly places worldwide, mixing nearby and overseas, in a static data file with id, name, coordinates and one fun fact. Facts must be original or properly credited.
- Voting: wallet connect, choose a destination, send the vote. Show the epoch countdown, live vote counts, the route queue, the trip log and the leaderboard. Voting costs Sepolia test ETH, so link to a public Sepolia faucet. No free-text player input anywhere.
- The site also works read-only without a wallet (watch the marker, see votes).

LOOK AND FEEL: SQUEEKCHAIN STYLE
Dark retro LED dot-matrix aesthetic: near-black background, glowing dot-grid details, uppercase monospace or condensed headings, and neon accents (purple, teal, amber). Dotted route line and a dark map theme. The hamster marker is a small pixel-art hamster in a wheel, animated running when the wheel is active and curled asleep when idle. Postcards look like small LED panels. Mobile-first layout, large vote buttons, strong text contrast. Visuals use CSS, SVG and canvas only, with no external images. Original artwork only, with no copyrighted characters or logos.

Revision to the existing website only. Do not redeploy or modify the contract, its address, the ABI or the deployment config (imd-deployment.json). Keep all current behaviour, layout, styling and data reads unchanged.

1. RENAME. The project is now called "Squeek's First Road Trip" (replacing "Hamster Road Trip"). Update it everywhere visible: page title, loading text, header wordmark, hero and section text, help text, meta and Open Graph/Twitter titles and descriptions, the share image (share.svg), favicon labels, README and docs. Use a typographic apostrophe (’) in visible text.

2. SQUEEK, NOT "THE HAMSTER". Squeek is the name of the real hamster. Respect 429 Retry-After. - GET /squeeks/{tokenId}: level, basePower, mergeState ("ready" | "cooldown"), nextMergeHeight, custody {owner, depositor, stray, burned}, metadata {name, attributes[], imageDataUri (onchain SVG)}, economy {coreBlockHeight, currentRound, mergesOpen, stakingPaused, maximumLevel}. - GET /economy/state: identities (core, token, mining, staking proxy addresses), staking {totalNftPower, totalSqkPower, sqkPerPower, rewards}, mining, supply. - GET /accounts/{address}: tokens[] {tokenId, level, basePower, custody, nextMergeHeight, mergeState}, power, rewards, 7-day earnings[]. - GET /settlements?range=7d: summary.completedBlockCount and buckets, to estimate Squeek blocks per day. - Contracts on Sepolia (verify addresses from /economy/state identities and the docs' deployment record, not from this text): SqueekNFT ownerOf/tokenURI; SqueekMining weightForLevel(collection, level) and cooldownBlocks(collection, level) for the full level table. Explain that a staked Squeek must be withdrawn by its depositor before it can be transferred and stops earning until the buyer deposits it again. - Share of every staking reward = power / (totalNftPower + totalSqkPower), shown as "once deposited" when it sits in a wallet. - Rewards attachment: state clearly whether any unclaimed SQK travels with this Squeek in the current release (read it; in the observed release rewards accrue to the depositor's account, so "none attached"). - Merge readiness: "Ready" or "N Squeek blocks left (about X days at the 7-day pace; slower when Squeektoshi rests)". Score = power per ETH, +25% if it merges with a Squeek the buyer owns today, -10% if it must leave staking first. Show this formula under a "How we score" disclosure. - Shareable state in the URL hash (#ids=12-45-301&prices=0.02-0.01-0.008) so buyers can send a comparison to a seller. DESIGN - An appraiser's desk: warm paper background, ink text, one green accent for good signals, amber for caution, red for blockers. Fraunces for headings, IBM Plex Sans for body, IBM Plex Mono for numbers with tabular figures. Light and dark themes via prefers-color-scheme. - Loading skeletons per card; clear errors ("Squeek #123 does not exist or was burned in a merge"). - Works on phones: inputs stack, cards stack, the comparison table scrolls inside its own box. RULES - Read-only. No wallet connection, no transactions, no signatures, no private keys, no tracking, no backend. Never take token IDs or amounts from the API into a transaction. - Label every estimate as an estimate and show where each number came from (a small "source" link per value: API endpoint or contract call). - Testnet SQK and Squeeks have no monetary value; say so in the footer next to "Reads Squeekchain's public API and Sepolia contracts. Nothing is signed." - Pure static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step required. Host on IPFS/ENS and deliver the code to GitHub with a README that documents every data source and the scoring formula.

jobs.objective:
Build a small browser rhythm game called "Wheel Rhythm", a static single-page site (HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, no backend, no wallet needed). The game is played on the real-time activity of Squeekchain's hamster wheel.

GAMEPLAY
A pixel-art hamster runs on a wheel. Seeds fall down 3 lanes. The player catches them with keys A, S, D (or Left, Down, Right arrows) on desktop and by tapping the lanes on mobile. Timing windows: perfect, good, miss. Show a combo counter and a score. Save the best score in localStorage. Score and combo reset rules: a miss resets the combo to zero.

LIVE DATA (the core of the game)
Every 5 seconds fetch https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status (public, CORS enabled, JSON). Use exactly these fields:
- measurement.rpmMilli: wheel RPM x 1000 (0 when idle). Drives seed speed and density.
- measurement.coreStatus: "SPINNING" or "IDLE". Decides the mode.
- measurement.freshness: "online" means live. Treat anything else, or data older than measurement.staleAfterSeconds (120), as stale.
- builder.anchor.blockProgress: string, 0 to 1e9. Divide by 1e9 for a block progress bar.
- builder.anchor.blockHeight: string, show as a small label like "Block #5204".
Read every field defensively (values may be strings or numbers, any can be missing) and never crash. If the request fails or the data is stale, keep the last good values and show a small "offline, last data" badge.

MODES
The hamster is asleep most of the time, so IDLE must be a complete, fun game mode, not an empty screen.
- SPINNING (the hamster is running): difficulty scales with rpmMilli, clamped to a playable range. Score multiplier x2 and a short "he is running" visual effect.
- IDLE (rpmMilli is 0 or coreStatus is IDLE): the track is the hamster's real last 24 hours. Fetch https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/settlements?range=24h (buckets[], each with workAdded and settlementCount). Map the 24 hourly buckets to 24 short sections of one track. Higher workAdded in an hour means denser, faster seeds for that section. An hour with 0 work is a quiet rest section with a sleeping hamster. Show a small 24-hour strip above the lanes so the player sees which hour they are playing. The track is the same for every player that day, so scores are comparable. If the endpoint is unreachable, fall back to a built-in calm pattern and show a small "offline track" badge. Score multiplier x1.
- Label the modes clearly: "Live" (hamster running) and "Replay of the last 24 hours" (hamster asleep).
- When the status flips from IDLE to SPINNING during a run, show a clear wake-up moment and switch to the x2 live mode without restarting the run.

UI
- Header: live status pill (SPINNING or IDLE), RPM, block height, and the block progress bar.
- Game area with 3 lanes, a hit line, combo and score.
- Start screen with 3 short rules. Game over screen with score, best score and a Play again button.
- Responsive: works at 360 px width on mobile and on desktop. Touch targets at least 48 px.
- Colors: dark navy background, gold and warm orange accents, simple pixel look, readable text, good contrast.
- Sound effects optional, with a mute toggle, muted by default.

QUALITY
- Smooth 60 fps with requestAnimationFrame, no layout jank.
- No external libraries, no tracking, no wallet connection.
- Include a README that explains how the game reads the Squeekchain API and how to tune difficulty.
- All text in English. Do not use any copyrighted characters.

jobs.objective:
Wheel Odds turns a real hamster on a real wheel into a fair prediction market. Every 10 minutes Squeekchain certifies how much work the wheel did. Players bet testnet ETH on whether the next round lands over or under a line, then anyone can press Settle and the contract reads SqueekCore directly and pays winners pro rata. There is no admin, no fee and no oracle, and every stake is refunded if nobody backed the winner or SqueekCore never certifies the round.

AI on the wheel: each upcoming round gets an AI line from a decay-weighted model of recent rounds. Players bet that the hamster beats the AI or that the AI holds, and a DeepSeek analyst explains the line in plain words. An Ask AI chat answers questions about the site in English or Vietnamese.

Also built in: lines taken from the wheel's recent quartiles, a leaderboard of top earners and AI slayers rebuilt from onchain events, invite links that open a specific round and bet, claim history with transaction links, and the full contract source inside the app.

It reads the live SqueekCore reported by the Squeekchain API, because the core in the published deployment record has stopped receiving settlements. The app warns if the API ever switches to another core.

The code repository is https://github.com/ekervo/wheel-odds and the executable is https://wheel-odds.vercel.app.

jobs.objective: Launch two contracts in this repository on Robinhood Chain, in this order, without changing their logic. 1) src/ConditionalsV2.sol:ConditionalsV2, constructor (address owner = $owner, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IIntake intake = 0xa43e6f75ee006411f79ac1c84120606c2330de82, address oracleSigner = 0x5598aa9146215bc13eb26f2c692ad1461fd32982, address feeRecipient = 0x63bcf2d1483c7628d7d53704ff9c8199dc28d907). 2) src/ConditionalsZap.sol:ConditionalsZap, constructor (ConditionalsV2 conditionals = $contract:ConditionalsV2, IPoolManager poolManager = 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IERC20 usdg = 0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168). Neither constructor makes external calls. ConditionalsV2 is a conditional prediction market in IMD settled by the IdentityMD oracle. A market asks 'if CONDITION, will OUTCOME?' with four outcomes (index 2*world+side). A share of the outcome that happens pays 1 IMD. The creator deposits two 0.5 IMD oracle questions plus a neutral seed of b ln 4 that funds an LMSR maker (0.5 to 100 IMD b, Solady expWad and lnWad, log-sum-exp, rounding margins that keep makerBalance >= C(q) >= every q[i]); the seed is the creator's maximum loss. Until closeTime: stakeConditional (and stakeFor, paid by the caller and credited to an account) mints a complete set, sells the opposite side to the maker and buys more of the chosen side, so the stake is paid in its world on its side and refunded in the other world; buy, sell and exit trade with the maker with slippage bounds. Every maker trade pays 2%: half accrues to the creator in owed, 67/200 is sent to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD because IMD reverts on transfers to zero, and the rest accrues to feeRecipient in owed. When the maker is short of every outcome it turns those complete sets back into IMD (_absorb). The oracle flow is unchanged from Conditionals v1, IMD launch 2278, audited: after resolveTime anyone calls requestResolution, the contract pays the Intake with requestWithFailure for oracle.request@oracle-1 questions (panel 5, quorum 4, bool, panel evidence, window pinned to one Ethereum block, block.number - 10, since block.number on Robinhood Chain is the Ethereum block number) and stores keccak256 of each canonical question document. onOracleResult (selector 0x510379c7) accepts an answer only from the Intake for its own pending request, with the stored questionHash, answerType bool, panelSize and quorum at least the market's, agreed >= quorum, not expired, and an EIP-712 signature (domain IdentityMD Oracle, version 2) from the market's oracle signer. onFailure (0x5a0df71e) only clears the ask. Settlement pays 1 IMD per share of the outcome that happened and gives the creator the maker's residual and unspent budget. With no usable answer 30 days after resolveTime anyone can void. Each account is refunded what it paid, excluding fees, for the shares it still holds; gains and losses it already realised are not refunded. If the market holds less than that total (a short void), each account is paid between its position's value at the final prices and its cost, never above its cost, and the creator is paid last. Those capped refunds can add up to less than the pool, so sweepVoid pays the creator what is left from 365 days after the void, and refunds still unclaimed at the sweep lapse; a void that was not short leaves nothing over and its refunds never lapse. The owner can only propose an oracle configuration for future markets behind a 3 day delay and set the fee recipient; it cannot touch trades, answers or open markets. No token, no proxy, no pause. ConditionalsZap has no owner and holds nothing between calls. stakeWithEth and stakeWithUsdg swap exact input through two hookless Uniswap v4 pools (USDG to ETH, fee 500, spacing 10; ETH to IMD, fee 10000, spacing 100) inside one PoolManager unlock, revert on a partial fill or below the caller's minImd, and call stakeFor for the caller. All positions, exits and payouts are in IMD in ConditionalsV2. ConditionalsV2's runtime is 24,269 bytes with optimizer_runs 1, so any fix must keep it under 24,576. This code already went through IMD launch 2765, which parked on one last finding that sweepVoid now settles; ADAPTATION.md records every finding and fix from that audit, including the buy() cast overflow, void dilution by cooperating accounts and refunds above cost. Deliberate design, documented there: each ask is paid from the budget while it lasts and the caller pays only the shortfall; createMarket binds only the price, and an oracle rotation is protected by its 3 day delay and event; sell and exit will not push an outcome more than 20b below the top, so exit can leave shares worth under about 2e-9 IMD each; the conditionals view, the pendingOracleConfig getter and several constants are not public, to fit the size limit. legacy/ holds the deployed v1 for reference and is not built. The test suite (unit, fuzz, invariant, oracle conformance vector and a live-API question-hash vector; fork tests with ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL) must keep passing.

Settlement pays 1 IMD per share of the outcome that happened and gives the creator the maker's residual and unspent budget. With no usable answer 30 days after resolveTime anyone can void. Each account is refunded what it paid, excluding fees, for the shares it still holds; gains and losses it already realised are not refunded. If the market holds less than that total (a short void), each account is paid between its position's value at the final prices and its cost, never above its cost, and the creator is paid last. Those capped refunds can add up to less than the pool, so sweepVoid pays the creator what is left from 365 days after the void, and refunds still unclaimed at the sweep lapse; a void that was not short leaves nothing over and its refunds never lapse. The owner can only propose an oracle configuration for future markets behind a 3 day delay and set the fee recipient; it cannot touch trades, answers or open markets. No token, no proxy, no pause. ConditionalsZap has no owner and holds nothing between calls. stakeWithEth and stakeWithUsdg swap exact input through two hookless Uniswap v4 pools (USDG to ETH, fee 500, spacing 10; ETH to IMD, fee 10000, spacing 100) inside one PoolManager unlock, revert on a partial fill or below the caller's minImd, and call stakeFor for the caller. All positions, exits and payouts are in IMD in ConditionalsV2. ConditionalsV2's runtime is 24,269 bytes with optimizer_runs 1, so any fix must keep it under 24,576. This code already went through IMD launch 2765, which parked on one last finding that sweepVoid now settles; ADAPTATION.md records every finding and fix from that audit, including the buy() cast overflow, void dilution by cooperating accounts and refunds above cost. Deliberate design, documented there: each ask is paid from the budget while it lasts and the caller pays only the shortfall; createMarket binds only the price, and an oracle rotation is protected by its 3 day delay and event; sell and exit will not push an outcome more than 20b below the top, so exit can leave shares worth under about 2e-9 IMD each; the conditionals view, the pendingOracleConfig getter and several constants are not public, to fit the size limit. legacy/ holds the deployed v1 for reference and is not built. The test suite (unit, fuzz, invariant, oracle conformance vector and a live-API question-hash vector; fork tests with ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL) must keep passing.

jobs.objective:
Build "Fantasy Hamster", a daily fantasy game for Squeekchain, a proof-of-work chain where a real hamster (Squeektoshi) on a real wheel produces the chain's work. Each day players draft what they think the hamster will do tomorrow, and the real wheel data scores them. Think Wordle meets fantasy football. Single-page static site. No wallet, token, payments, backend or signup. All copy in English.

GAME LOOP
- A game day is one UTC calendar day. Players draft today for tomorrow. Drafts close at 00:00 UTC, so nobody drafts knowing the result.
- Each game day offers 12 event cards, chosen from the catalog by a seeded PRNG keyed on the UTC date, so every player sees the same 12.
- Pick exactly 5 cards and name one Captain (double points).
- Card points are priced from the last 7 complete UTC days: points = clamp(round(10 / max(hitRate, 0.1)), 10, 100). Rarer events pay more. Show the hit rate on the card.
- Live view: during the game day, cards light up the moment they are decided, and cards that can no longer hit are marked dead.
- Result reveal: flip cards one by one as hit or miss, then total, personal best and streak.

EVENT CATALOG
Watches are the 6-hour UTC buckets: Dawn 00-06, Morning 06-12, Afternoon 12-18, Night 18-24. A watch is active if activeRoundCount > 0. Each event is a pure function of the day's four buckets, plus the prior days where stated.
Warm-Up: work >= 5000. Five Figures: work >= 10000. Big Legs: work >= 14000. The 20K Legend: work >= 20000. Clocked In: active rounds >= 12. Overtime: active rounds >= 30. Block Party: completed blocks >= 1000. Block Bonanza: blocks >= 1300. Dawn Patrol, Breakfast Run, Afternoon Jog, Night Shift: that watch is active. Back to Back: two consecutive active watches. Triple Shift: 3 or more active watches. Around the Clock: all 4 active. One Big Run: exactly 1 active watch. Monster Session: one watch with work >= 7000. Even Split: 2 or more active watches and no watch above 50% of the day's work. Slow Burn: work from 1 to 6000. Beauty Sleep: 3 or more consecutive inactive watches. Day Off: zero work. Beat Yesterday: work above the prior day. Personal Record: work above each of the prior 6 days.

DATA
Both endpoints are public with open CORS. All numbers arrive as strings.
GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/settlements?range=7d returns buckets[] with startAt, endAt, activeRoundCount, workAdded, completedBlockCount and window.bucketSeconds (21600). Buckets align to 00, 06, 12, 18 UTC.
CRITICAL: the window extends into the future. A bucket whose endAt is later than now is in progress or not started and reports zeros. Never treat it as a real zero. An event is decided only when the buckets it needs are complete or it has already hit.
GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status returns measurement.freshness, coreStatus (IDLE, ACTIVE, COUNTER_FAULT), rpmMilli, cumulativeWorkUnits, observedAt, staleAfterSeconds, and builder.anchor.blockHeight.
Poll status every 20s and settlements every 5 minutes. Pause while the tab is hidden. Honour Retry-After on 429. Save each scored day in localStorage with try/catch, because the API only covers 7 days. If a day is gone from the API and was never saved, show "result expired". Never invent or simulate data. If the API fails, show an honest "signal lost" state with the last-known time.

HAMSTER
A pixel hamster in SVG or CSS is the page's heart, with three states: running on its wheel at a speed scaled to rpmMilli (ACTIVE), asleep (IDLE), confused (COUNTER_FAULT or stale). The hamster sleeps most of the day, so the sleeping state must be charming, and the page must feel alive and useful while it sleeps: tomorrow's draft, countdown to lock, yesterday's result.

SOCIAL, NO BACKEND
- Share result: copyable Wordle-style text with day number, score and a hit/miss row, plus an X intent link.
- Rival link: URL hash encodes day, picks, captain and a display name of up to 16 chars. Opening it shows a head-to-head of both rosters scored from public data, and offers "Add rival". Rivals for a day are stored locally and ranked.

STREAM OVERLAY
?overlay=1 renders a transparent-background lower third for OBS browser sources at 1920x1080: the viewer's 5 cards, live hit state and the hamster. No controls.

DESIGN
Warm, playful, collectible trading cards: cream paper, dark ink, one bold accent, thick outlines, chunky type. Each event card gets its own small illustration in SVG. Card flips must feel satisfying. No dark neon gradients, no emoji as UI icons, no external fonts, CDNs or trackers. Mobile first from 360px. Keyboard accessible. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

BUILD
Static export that works from any base path, including IPFS gateway subpaths and ENS: relative asset URLs and hash routing only. Keep game logic in pure modules with unit tests covering PRNG determinism, pricing, every event, UTC day boundaries and in-progress buckets. Include a README and a 3-line "How to play". Footer: "Fan-made game for Squeekchain. No real money. Data from api.squeekchain.com".
