jobs.objective:
Fix the Hamster Hour leaderboard counting. Right now a binary bet counts as "played" unless a MarketVoided event exists, but MarketVoided is emitted lazily (only on first claim/finalize), so refunded bets show as counted. Example: 0xa1c1…217a has 7.37 IMD on SNOOZE in window 429, which is one-sided, and claimable() returns the full 7.37 as a refund, yet it is ranked #1.

New rule, computed from BinaryBet events, not from MarketVoided:
- A binary bet in (window k, market m) counts only if (1) window k has a Settled event and no TimedOut event, and (2) market m in window k has stake on BOTH sides (sum side=true > 0 and sum side=false > 0).
- Everything else is either "pending" (window not settled and not timed out yet) or "refunded" (one-sided or timed out). Refunded bets are excluded entirely, not shown as pending.
- EXACT tickets: count only when the window is Settled (keep the current behavior).
- Team wallet 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 stays unranked.

Expected result with the current chain data: 0xc657…0808 (5 IMD, window 440), 0x2300…72f1 (5 IMD EXACT, window 429), 0xdc8a…6c26 (4 IMD, window 440). 0xa1c1 should drop out. Pending section shows only bets in unsettled windows whose market is already two-sided, or label one-sided ones as "will refund unless someone takes the other side".

Do not touch contracts or keeper. Do not push to git; show me the diff.

versions.objective:
Hamster Hour: a pari-mutuel betting game on a real hamster. Squeekchain (https://sepolia.squeekchain.com) runs a physical hamster wheel and settles a round every 10 minutes with the number of wheel passes. Hamster Hour lets people bet IMD on how far the hamster runs over the next 6 rounds (one hour). Results come only from the IMD oracle.

CONTRACTS (Ethereum mainnet, no owner, no upgradeability, no admin withdraw). TEAM = the wallet that requested this launch, immutable.

1. HamsterHour
- Windows are defined by Squeekchain round numbers: window k covers rounds 6k to 6k+5. Round duration 600 s from genesisTimestamp 1791847800; the contract derives the current round from block.timestamp. Betting on window k is open until round 6k starts.
- Bets in IMD (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7) via transferFrom, minimum 0.5 IMD.
- Three pari-mutuel markets per window, each its own pool:
  a) OVER/UNDER: total passes above or below the line. Line = average total passes over the last 7 settled windows, fixed at window creation; bootstrap line 1000 until 7 windows exist.
  b) EXACT: bettor submits a uint256 guess of total passes. Closest wins 60% of the pool, second 30%, third 10%; ties split equally. The EXACT winner also receives the full jackpot balance (see below).
  c) SLEEP: yes/no, total passes == 0.
- Settlement: after round 6k+5 ends, anyone may call settle(k) with a signed IMD oracle attestation for the question template "What is the total number of wheel passes recorded by Squeekchain for rounds {6k} through {6k+5} inclusive, as published at {sourceUrl}? Answer as a single uint256." The contract verifies it through OracleVerifier and stores the result. Lazy: windows with no bets are never settled.
- Split of every window's total bets: 91% to winners pro rata, 5% to stakers, 3% to an oracle reserve that reimburses 0.5 IMD to whoever supplied the settlement attestation, 1% to TEAM.
- Staking: once setStakingToken is set, anyone can stake and unstake that token here. The 5% share is distributed pro rata by stake-weight at each settlement (accumulator pattern, pull-based claimStaking). Before the token is set, the 5% accrues in a reserve that is released to stakers evenly over the 30 windows after the token is set.
- Jackpot: the contract accepts any ERC-20 sent to it; the balance of the token set once via setJackpotToken is paid in full to the EXACT winner of each settled window. Empty jackpot pays nothing.
- Edge cases: a market with bets on only one side is void and refunded; a window with no valid attestation within 48 hours after it ends is void and refunded; all claims pull-based via claim(k).
- Configuration: setStakingToken and setJackpotToken are one-shot; sourceUrl and genesisTimestamp are updatable. All four callable only by TEAM, each with a 48-hour timelock and a public event. Nothing else is adjustable. No other TEAM powers.
- Events for every bet, settlement, claim, void, stake, unstake, config change.

2. OracleVerifier
- Verifies IMD oracle attestations exactly as the IMD attester scheme requires: attester signature, question hash, validity window, uint256 answer. Rejects expired, mismatched or replayed attestations.

TESTS: pari-mutuel math for all three markets, EXACT ties, one-sided void, no-attestation void, split sums to 100%, oracle reimbursement, staking accumulator, pre-token reserve release over 30 windows, jackpot payout, attestation replay rejected, line over 7 windows, round-to-window math around genesis, timelocks.

WEBSITE: dark console style like sepolia.squeekchain.com, monospace. Top: the live Squeekchain stream embedded full width (YouTube id from https://media.squeekchain.com/live/current.json), countdown to the current window close, the line, live pool sizes and implied payouts per side, jackpot balance. Tabs: Bet (three markets, connect wallet, approve IMD, place bet, claim), Stake ("staking opens with the token" until set, then stake, unstake, claim), History (settled windows with links to the oracle attestation on explorer.imd.fun). Mobile first. No fake data.

README first section: no owner, no house, pari-mutuel only, results only from the IMD oracle, the contract never owes more than it holds, TEAM gets 1% of bets and nothing else.

Project: Hamster Hour, https://ipfs.imd.fun/ipfs/bafybeidp4zcka5l7nf3gnj4fcmooxhp3vc3wucml6st4bckcjwa3ain3f4/ (launch 1959; contracts HamsterHour 0xc5217f129da200a8e86229de4eabf3686eef64b1 and OracleVerifier 0xdcd7a7dee31d589f9df8113780050c18e7ea1f7d on Ethereum, repo identity-md-launches/launch-1951-workflow-contract-stage-context). Keep every existing on-chain feature. Rebuild the look and the player flow as described. Six changes.

1. LIVE WHEEL CAM. media.squeekchain.com/live/current.json blocks cross-origin reads, so the cam never shows. Embed the YouTube player directly: https://www.youtube.com/embed/6K_uF2s-LSw?autoplay=1&mute=1, full width at the top, 16:9, lazy. Try current.json in the background and swap the embed only if it answers with a different publicId. Never show "unavailable" while the hardcoded id works. Keep the "Open source" link.

2. ONE-CLICK SETTLE. In the settle panel add a "Buy oracle answer" step before the paste field. For window k: build the oracle.request body exactly as docs/ORACLE.md in the contract repo specifies: question = question(k) read from the contract, chainId 1, window {hours: 24}, answerType "uint256", evidence "panel", panelSize 20, quorum 14, validForSeconds 86400, consumer {chainId: 1, verifyingContract: HamsterHour}. Pay the 0.5 IMD through the protocol's standard paid route for a browser wallet (the IMD Intake contract on Ethereum, approve + request, or the route the IMD protocol docs name), then poll GET https://api.imd.fun/oracle/requests/<uuid>/attestation every 15 s, show the panel link on explorer.imd.fun, and when the attestation arrives, prefill it and enable "Settle". Keep the manual paste path as a fallback. Only allow buying when the window has ended and has bets. Show the 0.5 IMD reimbursement note.

3. TEAM CONTROLS. Keep the four settings, current values, pending values and execute dates visible to everyone. Show inputs and the Schedule/Execute buttons only when the connected wallet equals the contract's TEAM address; otherwise read-only.

4. MAKE IT RADICALLY SIMPLE.
- First screen on mobile: the live cam, the countdown, the line, and three big buttons: OVER, UNDER, SLEEPING. One tap opens an amount sheet with 1 / 5 / 10 / 25 IMD chips and a Place bet button. Approve and bet are one flow with clear states: Approving… → Placing… → Bet placed, you win X if OVER.
- Under each button show live "pays x1.8" from pool sizes, updating as bets arrive.
- EXACT lives behind a "Guess the exact number" link, not as a primary market.
- One line under the buttons: "Bet IMD on how far the hamster runs in the next hour. Winners share the pool. Verified by the IMD oracle." and a second dim line: "Lose a bet, mine $HAMSTER. Coming soon."
- Plain words everywhere. No "pari-mutuel", "attestation", "void", "settle" in player-facing copy: use "shared pool", "verified result", "refunded", "close the window". Precise terms only in a "How it works" drawer and in the settle and TEAM panels.
- After a window ends: a result card with passes, who won, your payout, and one Claim button. Claimable windows surface automatically on the Bet tab, no window-number lookup needed.
- A "My bets" strip on the Bet tab with the wallet's open positions in the current and next window.
- Stake, History, Settle and TEAM controls move under a "More" menu. The Bet tab is the whole app for most visitors.
- Wallet connect in one tap; show IMD balance and a "Get IMD" link to the IMD/ETH pool when balance is below 0.5.
- Header: a small "X" link to https://x.com/hamsterhourgame next to the wallet button. Footer: the same link plus the two contract links.
- Empty and error states in plain language: "No bets yet, be first", "Betting closed, next window opens in 12:03".

5. INTRO OVERLAY. On first visit show a full-screen overlay: a looping muted video of a hamster chewing, download https://static.klipy.com/ii/d6b0ce929193df3c242ac34b5654d2ce/af/08/uurjWLxi1HRjI5kfVD.mp4 into the site assets (do not hotlink; if the download fails, use a looping pixel-art animation of the mascot chewing instead). Make it feel like a meme, not a corporate splash: the video big and centered with a neon green frame, the title HAMSTER HOUR in large monospace above it, one line "bet. lose. win $HAMSTER." and two buttons: "Start playing" (closes the overlay) and "Follow on X" (opens https://x.com/hamsterhourgame in a new tab). Remember dismissal in localStorage, show it once per device, Escape and tap outside also close it.

6. VISUAL STYLE. Build the whole look from this description, no external image files will be supplied. Terminal aesthetic: background #0b0d0b with a faint grid of #163a1c lines at 25 px pitch across the entire page. Accent neon green #39ff6a with a soft outer glow for rings, countdown digits, pool numbers and button borders. Headings in off-white #f2f0e6, secondary text in dim green #5a8f63. One monospace font everywhere (IBM Plex Mono or JetBrains Mono); the title HAMSTER HOUR bold, wide, uppercase. Buttons: dark fill, 1 px neon border, glow on hover, square pixel-crisp corners. Draw the mascot yourself as pixel-art SVG: a chubby orange-and-cream hamster with round green-lensed goggles, front view, big cheeks, inside a glowing neon green ring; use it as the header logo, favicon, og:image, loading state and result card (happy when you win, asleep for a zero round). Draw a second pixel-art SVG of the same hamster running in a side-view wheel with motion lines for the hero on desktop. No gradients except the neon glow, no stock icons, no emoji, no photos.

Keep everything live and real. No fake numbers, no placeholders, zero console errors, mobile first at 375 and desktop at 1440, no horizontal scroll.

ACCEPTANCE: fresh visit at 375 and 1440 shows the intro overlay with the video, then the YouTube player within 3 s of dismissing it; OVER tap → amount → one bet transaction; the settle flow produces a valid settle transaction for a finished window with bets; TEAM buttons are absent for a non-TEAM wallet.

Project: Hamster Hour, https://hamster-hour-bet-on-the-wheel.sites.imd.fun (launch 1959 v2; contracts HamsterHour 0xc5217f129da200a8e86229de4eabf3686eef64b1 and OracleVerifier 0xdcd7a7dee31d589f9df8113780050c18e7ea1f7d on Ethereum). jobs.objective: Audit the IMD Bell contracts in src/. MarketHoursHook is a Uniswap v4 hook that lets its coin trade only during a daily session: while the market is closed, limit orders wait in two books and each book is filled at one clearing price when a bell rings (opening 12:00 UTC, closing 16:00 UTC). It creates BellGame (sealed commit-reveal guesses at the next opening price, points only, no tokens), BellRinger (rings the due bell, runs that bell's chores and pays the caller a capped reward priced from block.basefee) and SwarmBudget (pays two fixed nightly Intake requests); MarketHoursCoin is a fixed-supply ERC-20. jobs.objective:
You are a crypto perpetual futures trader. Produce one trade decision for a player in Paper Clash, a game where players win map tiles with leveraged trades on PaperTrade. The player has chosen to let you make every trading decision. The goal: take the tile O6 (Forest). That needs the trade to close with a net return on margin above +3.1%. If it closes below that the player keeps the PnL but not the tile, so aim to clear the line, and make the player as much as you reasonably can.

## Fixed constraints
- Market: "BTC" or "ETH" perpetual (BTC, ETH). Pick the one with the better setup right now.
- Direction: exactly one of "long" or "short".
- Margin: $200 (the player chose it; you don't).
- Leverage: an integer from 5 to 1000 inclusive (the tile's minimum, and PaperTrade's $1,000-$10M position size).
- Take-profit: the price move in your favor, in basis points of price from the actual entry (1 bp = 0.01%), not return on margin. It must clear the line:
         5x → bust 1995 bp; BTC take-profit ≥ 75 bp; ETH take-profit ≥ 75.8 bp
       503x → bust 14.9 bp; BTC take-profit ≥ 3.8 bp; ETH take-profit ≥ 4.1 bp
      1000x → bust 5 bp; BTC take-profit ≥ 2.9 bp; ETH take-profit ≥ 3.3 bp
- Stop-loss: a price move against the position in bp, smaller than the bust distance, or null to hold to liquidation (liquidation is then the stop).
- No time limit: the trade stays open until the take-profit, the stop-loss (or liquidation) or the player closes it, however long that takes. There is no funding, so holding costs nothing.
- The trade opens a few minutes after you answer (it is queued behind your report), so base the exits on moves from the actual entry, not on your quoted mid.

## Papertrade execution
Entry and exit fill at the Hyperliquid BBO mid ((best bid + best ask) / 2). There is no funding or fee on notional. Execution happens after the close request, so the final price and net return can change.
Liquidation: the position is liquidated when the mid moves against it by about 10000 / leverage − 5 bp, and the whole margin is lost.
Winning closes are haircut; losses are not. Use this payout calculation, not raw price move × leverage:
1. Let b be the favorable price move in bp, u = (b − 0.3) / 9.7. The active curve is off-hours. For 0 < u < 1, holdback in bp = 6.085 × 9.7 × u^2 × (1 − u)^3; otherwise holdback = 0.
2. Deduct the 0.2 bp deadband and holdback: m = max(0, b − 0.2 − holdback) / 10000. If m = 0, net return is 0.
3. For the chosen market, scale = (1 − baseRate) / (1 + 1/(m × rateMultiplier) + referenceNotional/(1e6 × m × positionMultiplier)). Market parameters: {"BTC":{"baseRate":0.1,"rateMultiplier":15000,"positionMultiplier":814.598,"referenceNotional":100000},"ETH":{"baseRate":0.1,"rateMultiplier":15000,"positionMultiplier":483.979,"referenceNotional":100000}}.
4. Net return on margin (%) = m × leverage × 100 × scale × (1 − 0.02 − 0.005). The win fee is 2% and builder fee is 0.5%, both on the scaled gain.
Reference net returns at 100x (scale proportionally for other leverage):
  1 bp → BTC +0.110%, ETH +0.082%
  3 bp → BTC +0.345%, ETH +0.269%
  5 bp → BTC +1.541%, ETH +1.312%
  10 bp → BTC +7.207%, ETH +6.724%
  20 bp → BTC +15.857%, ETH +15.267%
  50 bp → BTC +42.098%, ETH +41.426%
The minimum take-profits above include these deductions and target 0.1 percentage points above the tile's gain before rounding the move up. Aim beyond the minimum to allow for execution price changes. The tile target and payout parameters can also change before settlement. Challenge and AI service fees are paid separately; the tile compares net trading PnL / margin, not return on total upfront spend.

## How to decide
The decision is yours. Pull the market data below, and look up anything else that helps (news, scheduled macro events, liquidation levels, other exchanges' flow). Be decisive: always return a trade. Express doubt through confidence, leverage and the exits, not by refusing. Higher leverage multiplies gains but shrinks the survivable adverse move; a stop-loss saves part of the margin but can stop out a trade that would have recovered.

## Market data (Hyperliquid public API, no auth)
POST https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info with Content-Type: application/json. Times are Unix ms. For each of BTC and ETH:
1. Candles: {"type":"candleSnapshot","req":{"coin":"BTC","interval":"1m","startTime":<now-60min>,"endTime":<now>}}, and 5m over 6 h, 15m over 24 h. Fields: t, T, o/h/l/c (strings), v, n. Oldest first.
2. Context: {"type":"metaAndAssetCtxs"} → [meta, ctxs]; ctxs[index of the coin in meta.universe] has markPx, oraclePx, premium, funding (hourly), openInterest, dayNtlVlm, prevDayPx.
3. Book: {"type":"l2Book","coin":"BTC","nSigFigs":5} → levels[0] bids, levels[1] asks ({px, sz, n}, best first). mid = (best bid + best ask) / 2.
Also useful: {"type":"recentTrades","coin":"BTC"}, {"type":"fundingHistory","coin":"BTC","startTime":<ms>}.

Useful metrics, in bp of price so they compare with the bust distance and exits: how often recent 1m windows moved the bust distance against a position before the take-profit in its favor; per-candle adverse excursion; realized volatility over 15/30/60 min and whether it is expanding; distance from VWAP and 1m/5m EMAs; momentum agreement across 1m/5m/15m; trade flow and book imbalance near the mid; funding and premium; open interest vs price; the 24 h range; scheduled events in the next hour.

## Output
Return ONLY one JSON object, no fences or commentary. Write it to artifacts/report.md (output "report"), not just the final reply. Exactly these keys:
{
  "market": "BTC" | "ETH",
  "direction": "long" | "short",
  "leverage": <integer 5-1000>,
  "take_profit_bp": <number, favorable price move in bp from entry>,
  "stop_loss_bp": <number smaller than bust_distance_bp, or null to hold to liquidation>,
  "bust_distance_bp": <number, 10000/leverage - 5>,
  "expected_net_return_on_margin_pct": <number, if the take-profit hits>,
  "confidence": <number 0.0-1.0>,
  "regime": "trending_up" | "trending_down" | "ranging" | "volatile_choppy",
  "entry_mid": <number, the live mid you based the trade on>,
  "data_time_utc": "<ISO 8601 time you fetched the data>",
  "reasoning": "<2-4 plain sentences: the evidence for the market and direction, and why this leverage and these exits fit the volatility and the line to beat>",
  "risks": "<1-2 sentences: what would most likely stop it out or liquidate it>"
}
Use JSON numbers (and null for no stop-loss).

jobs.objective:
Build HAMLOCK, the hamster-powered time lock for Squeekchain (the hamster-powered proof-of-work toychain on Ethereum Sepolia, chainId 11155111). A user locks Sepolia ETH and it only opens after Squeektoshi the hamster has run the distance the user picked, measured on Squeekchain's own SqueekCore contract. Breaking the jar early costs 20%, which goes to everyone still holding. Ask for an independent security review of the contract before deployment. Code and contracts only in this job; the website comes in a later job.

SQUEEKCORE (read only, never written): Sepolia proxy 0x980b4424c007caf7a1f3670b48c8eaef7ebc3d44 (the core the official API https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/core reports as identities.core). Interface: function state() view returns (CoreState) with struct CoreState { uint64 settledThroughRound; uint64 cumulativeWork; uint96 cumulativeBlockUnits; uint64 blockHeight; uint96 blockProgress; uint32 workPerThousandBlocks; uint256 authorizationNonce; bool paused; }. cumulativeWork only goes up; 1 work unit = 1 wheel turn = about 0.878 m.

CONTRACT Hamlock (Solidity 0.8.28, one file, no owner, no admin, no pause, no upgrade, no external libraries needed). Constructor takes the SqueekCore address, stored immutable as core. Constants: WORK_PER_KM = 1139; MIN_KM = 1; MAX_KM = 100 (uint16); MIN_DEPOSIT = 0.001 ether; MAX_DEPOSIT = 1 ether; MAX_DURATION = 30 days; PENALTY_BPS = 2000; BURN = 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD.
Storage: struct Jar { uint128 amount; uint64 startWork; uint64 targetWork; uint64 deadline; uint16 km; uint256 rewardDebt; }; mapping(address => Jar) public jars (one active jar per wallet); mapping(address => uint256) public kmCompleted, jarsCompleted, jarsBroken; uint256 public accRewardPerWei (scaled by 1e24), totalLocked, activeJars, totalPenalties, totalBurned.
Reading the core: an internal try/catch wrapper returns (ok, cumulativeWork) and never reverts.
lock(uint16 km) payable: revert AlreadyHasJar if caller has a jar; BadDistance if km outside 1..100; BadDeposit if value outside 0.001..1 ether; CoreUnavailable if the core cannot be read. startWork = current cumulativeWork; targetWork = startWork + km * 1139; deadline = block.timestamp + 30 days; rewardDebt = ceil(amount * accRewardPerWei / 1e24) (round UP). totalLocked += amount; activeJars += 1. emit Locked(owner indexed, amount, km, startWork, targetWork, deadline).
pendingReward(owner) view: accrued = amount * accRewardPerWei / 1e24 (round down); return accrued > rewardDebt ? accrued - rewardDebt : 0. Rounding must never let the contract owe more than it holds.
isOpenable(owner) view: true if the jar exists and (block.timestamp >= deadline, or the core reads ok and cumulativeWork >= targetWork).
workRemaining(owner) view: 0 if no jar or reached; full distance if the core is unreadable. currentWork() view.
open(): revert NoJar; before the deadline revert StillLocked unless the core reads ok and cumulativeWork >= targetWork. hamsterRanIt = core reads ok and cumulativeWork >= targetWork (also checked after the deadline). Pay amount + pendingReward, delete the jar, totalLocked -= amount, activeJars -= 1; if hamsterRanIt then kmCompleted += km and jarsCompleted += 1. emit Opened(owner indexed, amount, reward, hamsterRanIt, km). After the deadline the jar always opens, even if the core is gone.
breakJar(): revert NoJar; revert AlreadyOpenable if isOpenable. forfeited = pendingReward; penalty = amount * 2000 / 10000; refund = amount - penalty. Delete the jar, update totals, jarsBroken += 1, toShare = penalty + forfeited, totalPenalties += toShare. If totalLocked is now 0, send toShare to BURN and add it to totalBurned; otherwise accRewardPerWei += toShare * 1e24 / totalLocked. emit Broken(owner indexed, refund, penalty, forfeited, burned). Send refund.
All ETH sends via call, revert TransferFailed on failure; a nonReentrant guard on lock/open/breakJar; checks-effects-interactions.

TESTS (Foundry, with a mock core): limits; one jar per wallet; stays locked until target, opens exactly at target; 30-day valve opens without score, also when the core reverts; breaking pays 80% and splits the penalty pro rata (0.3/0.1 holders get 0.075/0.025 when a 0.5 jar breaks); late joiners get nothing from earlier penalties; a breaker's earned reward goes to the others; burn when nobody holds; cannot break an openable jar; reentrancy; fuzz invariant that the balance always covers every deposit plus every pending reward.

DEPLOY: Sepolia only, no token, no owner. Constructor argument: 0x980b4424c007caf7a1f3670b48c8eaef7ebc3d44.

Build HAMLOCK, the hamster-powered time lock for Squeekchain (the hamster-powered proof-of-work toychain on Ethereum Sepolia, chainId 11155111). A user locks Sepolia ETH and it only opens after Squeektoshi the hamster has run the distance the user picked, measured on Squeekchain's own SqueekCore contract. Breaking the jar early costs 20%, which goes to everyone still holding. Ask for an independent security review of the contract before deployment. Code and contracts only in this job; the website comes in a later job.

SQUEEKCORE (read only, never written): Sepolia proxy 0x980b4424c007caf7a1f3670b48c8eaef7ebc3d44 (the core the official API https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/core reports as identities.core). Interface: function state() view returns (CoreState) with struct CoreState { uint64 settledThroughRound; uint64 cumulativeWork; uint96 cumulativeBlockUnits; uint64 blockHeight; uint96 blockProgress; uint32 workPerThousandBlocks; uint256 authorizationNonce; bool paused; }. cumulativeWork only goes up; 1 work unit = 1 wheel turn = about 0.878 m.

CONTRACT Hamlock (Solidity 0.8.28, one file, no owner, no admin, no pause, no upgrade, no external libraries needed). Constructor takes the SqueekCore address, stored immutable as core. Constants: WORK_PER_KM = 1139; MIN_KM = 1; MAX_KM = 100 (uint16); MIN_DEPOSIT = 0.001 ether; MAX_DEPOSIT = 1 ether; MAX_DURATION = 30 days; PENALTY_BPS = 2000; BURN = 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD.
Storage: struct Jar { uint128 amount; uint64 startWork; uint64 targetWork; uint64 deadline; uint16 km; uint256 rewardDebt; }; mapping(address => Jar) public jars (one active jar per wallet); mapping(address => uint256) public kmCompleted, jarsCompleted, jarsBroken; uint256 public accRewardPerWei (scaled by 1e24), totalLocked, activeJars, totalPenalties, totalBurned.
Reading the core: an internal try/catch wrapper returns (ok, cumulativeWork) and never reverts.
lock(uint16 km) payable: revert AlreadyHasJar if caller has a jar; BadDistance if km outside 1..100; BadDeposit if value outside 0.001..1 ether; CoreUnavailable if the core cannot be read. startWork = current cumulativeWork; targetWork = startWork + km * 1139; deadline = block.timestamp + 30 days; rewardDebt = ceil(amount * accRewardPerWei / 1e24) (round UP). totalLocked += amount; activeJars += 1. emit Locked(owner indexed, amount, km, startWork, targetWork, deadline).
pendingReward(owner) view: accrued = amount * accRewardPerWei / 1e24 (round down); return accrued > rewardDebt ? accrued - rewardDebt : 0. Rounding must never let the contract owe more than it holds.
isOpenable(owner) view: true if the jar exists and (block.timestamp >= deadline, or the core reads ok and cumulativeWork >= targetWork).
workRemaining(owner) view: 0 if no jar or reached; full distance if the core is unreadable. currentWork() view.
open(): revert NoJar; before the deadline revert StillLocked unless the core reads ok and cumulativeWork >= targetWork. hamsterRanIt = core reads ok and cumulativeWork >= targetWork (also checked after the deadline). Pay amount + pendingReward, delete the jar, totalLocked -= amount, activeJars -= 1; if hamsterRanIt then kmCompleted += km and jarsCompleted += 1. emit Opened(owner indexed, amount, reward, hamsterRanIt, km). After the deadline the jar always opens, even if the core is gone.
breakJar(): revert NoJar; revert AlreadyOpenable if isOpenable. forfeited = pendingReward; penalty = amount * 2000 / 10000; refund = amount - penalty. Delete the jar, update totals, jarsBroken += 1, toShare = penalty + forfeited, totalPenalties += toShare. If totalLocked is now 0, send toShare to BURN and add it to totalBurned; otherwise accRewardPerWei += toShare * 1e24 / totalLocked. emit Broken(owner indexed, refund, penalty, forfeited, burned). Send refund.
All ETH sends via call, revert TransferFailed on failure; a nonReentrant guard on lock/open/breakJar; checks-effects-interactions.

TESTS (Foundry, with a mock core): limits; one jar per wallet; stays locked until target, opens exactly at target; 30-day valve opens without score, also when the core reverts; breaking pays 80% and splits the penalty pro rata (0.3/0.1 holders get 0.075/0.025 when a 0.5 jar breaks); late joiners get nothing from earlier penalties; a breaker's earned reward goes to the others; burn when nobody holds; cannot break an openable jar; reentrancy; fuzz invariant that the balance always covers every deposit plus every pending reward.

DEPLOY: Sepolia only, no token, no owner. Constructor argument: 0x980b4424c007caf7a1f3670b48c8eaef7ebc3d44.

Two changes to the HAMLOCK site. Do not touch the contract or its address.

1) WATCH THE HAMSTER LIVE, ON OUR PAGE
Replace the "Watch the livestream" link (which only opens x.com) with an in-page player inside the hamster card.
- Read the live descriptor from LIVE_URL = https://hamlock-live.jubilee-registry.workers.dev/current (and the schedule from https://hamlock-live.jubilee-registry.workers.dev/schedule). Keep both URLs as one constant at the top of the code so they are easy to change. Poll every 30 seconds while the page is visible.
- Descriptor shape: {"schemaVersion":2,"state":"idle"|"starting"|"ending"|"live"|"error","playback":{...},"validUntil":ISO|null}. It is live only when state is "live" AND validUntil is in the future.
- When live, the hamster card shows a red LIVE badge and a "WATCH LIVE" button. Clicking it swaps the pixel hamster art for a 16:9 iframe:
  - playback.kind "x": https://studio.x.com/embed/broadcast/{broadcastId}?dnt=true  (broadcastId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9]{13,16}$)
  - playback.kind "youtube": https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/{publicId}?autoplay=1&mute=1  (publicId ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$)
  - playback.kind "twitch": https://player.twitch.tv/?channel={publicId}&parent={window.location.hostname}&muted=true  (publicId ^[a-z0-9_]{4,25}$)
  Never build an iframe from a value that fails its pattern. A close button returns to the pixel art.

- If LIVE_URL fails, fall back to the old x.com link. The wheel stats (SPINNING / IDLE, rpm) stay as they are.

2) DEGEN MODE: REWRITE ALL COPY
Short, lowercase, dry, crypto-native. No soft or poetic filler, no "little", "tiny feet", "bottled", "simple rules", no marketing voice. Use this copy exactly where it fits; delete any line that has no replacement here.
- Title / hero: "HAMLOCK" with the line "your bags. his legs."
- Under hero: "lock eth. the hamster runs. you get it back. maybe."
- Lock card title: "lock a bag". Distance label: "km to unlock". Under slider: "{work} work units · he does ~10 km on a good night". Amount label: "how much". Under amount: "0.001–1 sepolia eth. testnet. zero real value."
- Lock button: "LOCK IT". When the wallet already has a jar: "already locked. sit tight."
- Hamster card: name "squeektoshi", line "the only validator that eats seeds". Status SPINNING shows "HE'S COOKING"; IDLE shows "ASLEEP. COPE."
- My jar title: "your bag". Not connected: "connect to see your bag." Labels: "locked", "km", "rewards from paper hands". Progress line: "{settled} / {target} km settled · {live} km live, not settled yet".
- Open button: "CASH OUT". Break button: "PAPER HAND IT (-20%)". Break confirm: "you get {refund} eth back. {penalty} + {forfeited} goes to the people with spines. sure?" with buttons "do it" / "nvm".
- Deadline line: "auto-unlock in {countdown}. even hamsters take days off."
- Stats title: "the pot". Labels: "locked", "bags", "paper hand tax", "burned".
- Leaderboard title: "diamond paws". Columns: "wallet", "km run", "bags", "paper hands". Empty: "nobody's finished a run yet. be first."
- How it works title: "rules". Exactly five lines:
  "lock 0.001–1 sepolia eth. pick 1–100 km."
  "the counter starts when you lock. when squeektoshi runs your km, you cash out."
  "break early = you lose 20%. it goes to whoever's still holding. nobody left? burned."
  "30 days max. then it opens anyway."
  "no owner. no admin. just a hamster."
- Share on X text: "i trusted my eth to a hamster. it unlocks when @squeektoshi runs {km} km. #hamlock" plus the site URL.
- Footer: "testnet toy. zero real value. not affiliated with squeekchain. it's a hamster, dyor." plus the contract and source links.
Keep the current dark dot-matrix look, but louder: the lime accent stays, add the red LIVE badge, bigger numbers, less body text. Every number still comes from the contract or the APIs, never hardcoded.

jobs.objective:
Build "Race Squeektoshi": a polished, original browser GAME for Squeekchain, the hamster-powered proof-of-work toychain on Sepolia. It must be a game people want to replay, NOT a dashboard or explorer. Static site, no backend, no wallet needed to play.

HOSTING (IPFS): relative asset paths (Vite base './'), hash-based routing only, no server rewrites, works under any gateway subpath. Ship source + production build in dist/.

DATA: public Squeekchain API, read from the browser:
- GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status (live wheel: running/resting, rpm, speed, work units, current round)
- GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/measurement/stats?range=7d and ?range=30d (typical activity, records)
- GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/settlements?range=24h (settled rounds/blocks)
- GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/events?limit=20 (milestones)
Call the real endpoints first and build on the actual response fields; never invent fields or fake numbers. Facts: 1 work unit = 1 wheel turn ≈ 0.88 m; rounds are 600 seconds; testnet SQK has no monetary value. Poll /v1/status every 5s while a race is active, otherwise every 15s; back off on errors. If the API is unreachable, show a clear offline state and keep Ghost Race playable from a bundled snapshot clearly labeled as cached.

MODE 1 – LIVE RACE (when the wheel is running):
- Player runs by tapping a key/button in rhythm (SPACE/arrow keys on desktop, big tap button on mobile). Speed comes from tap cadence with a stamina bar, so mashing alone does not win.
- Opponent is the real hamster: its on-screen pace = live speed from /v1/status, smoothly interpolated between polls.
- Race lengths: 30 s sprint, 60 s, and 10-minute "full round". Show both distances in meters, live gap, finish screen, personal bests.

MODE 2 – GHOST RACE (always available, default when the wheel is resting):
- Race against the hamster's recorded performances from measurement stats (typical pace, best recorded day/record), clearly labeled "recorded", never presented as live.
- Show a sleeping hamster and "Squeektoshi is resting" banner when the wheel is idle, with a live check that switches to Live Race when running resumes.

MODE 3 – ROUND PREDICTOR:
- Before a 600 s round starts, player predicts the hamster's wheel turns for it (slider + number input, with a hint from the 7-day typical value). Predictions lock when the round starts.
- Resolve using real data: derive the round's work from the API (inspect which endpoint/field gives per-round work or a cumulative counter at round boundaries). Store pending predictions in localStorage; resolve them on the next visit if the data is available, otherwise mark "could not verify". Document the exact method in README.
- Scoring: exact band big bonus, tiered points by % error, streaks, last 20 predictions history.

PROGRESSION: local profile in localStorage (all access wrapped in try/catch, game still works if storage is blocked): nickname, bests per mode, total points, prediction streak, 8+ unlockable badges/titles. "Share result" copies a short text for X with the site URL.

LOOK & FEEL: dark dot-matrix/LED pixel style, amber/gold on near-black, original pixel-art hamster with run/idle/sleep animations, wheel spinning at real pace. Fun sound effects with mute toggle (muted by default until first interaction). Smooth 60 fps canvas animation, responsive from 360 px phones to desktop, keyboard and screen-reader friendly controls, no layout shift. Footer: "Fan-made game for Squeekchain. Sepolia testnet; SQK has no monetary value." Use only original art, no Squeekchain logos.

PAGES (hash routes): #/ home with live wheel status and mode select, #/race, #/ghost, #/predict, #/profile, #/how-to-play.

META: title, description, favicon, Open Graph and Twitter large-image card with an original OG image.

ACCEPTANCE: TypeScript strict, production build passes, no console errors, every number on screen comes from the real API or is labeled as recorded/cached, all three modes playable on mobile and desktop, offline state works. README: game rules, scoring, API endpoints and fields used, round-resolution method, how to build and deploy.

jobs.objective:
Build an English-language browser game called “Squeek Wheel Oracle” for the Squeekchain community.

Existing prototype and visual reference:
https://squeek-wheel-oracle.netlify.app

This is my prototype. Preserve its dark forest-green background, lime accents, animated hamster wheel, prediction gameplay and boss progression. Build a genuinely playable game, not a landing page or read-only dashboard.

CORE GAME
Players predict whether the real hamster’s measured activity over a clearly defined future time window will finish UNDER or AT/OVER an announced target.

Use a documented official Squeekchain API or verified public on-chain data source. Research the official documentation and verify the actual endpoints, contracts, units and update frequency before implementing. Do not invent APIs, contract addresses or telemetry.

Prefer cumulative wheel work or distance if available. Use differences between valid cumulative readings to measure activity over the game window. If distance is not available, use the actual supported metric and label its units correctly. Do not convert work into distance without a documented conversion.

Before each round, display:
- the metric, target and measurement-window duration;
- data source and freshness;
- the algorithm’s prediction;
- the player's UNDER and AT/OVER choices.

Lock the player's prediction before the measurement window starts. Freeze the target for the whole round. Settle only after receiving valid source readings covering the window. Explain the settlement rule in the UI. Equality counts as AT/OVER.

Handle stale data, unavailable APIs, counter resets and missing observations explicitly. Void unverifiable rounds without awarding points or dealing damage. Never silently replace real data with random values. If only a simulated demo can be implemented, label it clearly as DEMO and state that live integration is incomplete.

GAMEPLAY
- Correct prediction: 100 points and 20 damage to the Vacuum of the Void boss.
- Consecutive correct forecasts add 10 bonus points per additional win, capped at 50 bonus points.
- Incorrect prediction: zero points and streak reset.
- Five correct predictions defeat a 100-HP boss; a new boss then appears.
- Explainable algorithm opponent: use recent completed windows with the same metric and duration. Never expose future outcomes to the algorithm. Label it a statistical baseline, not an LLM.
- Animated hamster wheel, round history, score, streak, boss count, short narrative event messages, optional sound and JSON export.
- Save single-player progress locally and clearly disclose that browser scores are not tamper-proof.
- Responsive desktop/mobile layout and keyboard-accessible controls.

DATA AND SAFETY
Show source links, last successful update time and clear LIVE / STALE / OFFLINE / DEMO status.
No real-money betting, token launch, wallet transactions, approvals, paid rewards or unnecessary wallet connection.
Do not claim official Squeekchain affiliation or guaranteed Genesis eligibility.
Do not expose secrets in client code.
Do not copy another community project's design or implementation.

DELIVERABLES
A working website hosted through this IMD job, with source code and a short README describing the verified data source, settlement rules, limitations and tests.
Test the game flow, scoring, boss damage, reload persistence, mobile layout and unavailable-data behavior.
If an essential integration cannot be completed, document it honestly rather than pretending it works.

jobs.objective:
WHAT THE SITE IS FOR:
"SqueekPack: Jetstream Run" is a responsive, telemetry-driven Web3 retro-arcade gaming platform built specifically for the Squeekchain ecosystem. It transforms Squeektoshi's real-world physical hamster mining activity (Proof-of-Hamster) into dynamic arcade gameplay. Players navigate a vintage-helmeted hamster equipped with a steam jetpack through industrial copper conduits, where flight physics, wind speed, gravity, and score multipliers adapt in real time to live wheel telemetry fetched from Squeekchain's public API (https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status). The platform enables EVM wallet connectivity (MetaMask/OKX/Rabby) allowing players to cryptographically sign their high scores and compete on a round-based leaderboard.

WHAT EACH PAGE / SCREEN SHOWS:

1. Main Arcade View (Game Screen & Live HUD):
- Top Navigation & Telemetry HUD: Real-time Squeektoshi telemetry pill showing live wheel speed (RPM), hamster status ("SPINNING 🔥" or "SLEEPING 💤"), current block height, current score, audio mute/unmute toggle, and a "Connect Wallet" button.
- Main Canvas Area: 60 FPS HTML5 procedural 2D canvas displaying the player character (hamster with vintage motorcycle helmet & twin-nozzle jetpack), dynamic particle exhaust, 3-layer parallax mine background with rotating hamster wheels, industrial copper conduit obstacles, floating $SQK coins (+50 pts), and glowing Golden Nut power-ups.
- Pre-Game Idle Overlay: Shows animated "Tap or Press Space to Boost" indicator and current round mode banner (e.g. "Zoomies Mode Active: 2x Points!").

2. Game Over & Score Submission Modal:
- Summary Card: Final score, distance reached, $SQK coins collected, and the telemetry mode active during the run.
- Web3 Score Attestation: If wallet is connected, displays truncated address (e.g., 0x12...ab) with a "Sign & Submit High Score" button that triggers personal_sign with the score and current Squeekchain block height.
- Action Buttons: "Play Again (Instant Restart)" and "View Leaderboard".

3. Leaderboard Modal / View ("Hall of Squeeks"):
- Interactive ranking table showing: Rank (#1 to #50), Player Address / Alias, Score, Active Mode (Zoomies / Night Shift), Block Height, and Date.
- Filter toggle between "Current Round" and "All-Time Legends".
- "Your Best Score" sticky footer banner.

4. Live Telemetry Inspector & Lore Modal ("About the Hamster"):
- Explains the connection between the game and Squeekchain's Proof-of-Hamster consensus.
- Live Telemetry Dashboard: Direct monitor displaying raw API readings from api.squeekchain.com (RPM, speed in mm/s, cumulative work units, and core status) with a direct link to the official Squeekchain livestream and whitepaper.

5. How to Play & Controls Modal:
- Visual control guide: Touch/tap for mobile, Spacebar/Left-Click for desktop.
- Power-up legend: Explains $SQK token value, Golden Nut 3-second invulnerability, and how Squeektoshi's real wheel speed triggers either "Zoomies" (tailwind + 2x multiplier) or "Night Shift" (neon dark mode + heavier gravity).

jobs.objective:
Every 10 minutes Squeekchain certifies how much work the wheel did. Players bet testnet ETH on whether the next round lands over or under a line, then anyone can press Settle and the contract reads SqueekCore directly and pays winners pro rata. There is no admin, no fee and no oracle, and every stake is refunded if nobody backed the winner or SqueekCore never certifies the round.

AI on the wheel: each upcoming round gets an AI line from a decay-weighted model of recent rounds. Players bet that the hamster beats the AI or that the AI holds, and a DeepSeek analyst explains the line in plain words. An Ask AI chat answers questions about the site in English or Vietnamese.

Also built in: lines taken from the wheel's recent quartiles, a leaderboard of top earners and AI slayers rebuilt from onchain events, invite links that open a specific round and bet, claim history with transaction links, and the full contract source inside the app.

It reads the live SqueekCore reported by the Squeekchain API, because the core in the published deployment record has stopped receiving settlements. The app warns if the API ever switches to another core.

The code repository is https://github.com/ekervo/wheel-odds and the executable is https://wheel-odds.vercel.app.

- Emission engine 0xcd46990f8349057335289Ef282c276204B6CDC62 — implementationCodeVersion()==9; checkpoint()=0xc2c4c5c1 (permissionless); checkpointStatus()->(bool corePaused,uint64 nextRound,bool roundSettled).

versions.objective:
Write Burrow, one protocol for Squeekchain on Ethereum Sepolia where a Squeek NFT can be collateral, a marketplace and a Uniswap v4 hook both pay their fees to the same vault, and bonding sells discounted shares for assets the treasury keeps. Foundry, unit tests plus Sepolia fork tests, and a deployment script the operator runs. Do not deploy from the job.

The vault share token is named Burrow SQK, symbol bSQK, 18 decimals. Holding bSQK is the single way to earn from everything: loan interest, marketplace fees and swap fees all arrive as SQK into the vault and raise the share price. There is no rebase and no second staking contract.

LIVE ADDRESSES, every one verified by calling it; pass them to constructors, never hardcode. SQK 0x5501e1fa81be1c3f49225fa7668da0245d07db60, ERC20 with EIP-2612 permit, 18 decimals. Squeek NFT 0xcb98349c134ab983da5bfd80527dfe2552bdb70f, ERC721, 9987 minted. Squeekchain staking 0x4b67b739dfd832f4eac67a7aa3bc244fb74cea4f exposing deposit(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), withdraw(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), claim(address recipient), setClaimRecipient(address), claimable(address) view, basePower(address account, uint8 collection) view, accountPower(address) view, stakeOf(address) view, stake(uint256), unstake(uint256 amount, uint256 maxFee, uint64 deadline) returns (uint256 net), quoteUnstake(address,uint256) view, exitPolicy() view returning (uint16 minBps, uint16 maxBps, uint16 saturationBps, uint8 windowDays, uint256 pressureFloor), live value (200, 6000, 2000, 7, 21000000e18). Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0xE03A1074c86CFeDd5C142C4F04F1a1536e203543, PositionManager 0x429ba70129df741B2Ca2a85BC3A2a3328e5c09b4, Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3. The public Squeekchain docs are stale for this deployment: their claimable(uint8,uint256[]) and position(uint8,uint256) selectors revert here, so call no signature this objective has not listed.

1. BurrowValuer. creditLine(uint256[] tokenIds) view returns the SQK a borrower may owe, equal to summed NFT power times pricePerPower times ltvBps over 10000. Power per level comes from a table set at construction matching the published policy 1000, 3000, 7000, 15000, 31000, 63000 and upward. There is no NFT market on this chain so pricePerPower is governed and is the main attack surface: the owner may move it only through a two day timelock, by at most 20 percent per change, inside a hard band fixed at construction. ltvBps capped at 6000. Events on proposal and execution with old and new values.

2. BurrowVault, ERC20 bSQK, the lending core and the single fee sink.
Lenders: deposit(uint256 assets) mints shares against totalAssets, which is idle SQK plus principal outstanding plus accrued interest. withdraw(uint256 shares) burns and pays from idle SQK, with a clear custom error when utilisation leaves none.
Borrowers: openPosition(uint256[] tokenIds) pulls NFTs with safeTransferFrom, records each level, then calls staking.deposit and staking.setClaimRecipient so the collateral keeps earning for the vault. borrow(uint256 amount) requires debt plus amount at or below the valuer line. repay, repayAll and closePosition, which calls staking.withdraw and returns the NFTs once debt is zero. Interest is a fixed per second rate set at construction, capped at 50 percent a year, accrued on every touch.
Self repaying loans, the heart of this: sweepRewards() calls staking.claim for the vault and applies what arrives first to accrued interest, pro rata by each position's escrowed power, then to principal. While the hamster runs, the loans shrink by themselves. Anyone may call it.
Liquidation: when debt exceeds the line, liquidate(address borrower) lets anyone repay the debt and take the NFTs, with liquidationBonusBps capped at 1500, surplus recorded for the borrower. Liquidation reverts within one hour of a price change so governance cannot harvest borrowers.
Fee sink: donate(uint256 amount) pulls SQK and raises the share price without minting. The marketplace and the hook call it. Nothing else is needed to pay stakers.
Bonding: bond(address asset, uint256 amountOrId, uint256 minShares) accepts a Squeek NFT or a v4 SQK pool position, values an NFT through the valuer and a position through its SQK principal, mints bSQK worth that value plus bondDiscountBps capped at 2000, vesting linearly over bondVestingDays, claimable with claimBond(). Bonded assets stay in the treasury; bonded NFTs are staked so they earn.

3. BurrowMarket. list(uint256 tokenId, uint256 price), cancel, buy with SQK pulled from the buyer, and a Dutch auction used for liquidated NFTs that decays linearly from a premium to a floor over a fixed window. Every sale takes feeBps, capped at 500, and forwards it with vault.donate. Sellers are paid the rest in the same transaction.

4. BurrowHook, a Uniswap v4 hook for the SQK pool, built on BaseHook from v4-periphery against the PoolManager above. Permissions: afterSwap and afterSwapReturnDelta only, declared in getHookPermissions. In afterSwap, when the output currency is SQK, skim hookFeeBps capped at 100 of the output, take it from the PoolManager with poolManager.take, and forward it with vault.donate; when SQK is not the output currency, take nothing. A v4 hook only works if its address carries its permission bits, so the deployment script must mine a CREATE2 salt with HookMiner and deploy through the deterministic deployer, and a test must assert the deployed address has exactly the declared flags.

RULES. Solidity 0.8.26, OpenZeppelin for ERC20, ERC721Holder, SafeERC20, ReentrancyGuard and Ownable2Step, v4-core and v4-periphery for the hook. Every value moving external function nonReentrant, checks effects interactions. Custom errors only. Token id arrays capped at 32, strictly ascending, no duplicates. The owner has no path to user assets: the only powers are pausing new borrows, the timelocked price, and parameters inside their hard caps.

TESTS. Unit tests on a mock staking contract mirroring the real one: share price never falls on deposit or withdraw, borrow refused above the line, interest accrual, sweepRewards cutting debt, liquidation one wei either side of the boundary, the timelock rejecting early or oversized moves, the post move liquidation freeze, bond vesting and discount caps, marketplace fee routing into the share price, hook flags matching its address, and every custom error. Fork tests with vm.createSelectFork pinned to a Sepolia block, deal for SQK, vm.prank on a real Squeek holder, proving against the real deployed staking and NFT contracts a full round trip: escrow, still earning, borrow, sweep, repay, close. Invariants: total assets never fall except on withdrawal, and summed debt never exceeds summed credit lines. Ship script/Deploy.s.sol reading the live addresses and parameters from environment variables, mining the hook salt, deploying all four and wiring them, plus a README with every address, every assumption, the unaudited testnet only warning, and the exact forge commands.

Burrow v2. After a full re-audit the operator rewrote the protocol so every contract deploys under the Sepolia 16.7M gas-per-transaction cap, and deployed it: vault 0xB63AbAb9019fa0Db4A3Ab1824C5E5Fa7171f1472, valuer 0x8F677a270fFd8769C01876216991c98561302C7b, market 0xDF0b997E701AaB73e69417e1910a9a9D93F0De8d, hook 0x9e0827db5831c49F9390707b467aA12A76E74044, all Sourcify exact matches. jobs.objective:
TITLE: AĞLA FENERBAHÇEM AĞLA — FULL MUSIC VIDEO

Create ONE COMPLETE, cinematic, satirical Turkish football music video lasting EXACTLY 180 SECONDS (3:00 minutes).

MANDATORY: Deliver the entire 3-minute finished video, NOT a trailer, teaser, preview, or 20-second sample.

If necessary, generate multiple shorter video sequences internally, then edit, transition, and combine them into ONE seamless 180-second MP4. Do not reduce the total duration.

CONCEPT:
A beautifully tragic but extremely funny music video about Fenerbahçe's repeated championship disappointments. Every season begins with new hope, new presidents, new coaches, expensive transfers and grand promises. Every season ends with the same exaggerated sadness.

The main recurring visual joke is hundreds of devastated yellow-and-navy supporters dramatically crying together.

VISUAL STYLE:
Ultra-realistic cinematic football documentary mixed with exaggerated dark comedy. Realistic Istanbul locations, Kadıköy football stadium, dramatic rain, emotional close-ups, slow motion, atmospheric stadium lighting, professional editing, 16:9, 1920x1080, 24 fps.

COMPLETE 180-SECOND STORYBOARD:

SCENE 1 — 00:00–00:15
A rainy evening in Kadıköy. Aerial shots of the football stadium. Empty seats, abandoned scarves, devastated supporters. A lonely fan looks toward the pitch as tears roll down his cheeks. Deeply melancholic cinematic opening.

SCENE 2 — 00:15–00:30
Summer arrives. Fenerbahçe fans are suddenly optimistic. Sunshine, excited crowds, supporters celebrating new dreams. The same disappointed fan from the opening becomes wildly enthusiastic.

SCENE 3 — 00:30–00:45
Time advances rapidly from summer to May. Football matches, missed goals, last-minute defeats and disappointed supporters. Happiness gradually turns into sadness.

SCENE 4 — 00:45–01:00
The endless presidential cycle. One club president leaves his office, another arrives confidently. Coaches repeatedly change. Expensive new players sign contracts. Everyone promises victory. Humorous cinematic transitions show that the same cycle keeps repeating.

SCENE 5 — 01:00–01:15
FIRST CHORUS: "Ağla Fenerbahçem ağla!"
A devastated yellow-and-navy supporter begins dramatically crying in the rain. Hundreds of nearby supporters join him. Show tearful faces, soaked scarves and exaggerated slow-motion reactions.

SCENE 6 — 01:15–01:30
"Sarı ve lacivertim ağla!"
An enormous stadium-wide shot of thousands of yellow-and-navy fans crying together. Rain pours dramatically. Scarves wave slowly. The spectacle feels like a tragic blockbuster, but the absurdity is unmistakably funny.

SCENE 7 — 01:30–01:45
A rapid montage of football excuses and disappointments. Supporters complain about referees, missed opportunities and poor tactics. Emotional faces, frustrated coaches, supporters covering their eyes.

SCENE 8 — 01:45–02:00
More coaches arrive and leave. New expensive international stars pose at presentations. Huge expectations build again, followed by missed chances and gloomy stadium exits.

SCENE 9 — 02:00–02:15
Another summer transfer celebration. Supporters cheer like the championship is already guaranteed. Suddenly the scene changes to another disappointing season finale. The same supporter returns to his familiar crying pose.

SCENE 10 — 02:15–02:30
A rapid visual journey through multiple seasons. Changing calendars, stadium celebrations, hopeful fans, disappointed crowds. Each season follows the same emotional cycle.

SCENE 11 — 02:30–02:45
FINAL CHORUS: "AĞLAAA FENERBAHÇEM AĞLAAA!"
The biggest emotional climax. Thousands of supporters crying together in slow motion. Dramatic rain, epic stadium-wide camera movements, intense cinematic lighting. One supporter dramatically falls to his knees while holding his scarf.

SCENE 12 — 02:45–03:00
The music fades toward the ending. The lonely supporter sits in the empty stadium. A new summer sunrise appears. His phone announces another exciting transfer. He smiles with renewed hope, then one final tear rolls down his cheek.

Fade to black at EXACTLY 03:00.

AUDIO:
This video is designed for an existing Turkish song generated separately in Suno. If the original audio is provided and accessible, use it as the ONLY soundtrack and synchronize scene transitions to the real music, particularly the repeated "Ağla Fenerbahçem ağla" chorus.

If the original audio is unavailable, deliver the complete 180-second video without music so the existing song can be added later.

NO additional songs, generated vocals or narration.

PRODUCTION REQUIREMENTS:
- EXACT final runtime: 180 seconds.
- One complete MP4, H.264, 1920x1080, 16:9.
- All 12 scenes must be present.
- Consistent recurring main supporter.
- Natural character movement and realistic faces.
- Smooth professional editing and transitions.
- No repetitive still-image slideshow.
- No watermarks or gibberish text.
- No missing scenes, truncated ending or shortened runtime.
- Deliver the final MP4 file, not merely a storyboard or script.

MANDATORY FINAL DELIVERABLE: ONE FINISHED 3-MINUTE VIDEO.

STRATOKS — COHERENT STORYBOOK WORLD, WORKING QUALITY SAMPLE

Continue https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-2775-stratoks-living-world at 04f473dd3b1b6101efc37fb85418baa72605ee59, derived from kilicsln/stratoks d0ee752. Preserve its resource fixes and verified wallet implementation. Deliver source, static preview and owner-run package; no production deployment or paid gameplay. Goal: one convincing functioning settlement integrated into the existing large world.

1. SINGLE ART DIRECTION
Primary reference: Fabledom https://puls.games/fabledom for storybook buildings, readable silhouettes, coherent materials and a lived-in village. Tiny Glade https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/ is secondary for roof/wall/garden detail; Foundation https://www.polymorph.games/en/ for terrain-fitting settlement composition. Study their official screenshots. Use visual references, not copied game assets or recreated 3D engines. Choose ONE palette, isometric projection, scale, lighting direction and shadow system, documented in ART-DIRECTION.md. Keep the yellow sprout-headed STRATOKS species. Eliminate the current clash between detailed sprites, flat vector trees and primitive huts; recoloring alone is insufficient.

2. USE OPEN RESOURCES PROPERLY
Evaluate reusable code/assets from https://kenney.nl/assets and https://quaternius.com/; OpenGameArt is another option. Select compatible free-to-use assets with verified per-pack commercial/redistribution terms, preferably CC0; permissive code libraries are welcome. Record exact source URL, creator, version/hash, license and modifications in ASSET-SOURCES.md; include required licenses/credits. No purchases or ripped game art. Adapt selected assets to one style rather than mix unrelated packs. For 3D source models, render consistent transparent isometric sprites/atlases offline and ship reproducible settings/scripts plus editable sources as licenses permit. Keep the current renderer unless a small compatible change is necessary; do not replace the engine with a demo template. If no pack fits, make consistent original assets.

3. CONCRETE IN-GAME SAMPLE
Deliver at least three clearly distinct, coherent structure appearances: shelter, storage and work area, each with two meaningful shape/material variants, not tint-only changes. Bind to actual existing functions; where storage/work is part of a shelter, represent that zone honestly rather than invent a new simulated building. Show existing construction/damage states. Include matching broadleaf/conifer trees, shrubs, rocks, ground details and shoreline treatment. Use selective detail and open spaces, not a log carpet. Do not relocate entities, regenerate terrain or invent roads. Derive dressing from real terrain/structures and keep decorations non-interactive and distinguishable. Preserve forest, desert, island and cold-world access; visually compatible fallbacks must prevent missing assets elsewhere. Weather variants must follow actual biome/state.

Keep original characters recognizable; adapt edge treatment, scale and shadows to the environment. Carrying/working/resting/helping props and animations must reflect actual inventory/action; no fabricated tools. The sample must run with autonomous residents, selectable resources and camera movement, not a baked background image. Retain compact HUD, dark forest/charcoal panels, warm gold accents, readable type, resident inspector, minimap and unobstructed mobile controls. No large marketing overlay.

4. CLOSE EXISTING DEFECTS, NO FEATURE EXPANSION
Reproduce tests/chains.test.js fuel-placement failure. Determine whether ignition prerequisites changed or placement logic is wrong; correct implementation/test/comment consistently. Retain separate wood-only and wood-plus-ignition-material cases so a green test does not hide scattered fuel. Verify exact accounting and bounded pile growth in unattended multi-seed runs. Make wallet timing tests robust under load without weakening auth checks. Correct stale README checkpoint counts and broken evidence links. Preserve brain weights, memories, identities, stocks, world topology, profiles, auth recovery, proxy controls and schema; no reset. No new behaviors beyond fixes needed here.

5. ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE
Build on the pinned source; run backend/frontend tests, typecheck/build, wallet regressions and copied-fixture load/save/restart. Show a reproducible animated sample at 1440px and 390px, close/mid/far zoom, plus cold/desert fallback views. Use the same fixture/camera for before/after. Publish unedited screenshots, running-world capture, asset/contact sheets and source-to-render mapping. Measure frame/tick time and memory; no invented performance claims. Independently review visual cohesion in the working browser, resource quantities and preservation. List failed tests and incomplete requirements. A style guide, cosmetic menu update or attractive still image alone is not completion. Owner aesthetic acceptance is separate.

jobs.objective:
Find and evaluate X accounts that have consistently posted about Identity.md ($IMD) from May 1, 2026 to November 1, 2026.

The goal is to build a useful follow list: who covers IMD, what each account contributes, and why someone should follow them.

**Scope and discovery**

Search for `$IMD`, `Identity.md`, `identitymd`, official project handles, and relevant product names, links, and contract addresses. Verify that each result refers to this project rather than another token or organization using “IMD.”

Use multiple discovery methods: keyword searches across individual months, replies and quote posts, and accounts mentioned by relevant contributors. Do not rely solely on top search results or the official account’s network.

**Selection criteria**

Include an account in the main list if it has:

- At least one substantive original post, quote post, or reply about IMD in at least three separate months during the period.
- At least five substantive IMD contributions overall.
- At least one qualifying contribution since September 1, 2026.

Reposts without commentary, ticker spam, giveaways, referral-only promotions, and generic engagement replies do not qualify.

Create a separate “occasional but valuable” list for accounts that miss these thresholds but have published at least two unusually useful contributions, such as original research, technical explanations, dashboards, or well-supported criticism. Keep official and team accounts in a separate section.

**For each account, provide**

1. Display name, handle, and profile link.
2. Relationship to IMD: team member, builder, independent researcher, investor, trader, community member, critic, or unknown. Distinguish disclosed relationships from inference.
3. Posting consistency: qualifying posts found, active months, and most recent qualifying post. Treat counts as lower bounds unless coverage is demonstrably complete.
4. Main focus: tokenomics, swarm capabilities, NFTs, development, onchain data, trading, ecosystem news, or another specific topic.
5. What makes the account distinct, supported by examples.
6. Why someone should follow it—and what they would miss by following only the official account.
7. Any relevant limitations: repetitive promotion, weak sourcing, undisclosed incentives, or low original contribution.
8. Three representative post links with dates and short explanations of their value.

**Ranking and output**

Rank accounts by usefulness and original contribution, not follower count or bullishness. Reward accurate analysis, primary evidence, practical knowledge, and informed disagreement.

Start with a concise table of the strongest accounts, followed by individual profiles and the two separate lists. Finish with a recommended starter list of 5–10 accounts covering different perspectives, explaining each selection in one sentence.

Be as comprehensive as the available evidence allows. Do not invent accounts, posts, affiliations, or metrics. Clearly state search limitations and distinguish “no qualifying posts found” from “no qualifying posts exist.”

jobs.objective:
Turing Wheel is a free browser toy for the Squeekchain community: a shared LED computer clocked by the real hamster Squeektoshi. One wheel pass is one CPU cycle, read from the public Squeekchain API and the SqueekCore contract on Sepolia. It is a static site in Vite and strict TypeScript with no UI framework, no backend, no token and no real money.

Fix the five bugs below, found by QA at this commit, then rebuild and host the site. Change as little as possible. This is a repair, not a redesign: keep the look, copy and layout on every viewport the bugs do not mention. Do not add a dependency. Do not add console.log. Do not use the em dash character.

BUG 1: navigation loses keyboard focus. navButton in src/ui/app.ts scrolls to its target but leaves focus on the button, so the next Tab jumps back to the top of the page. After scrolling, move focus to the target with focus({ preventScroll: true }), giving the target tabindex -1 if it cannot take focus. Reduced motion handling of the scroll stays as it is.

BUG 2: thumbnails still animate under reduced motion. In src/ui/led/thumbs.ts, draw() renders Math.floor(t) when reduced is true, so each thumbnail still changes about 2.5 times a second. With reduced motion each thumbnail must be one still frame from a fixed constant t, never derived from the clock. tick() must not redraw on a timer in that mode, and setProgram() must still redraw once so a thumbnail never shows a stale program.

BUG 3: help tips stay open after an outside click in WebKit. helpTip in src/ui/chrome.ts closes on blur, but WebKit does not focus a button on click, so blur never fires. While a tip is open, a document pointerdown listener must close it when the event lands outside that tip's wrapper. Remove the listener when the tip closes. Keep the Escape, blur and toggle behaviour, and keep the rule that only one tip is open at a time.

BUG 4: on a landscape phone the wall is below the fold. At 844 by 390 the first viewport shows only the logo, because fitAll in src/ui/app.ts sizes the lockup from hero width alone. On short landscape viewports, about max-height 480px with orientation landscape, cap the lockup from the available height and tighten the hero so that the LED wall is visible in the first viewport on load. Viewports taller than that must not change.

BUG 5: spellcheck: false never reaches the DOM. h() in src/ui/dom.ts skips every prop whose value is false, so the editor's spellcheck: false is dropped and browsers can underline code. Make spellcheck: false set the attribute to "false". Every other prop with the value false stays skipped.

Build a complete, original, playable browser game called SQUEEKFOREST: SEEDKEEPER for the Squeekchain community.

This must be a NEW CODE BUILD, not a static website import, dashboard, landing page, or rehosting job.

Original project and visual reference:
https://github.com/Peymanworship/squeekforest

Original live site:
https://peymanworship.github.io/squeekforest/

Creator: @AhoteSpirit

CONCEPT

A living pixel forest powered by real Squeekchain data. Players become Seedkeepers who restore a procedurally generated forest through short interactive puzzles.

Preserve the original project's dark pixel-art forest atmosphere, glowing fireflies, trees, moonlight, and emerald palette.

CORE GAMEPLAY

- Fetch verified settled Squeek block height from https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/core.
- Generate reproducible 5x5 forest puzzles using the verified block height and available confirmed block evidence.
- Players select different seeds and plant them strategically on a grid.
- Each seed type has clear placement rules and environmental effects.
- Players must solve meaningful positioning puzzles with limited moves.
- Award local game points based on actual player choices, not random outcomes.
- New confirmed block milestones unlock new puzzles.
- Allow replaying previously unlocked puzzles.
- Make the game fully playable on mobile.

FOREST MEMORY

Store timestamped verified block-height snapshots locally. Display actual growth since the player's previous recorded visit, including additional blocks and trees. Never invent missing historical measurements.

Preserve the original forest growth rule: one additional visual tree every 60 settled Squeek blocks and a new grove every 1,200 blocks.

DATA INTEGRITY

Use documented Squeekchain public APIs. Validate responses and show LIVE, STALE, OFFLINE, or PRACTICE status clearly.

Offline practice must be explicitly labelled and must never appear to use verified live blockchain data.

No wallet connection, real-money gambling, token rewards, or transaction requirements.

MANDATORY DELIVERABLES

1. Create substantial NEW source code through this IMD build job.
2. Deliver a PUBLIC CODE REPOSITORY and a linked Pull Request containing the implementation.
3. Publish a working playable site on IMD.
4. Include a README, game instructions, data-source documentation, and testing evidence.
5. Test actual gameplay, scoring, persistence, mobile responsiveness, and API failure states.
6. Preserve clear creator attribution to @AhoteSpirit and acknowledge the original SQUEEKFOREST source.

A hosted website alone is NOT a completed deliverable. Do not mark the build complete without delivering a verifiable source repository and functional game.

This is an independent community project, not an official Squeekchain product. Do not claim guaranteed Genesis approval.

jobs.objective:
Build “Burrow Power,” an original, fully playable browser strategy game for the Squeekchain community. This is a game, not a dashboard, API wrapper, landing page, generic puzzle, or Number Slide reskin.

CORE GAME LOOP
The player manages an underground hamster burrow with three systems: nest warmth, garden health, and tunnel stability. Each shift has six turns. At each turn, the player allocates limited power to heat, water, or repair. Every choice changes the burrow’s condition and the next turn’s options. The shift succeeds if all three systems remain viable through turn six; otherwise it fails. Later burrow levels increase the challenge and unlock new upgrades. Show the rules, resource costs, consequences, score, and shift result clearly.

REAL SQUEEKCHAIN GAMEPLAY INTEGRATION
Use Squeekchain’s official public API as a real gameplay input, not just as a status display:
- Verify the current official API documentation, live schemas, field names, freshness rules, and event meanings before implementation.
- Fresh hamster wheel activity determines how much new in-game power is available each turn. Idle activity produces no new power; a visible reserve keeps the game playable.
- A real, confirmed Squeekchain round event unlocks one burrow upgrade or blueprint. Process each confirmed event once, including after refresh or restart.
- Show the source and observation time for live data. If the API is stale, unavailable, or returns an unsupported schema, pause live runs and explain why. Offer a separately labelled practice mode using a bundled fixture; never present fixture data as live.
- Document the exact conversion from real wheel measurements to in-game power. Calibrate and play-test the limits against real API values; do not invent chain data.

SITE
Create a polished, responsive site with:
1. **Burrow:** game introduction, current live-data status, and Start Shift.
2. **Play:** the complete playable game, resource meters, choices, turn feedback, and result screen.
3. **How to Play:** rules, scoring, the live-data connection, and clear disclosure that game points are not SQK.
Use an original dark, LED-dot Squeekchain-inspired art style. Support keyboard, mouse, and mobile touch. Save local progress safely; the game must still open if browser storage is unavailable.

SCOPE AND DELIVERY
This is a single-player browser game with local saves. No multiplayer backend, wallet, custom contract, token, betting, paid entry, financial reward, or private keys. Do not use the previous Number Slide project as the source.

Publish the working site and full source to a public GitHub repository. Include a README with setup steps, game rules, API endpoints/fields, conversion formula, tests, and limitations.

Before publishing, run the production build and test the complete six-turn game on desktop and mobile. Test fresh active data, idle data, stale data, API outage, unsupported schema, duplicate confirmed events, refresh/restart, and practice mode. Do not claim a test passed unless it was run. The deliverable is incomplete if it is only a dashboard or the live hamster data does not change gameplay.

Priority 1 — rewrite #how ("How COVER pays out") so a new reader understands the protocol before the click path. Replace or expand the current 01–03 steps with this structure and equivalent clear English:

A) One-line thesis: A buyer pays an mSQK premium for a fixed payout C. The claim pays if, over the next N certified SqueekCore rounds, the share of zero-work rounds is ≥ T.

B) Where rounds come from: Core advances on a ~10-minute clock. Only history at or before the certified frontier counts. A missing active record inside certified history counts as zero-work. Rounds past the frontier are unknown and do NOT count as zero-work just because time passed. If Core lags, settlement can wait indefinitely.

C) Terms: N ∈ {6,12,24,144}; T ∈ {30%,50%,70%}; cover amount C. Premium goes to CoverPool and the pool reserves C.

D) Settlement: After frontier ≥ inclusive end, anyone may settle. If zero-work/N ≥ T, the holder receives C; otherwise no payout. Premium stays in the pool either way. Early settlement is allowed when a certified prefix already decides the outcome (enough zero-work to hit T, or too few rounds left to reach T).

E) LPs: Deposit mints shares; redeem burns for free assets. Gates can block LP moves while a certified policy needs settlement/review. Shares can go to zero; reservations have no automatic timeout.

Keep the formula bar: zero-work rounds / N ≥ T → payout C. Keep the expandable early-settlement / LP disclosure, but do not let it be the only place that explains Core/frontier.

Also: in the hero illustrative window, keep “Illustrative window, not live round history” (or stronger: “Example only — not this Core window”).

- On quote failure, keep a visible error state on the button or immediately under it (do not silently revert to “Get quote” with the only message at the card bottom).
- Prefer failing fast across the Sepolia RPC list; do not leave the UI stuck spinning.

Priority 3 — naming clarity: next to Cover amount / Deposit / Redeem inputs, show a short chip or hint: “mSQK (on-chain symbol SQI)”. Keep the existing hero note and MockSQK address subtitle.

jobs.objective:
Build and publish SQUEEK & GLIDE for Squeekchain Genesis Code Lane. Deliver a playable 2D game, editable source and README for IMD continuation jobs. The player pilots; the real hamster supplies wind.

GAMEPLAY
Side-view endless flight. A round hamster pilots a homemade cardboard flying box with wooden braces and watermelon-seed-shell wings. The player stays at fixed horizontal position as the world scrolls left. Tap/click or press Space to flap upward; gravity pulls downward. Keep flap impulse and gravity constant. Ignore keyboard auto-repeat and duplicate touch/click events. Prevent page scrolling only for active game controls.
Paired cardboard walls extend from ceiling and floor, leaving a clear gap. Decorative gnaw marks must not create confusing collision edges. Vary gap heights within safe bounds; gaps never move vertically. Keep the first 10 gaps wide; narrow new gaps gradually from 11 to 30, then hold size constant. Never resize an existing gap. All consecutive gaps must be reachable at 2.2x speed, with safe clearance. Spawn by world distance to avoid bunching. Use a forgiving hitbox around the hamster and box, excluding decorative wings; fixed physics substeps or swept checks prevent tunneling at low frame rates.
Passing a pair awards 1 point once. Some gaps contain a sunflower seed worth 1 extra point, offset from center but reachable safely. Collect each once. Touching cardboard or top/bottom boundaries ends the run and stops scoring immediately. Animate a candy-wrapper parachute deploying, then show final score, local best and a prominent retry button.

LIVE HAMSTER CONTROLS SPEED
Only fresh hardware data; no practice, speed slider or simulated fallback. Enable play only with valid data. Reference: https://docs.squeekchain.com/developers/api/ and GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status .
Poll every 5 seconds with timeout, one request at a time, and backoff respecting Retry-After for 429/503. Require supported schemaVersion 1, non-null measurement, freshness online, provenance hardware, valid nonnegative numeric rpmMilli, and coreStatus ACTIVE or IDLE. Pause for malformed/unavailable data, COUNTER_FAULT, unknown schemas or non-hardware sources; never interpret them as rest. Check measurement.receivedAt and staleAfterSeconds so cached readings can age out between polls.
RPM = rpmMilli / 1000. Map 0-120 RPM to 1.0x-2.2x horizontal speed, clamped and configurable. Score never increases speed. Smooth valid speed transitions over about 2 seconds. Fresh IDLE readings use minimum speed and show 'Hamster đang nghỉ'. No changes to gravity, flap strength or gap height based on RPM.
Show live RPM, wind multiplier, connection status and a wheel animated at measured RPM. At zero RPM the wheel stops, while flight keeps minimum speed.
If a request fails or the reading becomes unusable, freeze physics, scrolling, scoring and animations that affect gameplay. Show a reconnecting/stale-data message and keep polling. After usable data returns, show a 3-second countdown before resuming; cancel the countdown if signal fails again. Pause hidden tabs; on return require fresh data and the countdown. Discard accumulated frame time on resume so nothing jumps. Retry resets all run state and retains only local best score. Handle denied/corrupt localStorage gracefully.

VISUAL DESIGN AND SCREENS
Original cozy storybook 2D art: cream hamster with orange cheeks, head and front paws visible above an open pale-yellow cardboard box. Add crossed tape, a mint star patch and a few bite marks. Two honey-brown popsicle-stick braces with simple wood grain reinforce the sides, tied with string; a small wooden tail fin completes the handmade craft. Keep the main body cardboard, not a heavy wooden crate.
Wings are black watermelon-seed shells with cream edges, attached with round wooden pivots. In side view, show one near wing and a partly visible far wing. Each flap moves both wings, pitches the box slightly upward and bobs the hamster. Strong wind trails its ears and a loose tape strip. Use clear shapes readable at small size.
On collision, a coral-pink candy wrapper with cream stripes unfolds into a parachute, with four strings tied to the box. Folded wrapper with serrated edges; no logos.
