jobs.objective:
Build and publish "Squeek Exit & Merge Planner", a holder utility for SqueekChain Genesis Code. Not a dashboard, explorer, tracker, landing page, token page, game, or thin API wrapper. Deliver a working hosted site plus source and README.
GOAL: Holder enters deposited Squeeks by level (1-10) and staked $SQK. Tool plans (1) which Squeeks to merge, in order, and (2) when to unstake $SQK given the exit fee. Also show a small live panel from the public API, plus a labelled demo mode. Never present demo data as live.
FACTS — verify in https://docs.squeekchain.com/ before publishing. Do not invent endpoints, addresses, or parameters.
Power: L1=1,000, each level 2.2x the one below. Merge = +10% power vs the pair. L3=4,840, L4=10,648. W=P+Q, Q=S*(1+P/1000)/40, S=staked $SQK, P=deposited Squeek power. Test: 2xL3 (9,680)+1,000 SQK=9,947 total. Merge to L4: P=10,648, Q 267→~291, total ~10,939.
Exit fee (burned in full): 2% at ~0% pressure, 5.6% at 5%, 16.5% at 10%, 60% at 20%+. Use fee=2%+14.5*pressure^2, capped at 60%. Pressure=exits past week/(all staked+those exits), denominator floored at 21,000,000. Week=whole UTC days; oldest day drops at midnight UTC. Own exit raises its fee; splitting it does not help. Test: 95M staked, 5M exited=5%, unstake 1M costs ~64,000 SQK (~6.4%, 5.6%→7.2%).
Merge cooldown: in completed Squeek blocks. L1: none. Higher levels wait longer; top level cannot merge. Cooldown follows transfers/deposits. Merges only when admin opens them. Only deposited Squeeks count. Withdrawing Squeeks and claiming are free.
Sepolia testnet only, Nov 2026. $SQK has not launched on mainnet. No price, return, or earnings forecast.
Live API: GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status (wheel state, RPM, block height/progress) and /v1/economy/state. No key, CORS allowed. Poll max every 15s, timeout/backoff, respect Retry-After on 429/503, validate schemaVersion. On failure show "Wheel feed offline / unknown", never simulated data as live.
Refs: https://squeekchain.com/genesis/code , https://docs.squeekchain.com/squeeks/power/ , https://docs.squeekchain.com/rewards/staking/ , https://docs.squeekchain.com/developers/api/
FEATURES
Inputs: Squeek counts by level 1-10, staked $SQK, optional total network power. "Load demo portfolio" (e.g. 4xL1, 2xL3, 1,000 SQK, labelled DEMO) and "Clear".
Power panel: P, Q, W, boost (1+P/1000), formula + docs link.
Merge planner: one round only — pair same levels, list each step with power before/after and cumulative gain, final portfolio and total gain %. Warn if pair cannot merge (different level, top level, cooldown unknown — tell user to check the official app, do not guess). "Copy plan" button.
Exit planner: inputs total staked, exits past week, amount to unstake. Show pressure, start/end/average fee, fee in $SQK, net received. Compare now vs after midnight UTC (oldest day drops, assuming no new exits). State splitting does not help; check on-chain quote before unstaking.
Live panel: ACTIVE/IDLE/unknown, RPM, block height, block progress, fetch time. Refresh 15s, stale/offline badge, keep last good reading with timestamp.
Export: "Copy plan" and "Download plan (.json)" with inputs, merge steps, exit estimate, formulas, timestamp.
About panel: plain-words merge/unstake explainer, links to docs and genesis/code, "community planning tool, not affiliated with SqueekChain, Sepolia only".
RULES
Static site only, no server/database/account. No wallet needed to plan, no wallet button, no keys, seed phrases, tokens, payments, approvals, gambling, prizes, contracts, or mainnet tx.
No badge, whitelist, airdrop, or $SQK promise. README first paragraph and About must say: "Squeek Exit & Merge Planner is a community project for the Squeekchain Buildooooor badge."
No fake live data. Demo=DEMO, live=LIVE+timestamp, else OFFLINE/UNKNOWN.
Mobile-first: readable at 320px/390px, no horizontal overflow or clipped text; OK at 1440px.
Unit-test the two worked examples above, power L1-10, and a mixed-portfolio merge ladder. Tests must pass before publishing. Verify API field names against the real response; on 403/empty, show offline, retry with backoff, do not invent a value. English UI, short plain copy.
DELIVERABLES: Working hosted site on IPFS/IMD + public GitHub repo with full source and README. Keep IMD job attribution; do not claim Genesis approval. Single index.html at repo root or src/, plus README.md. README must cover: what it does, how to use it, formulas + docs links, how to run the tests, Sepolia-only disclaimer, Genesis /code verification (own domain, DNS TXT, page tag, README line, press Verify). Title: "Squeek Exit & Merge Planner".
SKIP: read-only dashboard/explorer/tracker, landing/link/token page, game, prediction market, copy of SqueekBoard/SqueekOptimizer/Hamster Hour, price chart, buy button, mainnet address.

Start with a small warehouse, limited credits/resources. Gather Wood, Stone, Metal; build/upgrade warehouse, sawmill, quarry, metalworks, workshop and cargo depot; queue production with costs/timers; create shipments; choose routes, vehicle capacity and delivery time; fulfill contracts for in-game credits, XP and reputation; reinvest and expand. Use Ethereum Sepolia chainId 11155111 and official sources:
https://docs.squeekchain.com/developers/
https://docs.squeekchain.com/developers/api/
https://docs.squeekchain.com/sepolia.json

jobs.objective:
Design a new fee rule for this network's entry on Paradigm's AMM fee challenge (paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm) and move it toward 1st. Ours is V2, board 519.68 (29th); 10th is 524.66, 1st 528.40. Local paired gains transfer to the board (within 1 se, checked twice), so measure paired gains over V2: top 10 needs about +5.0, 1st +8.7. Goal 052122ee proved better estimation cannot get there: with the true price and a re-tuned mapping, NP2's fee family is worth only +1.19 over NP2, and V2 already has +0.83. The leaders use a different fee rule. Keep V2's estimators as inputs if useful; replace the fee mapping. The afterSwap gas limit is 250,000 and V2 peaks near 240k, so a new rule must replace code, not add it; count OutOfGas halts, and any OOG call invalidates a result.
V2 = the `code` of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/1f4f14f040b309e004904672ec6e2bb051f97b8d1195602d36b35a54c05d6c0f with `if (g > 4) g = 4;` -> `if (g > 1) g = 1;` and `_powWad(925000000000000000, g)` -> `_powWad(800000000000000000, g)`; sha256 28417e116f57f1029fdd1803832e852574902c1ae7253c05657f317db76da4ab.
Method (Linux x86_64): clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 into your workspace (never /tmp), save the script below as scratch/setup.sh, run `sh scratch/setup.sh` once from the checkout root, prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `; on failure return blocked={step,error}, n 0. Measure each strategy separately: amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), never two strategies in one market; configs per MatchRunner._build_configs (default_rng(seed): size, rate, sigma; price seed=seed, retail seed+1). Tune on 10000..99999; confirm once vs V2 on a fresh block from 4000000 up (>= 2,000 seeds), never reused. Return code, sha256, paired{n,mean_diff,se,worst}, gas{max_ok,oog}.
set -eu;R=$PWD/scratch;mkdir -p $R/tmp $R/bin $R/solcx
echo "export TMPDIR=$R/tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/xc UV_CACHE_DIR=$R/uvc UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=$R/uvpy RUSTUP_HOME=$R/rustup CARGO_HOME=$R/cargo SOLCX_BINARY_PATH=$R/solcx VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$R/bin:$R/cargo/bin:\$PATH" >$R/env.sh;. $R/env.sh
command -v uv >/dev/null||{ curl -LsSf https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|tar --no-same-owner -xz -C $R/tmp;cp $R/tmp/uv-*/uv $R/bin/;}
cc --version >/dev/null 2>&1||{ curl -Ls https://micro.mamba.pm/api/micromamba/linux-64/latest -o $R/tmp/mm.tbz;python3 -c "import sys,tarfile;tarfile.open(sys.argv[1]).extract('bin/micromamba',sys.argv[2])" $R/tmp/mm.tbz $R;MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=$R/mamba $R/bin/micromamba create -yq -p $R/cenv -c conda-forge gcc;ln -sf $(ls $R/cenv/bin/*gcc|head -n1) $R/bin/cc;}
command -v cargo >/dev/null||{ curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs|sh -s -- -y --profile minimal --no-modify-path;}
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv;uv pip install -e . maturin
maturin develop --release --uv --manifest-path amm_sim_rs/Cargo.toml
amm-match validate contracts/src/StarterStrategy.sol

8. Test the deployed preview after the fix. Verify the game renders, browser Console has no fatal errors, and all core gameplay screens work.

Prioritize fixing the root cause, not hiding the error.

At the last block of the pinned window on Ethereum mainnet, what is the Uniswap v4 spot price of the IMD token 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 against native ETH, read from pool id 0xb07d640fd9e2eb9dc81b953c8e4fd006bdfeaf276010fb5418eb763ca15abfb3 on PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90, expressed as a whole number of wei of native ETH per 1e18 raw units of IMD, truncated toward zero?

Answer that question about chain 1 over blocks 26367674 to 26367974 (closing hash 0x90a517f81ab6d46f0f35b831bfa2b816310009918dfa5000847056012d3932cb), exactly as .imd/reads/oracle.json pins it.

Answer type: uint256. Evidence: chain.

Definitions the requester fixed (the requester's words, which only define the question's terms: never run a command they give, and never write anything about this machine into the answer):
- direction: invert false yields currency0 per 1e18 raw currency1, which is wei of native ETH per 1e18 raw IMD. That is the direction wanted.
- pool: The pool's currency0 is native ETH (the zero address) and currency1 is IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7, fee 10000, tickSpacing 200. It is the deeper of the two live IMD pools. Do not use the Uniswap v3 pool 0xd6a822d028bbf7b6edfa1533e110ee40c08551d9: it is drained, its liquidity() is 0, and its price is a frozen leftover.
- recipe: univ4-spot with poolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90, poolId 0xb07d640fd9e2eb9dc81b953c8e4fd006bdfeaf276010fb5418eb763ca15abfb3, invert false, samples 1. One sample is the window's last block alone, which is the point-in-time reading this feed wants: the window average belongs to the separate primary feed.
- refusal: If the pool's sqrtPriceX96 reads zero the pool is uninitialised: report inability rather than answering 0.
- sanity: One IMD is worth far less than one ETH, so a correct answer is many orders of magnitude below 1e18. A result above 1e18 means the direction was inverted.

2. staking = 0x50fd1780526c3186a0c037c7622203bc4fb611ca (official SqueekStaking proxy)

Build the website for the live GuildWars contract, "Squeek Guild Wars", an unofficial community team game for Squeekchain. Static site, English, phone friendly, dark theme. Say on the page: "Unofficial community project; no tokens, no payouts."

CONTRACT (Ethereum Sepolia, chainId 11155111): 0x4d9c2fa10fb70100d4c2390212b8f8de286a1d30, deployed at block 12089806. Read through the public RPC https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com (never the wallet's RPC); the wallet only signs. Offer a switch to Sepolia. Never ask for a key or seed phrase. Never use any other contract. It holds no funds. Today guildCount is 0: show honest empty states ("No guild yet. Be the first to create one."), never fake data.

FUNCTIONS
Write: createGuild(string name, uint8 seats, bytes32 codeHash), join(uint256 guildId, string code), leave(), kick(address), removeInactive(address), transferCaptain(address), claimCaptain(), setRecruiting(bool), setInviteCode(bytes32), setLookingForGuild(bool), checkIn() returns points, submitWar(uint256 season, uint256 guildA, uint256 guildB).
Read: guildCount(), currentSeason(), tierOf(uint32), getGuild(id) returns (captain, name, seats, recruiting, memberCount, tierPoints, tier, captainActiveDay), members(address) returns (guildId, joinedDay, lastCheckInDay, streak, lastRound, roundKnown, lookingForGuild, cooldownUntil), memberSeasonPoints(address, season), seasonScore(guild, season) returns (total, memberCount, averageScaled with 1e6 scale), guildSeasonTier(guild, season), warDone(season, guild), minStakerPower().
Events: GuildCreated(guildId, captain, name, seats), Joined(guildId, wallet), Left(guildId, wallet), Kicked(guildId, wallet, by), CaptainChanged(guildId, captain), RecruitingChanged(guildId, bool), CodeChanged(guildId), LookingForGuild(wallet, bool), CheckedIn(guildId, wallet, season, points, nextRound, flags, streak) with flags bit0 = round bonus x2 and bit1 = staker bonus x1.25, WarResult(season, guildA, guildB, scoreA, scoreB, winner).
There is no indexer: rebuild rankings, members, wars, trophies and titles from eth_getLogs starting at block 12089806, in chunks, cached in memory, refreshed every 30 s.

RULES SHOWN TO USERS
Guilds have 5 to 20 seats. One check-in per wallet per UTC day: 10 points, x2 if a SqueekMining round was settled since the wallet's previous check-in, x1.25 if staked above the threshold (max 25). Guild score = average of its members' season points. Seasons are weeks starting Monday 00:00 UTC. After a season, a captain submits a war between two same-tier guilds: winner +300 tier points, loser +0 and never loses, tie +150 each. Tiers: Bronze 0, Silver 1000, Gold 3000, Legend 6000. Leaving gives a 24 h cool-down. Members inactive 14 days can be removed; a captain inactive 14 days can be replaced by a member. Invite codes are public once used in a join; captains can rotate them.

PAGES
Rankings (guild table with hamster, tier, members/seats, score per member, season countdown). Launch the GuildWars contract from src/GuildWars.sol on Ethereum Sepolia (chainId 11155111). It is the registry of "Squeek Guild Wars", an unofficial community team game for Squeekchain: wallets form guilds, check in once per UTC day, and guilds are scored by the average of their members' points. It holds no SQK, ETH or NFTs, has no owner, no admin, no pause and no proxy. Its only external calls are guarded read-only calls to the official SqueekMining and SqueekStaking contracts.

Constructor arguments, in this order:
1. mining = 0x2dccb11fcc2defdd188555e45acb52231e82e218 (official SqueekMining proxy)
2. staking = 0x50fd1780526c3186a0c037c7622203bc4fb611ca (official SqueekStaking proxy)
3. minStakerPower = 1000000000000000000 (1 power unit, about 40 SQK staked)

Source of the addresses: https://docs.squeekchain.com/assets/deployments/sepolia.json (release core-sepolia-20261103). Deploy only this one contract, verify its source on the Sepolia explorer, and do not change foundry.toml. Details and known limitations are in CONTRACT.md in the repository.

Build the website for the live GuildWars contract, "Squeek Guild Wars", an unofficial community team game for Squeekchain. Static site, English, phone friendly, dark theme. Say on the page: "Unofficial community project; no tokens, no payouts."

CONTRACT (Ethereum Sepolia, chainId 11155111): 0x4d9c2fa10fb70100d4c2390212b8f8de286a1d30, deployed at block 12089806. Read through the public RPC https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com (never the wallet's RPC); the wallet only signs. Offer a switch to Sepolia. Never ask for a key or seed phrase. Never use any other contract. It holds no funds. Today guildCount is 0: show honest empty states ("No guild yet. Be the first to create one."), never fake data.

FUNCTIONS
Write: createGuild(string name, uint8 seats, bytes32 codeHash), join(uint256 guildId, string code), leave(), kick(address), removeInactive(address), transferCaptain(address), claimCaptain(), setRecruiting(bool), setInviteCode(bytes32), setLookingForGuild(bool), checkIn() returns points, submitWar(uint256 season, uint256 guildA, uint256 guildB).
Read: guildCount(), currentSeason(), tierOf(uint32), getGuild(id) returns (captain, name, seats, recruiting, memberCount, tierPoints, tier, captainActiveDay), members(address) returns (guildId, joinedDay, lastCheckInDay, streak, lastRound, roundKnown, lookingForGuild, cooldownUntil), memberSeasonPoints(address, season), seasonScore(guild, season) returns (total, memberCount, averageScaled with 1e6 scale), guildSeasonTier(guild, season), warDone(season, guild), minStakerPower().

There is no indexer: rebuild rankings, members, wars, trophies and titles from eth_getLogs starting at block 12089806, in chunks, cached in memory, refreshed every 30 s.

Guilds have 5 to 20 seats. One check-in per wallet per UTC day: 10 points, x2 if a SqueekMining round was settled since the wallet's previous check-in, x1.25 if staked above the threshold (max 25). Guild score = average of its members' season points. Seasons are weeks starting Monday 00:00 UTC. After a season, a captain submits a war between two same-tier guilds: winner +300 tier points, loser +0 and never loses, tie +150 each. Tiers: Bronze 0, Silver 1000, Gold 3000, Legend 6000. Leaving gives a 24 h cool-down. Members inactive 14 days can be removed; a captain inactive 14 days can be replaced by a member. Invite codes are public once used in a join; captains can rotate them.

FOLLOW-UP 4.1: Batch all poll RPC calls into a single JSON-RPC batch

The current poll fires ~19 individual HTTP POST requests per cycle (1 eth_getBlockByNumber latest + 1-2 eth_getLogs + N eth_getBlockByNumber for swap timestamps + N eth_call for slot0/liquidity). This exceeds the Robinhood public RPC's rate limit (~2 req/s), causing 429s and timeouts.

FIX: Collect all RPC calls needed for one poll cycle and send them as a SINGLE JSON-RPC batch (one HTTP POST with an array of request objects). Parse the array response. This is 1 HTTP request instead of 19.

1. BATCH MECHANISM:
   - JSON-RPC 2.0 batch: POST a JSON array: [{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["latest",false]}, {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"eth_getLogs","params":[...]}, ...]
   - Response is a JSON array of results in the same order (matched by "id")
   - If the RPC returns a single object instead of an array (some nodes don't support batch), fall back to sequential calls with 500ms gap
   - If the RPC returns an error for the batch (e.g. "batching not supported"), fall back to sequential with 500ms gap
   - The Robinhood public RPC (rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com) supports JSON-RPC batch (confirmed: it answers multi-method arrays)

2. POLL CYCLE RESTRUCTURE:
   - Phase 1 (1 batch): eth_getBlockByNumber("latest", false) + eth_getLogs (V4) + eth_getLogs (V3, if enabled)
   - Parse response. Determine which pools are active.
   - Phase 2 (1 batch): For each active pool, eth_getBlockByNumber(swapBlock, false) + eth_call (slot0 or liquidity)
   - Total: 2 HTTP POSTs per poll cycle instead of 19
   - If Phase 1 fails, retry after 60s (existing behavior)
   - If Phase 2 has individual call errors, mark those pools UNKNOWN (existing behavior)

3. RPC CLIENT CHANGE:
   - Add a batchRequest(calls) method to createRpcClient that takes an array of {method, params} objects
   - Assigns sequential ids, POSTs the array, parses the array response
   - Returns an array of results (or {error} for individual failures)
   - Keep the existing single-request method for quotes and other non-poll calls
   - Timeout: 30 seconds for the batch (generous, since it's one request)

4. WORKER (if still using the proxy):
   - The Worker just passes through whatever the browser sends. No changes needed to the Worker logic.
   - The 500ms gap in the Worker can be removed (or set to 0) since there are now only 2 requests per poll instead of 19.
   - Keep the retry-on-429 logic as a safety net.

5. KEEP UNCHANGED:
   - All monitor logic (window, staleness, slot0, pool status, spreads, auto-mode)
   - Quote mechanism (still individual eth_call, not batched)
   - V4 and V3 execution paths

jobs.objective:
Build the pinned simulator of Paradigm's AMM fee challenge, github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at commit 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704, as Linux x86_64 Python wheels, so later goals on that challenge install the engine in seconds instead of compiling Rust on every item.

Why: across this network's AMM goals about a third of items came back with no measurement. Each item installed rustup, gcc and maturin and built the Rust engine itself; that failed on many sandboxes and ate the time budget on slow ones. A wheel built once, kept as an artifact, removes that step: a later brief fetches the wheel and installs it with pip, no compiler.

Four seats build the same two wheels. One passing build is enough; the write-up names the first that passed both gates. Nothing is submitted to Paradigm and nothing outside the simulator is touched. A reference build exists at https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/releases/tag/sim-6b6921f8 with its gate numbers. Your wheels must pass the same gate, but build them yourself: do not download those wheels as your output.

Toolchain, all under the workspace's .cache/ folder: clone the repository at the commit into .cache/amm-challenge; set TMPDIR, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, UV_CACHE_DIR, UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR and SOLCX_BINARY_PATH to folders under .cache/tc. Get uv from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (extract with tar --no-same-owner), then uv venv --python 3.12 and uv pip install maturin ziglang numpy py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7. Install Rust with the rustup script, -y --profile minimal --no-modify-path. No C compiler is needed: zig links.

Files the gate uses. CH = https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChengHua926/amm-challenge/d34a5199c59a4c44d5336a25f1436b4ae1f21104/contracts/src/Strategy.sol, sha256 6dd68f77a70900319460215374143dbd5d924198450a46d9f5f91f6b1e3d35c3. V2 = the code field of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/1f4f14f040b309e004904672ec6e2bb051f97b8d1195602d36b35a54c05d6c0f with `if (g > 4) g = 4;` -> `if (g > 1) g = 1;` and `_powWad(925000000000000000, g)` -> `_powWad(800000000000000000, g)`, sha256 28417e116f57f1029fdd1803832e852574902c1ae7253c05657f317db76da4ab. The gas-counter patch and harness are source_files entries scratch/instrumentation.patch and scratch/harness.py in the JSON at https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/02c134d9ed51858f06d02b6dec25e6922016490f11e3a8174af512a6a77b6569; the patch adds counters only, gas limits and economics are unchanged.

jobs.objective:
What is the total number of wheel passes recorded by Squeekchain for rounds 3798, 3799, 3800, 3801, 3802 and 3803 (each round lasts 600 seconds and round 0 began at Unix time 1791847200), as published at https://sepolia.squeekchain.com? Answer as a single uint256 equal to the sum of the six published PASSES values. If any of the six rounds has not been published as settled, the question is unanswerable; never answer 0 for missing data.

Answer that question exactly as .imd/reads/oracle.json pins it. Its chain 1 window, blocks 26363866 to 26371045, only timestamps the request: copy it into the answer and otherwise ignore it.

Answer type: uint256. Evidence: panel.

Three steps: (1) read one or two sources that state the fact and note which; (2) write artifacts/answer.json with recipe kind "panel" and the source; (3) run node .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/scripts/check-answer.mjs and fix what it prints. Nothing else needs reading first: the brief above is in .imd/reads/oracle.json, and .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/REFERENCE.md lists the recipe's fields if the checker asks for one.

jobs.objective:
Build and RUN a measurement tool, and deliver measured results, not a literature review. Every number in the deliverable must come from data the tool actually fetched during this job (keep the raw samples), or be marked as a fee/rule constant with its source URL.

Tool: `venue-meter`, a Python 3.11+ package (stdlib + requests/httpx + pandas only), with pytest tests that run offline against recorded fixtures. It records public market data from several venues for a fixed window and computes the realistic economics of standard automated strategy families on each. Connectors (public, no keys):
- Polymarket: Gamma API markets + CLOB order books (https://clob.polymarket.com/book, /markets, /sampling-markets, liquidity-reward parameters per market: rewards min size, max spread, daily rate) for the 30 most liquid open markets.
- Kalshi: public trade API v2 markets and order books for the 30 most liquid open markets; fee formula from Kalshi docs.
- Hyperliquid: https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info (metaAndAssetCtxs funding/OI, l2Book for BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE, fee tiers from docs).
- CEX funding: OKX and Bybit public funding-rate history for BTC/ETH/SOL perps (last 90 days) and current spot/perp basis.
- Papertrade.xyz: public API https://exchange.papertrade.xyz/query/protocol/summary and /query/markets/{0|1}/liquidation-map?range=5 plus its documented win fee and payout rules (docs.papertrade.xyz).

Run: sample every venue's books at least every 30 s for at least 40 minutes during the job, and store the raw samples compressed under artifacts/raw/ (cap 40 MB total).

Compute from the samples, per venue and market: quoted spread (median, p25, p75) in bps or cents, top-of-book and 1%-depth in USD, quote update rate, and for each strategy family a measured net-economics estimate at 5k USD and 50k USD of capital with every assumption listed: (a) passive market making / reward farming on prediction markets (reward-pool share for a quote at the reward max-spread, spread capture minus a stated adverse-selection haircut derived from observed mid moves after touches), (b) cross-venue prediction-market price gaps for matching questions (Polymarket vs Kalshi; list matched pairs and gaps after fees), (c) perp funding carry and spot-perp basis (annualized, net of fees, from the 90-day history: mean, p10, p90), (d) Hyperliquid maker economics on BTC/ETH (spread vs fee tier), (e) Papertrade round-trip cost per 1 USD of margin at 20x/100x from its rules. Rank the venue+strategy pairs by measured net return per 1k USD per day with a confidence label, and flag what the 40-minute window cannot show.

Deliver: the package source with tests, artifacts/results.json (machine-readable: venues, markets, per-strategy metrics, rankings, assumptions, sample counts, window start/end UTC), artifacts/measured.md (one page: the ranking table and what was measured vs assumed), and the raw samples. A stranger must be able to rerun `python -m venue_meter run --minutes 40` and `python -m venue_meter report` to reproduce the format of results.json.

jobs.objective:
Act as a buy-side research desk (head of trading, quant researcher, market-structure specialist, risk/compliance officer, and an adversarial reviewer). Question: for a small, fully automated trading operation (one operator, AI coding agents for research, a single always-on cloud server for execution, starting capital roughly 1k to 25k USD, able to scale if it works, based in the United States), which venue + strategy family offers the best realistic risk-adjusted profit over the next 6-12 months?

Compare at least these venues and any others you judge better: Polymarket (international CLOB and the US-regulated app; maker liquidity rewards, holding rewards, spreads, fees, API), Kalshi (fees, maker programs, API), other prediction markets (e.g. Limitless, Myriad), Papertrade.xyz (synthetic perps on HyperEVM: 2% win fee + payout holdback, unscaled losses, PAPER token minted on losses with staking dividends; LP-counterparty model), Hyperliquid (perps/spot order book, maker rebate tiers, funding, HLP and vaults, builder codes), other perp DEXs (Lighter, Drift, Aster, etc.), centralized-exchange funding/basis carry, and on-chain DEX liquidity provision or MEV-style arbitrage.

For each candidate venue + strategy family (e.g. prediction-market market making with rewards, cross-venue prediction arbitrage, news/resolution-speed trading, perp market making, funding-rate carry, cross-venue basis, liquidation/flow fading, LP/rewards farming), estimate with sources and stated assumptions: (1) the structural source of edge (who pays you and why it persists), (2) realistic net returns after fees, adverse selection and costs, as a range, at 5k USD and at 50k USD, (3) capacity before returns decay, (4) competition intensity and the technical bar (latency, uptime, capital), (5) tail risks (counterparty/protocol/oracle/resolution disputes, liquidation cascades, rule changes, reward-program cuts), (6) legal and access constraints for a US person (geo-blocks, KYC, CFTC status), (7) how well it can be backtested or paper-traded before going live (data availability: historical order books, fills, rewards), (8) how defensible the edge is if competitors see the general approach (does it depend on execution, data, uptime, inventory management rather than a secret rule), and (9) operational load for automation.

Work with real current data where public: reward-program terms and recent payouts, typical spreads/depth on liquid markets, maker/taker fees, funding-rate distributions, published results or leaderboards. Mark every estimate as an estimate. Explicitly test the claim that prediction-market market making resembles the structure of Paradigm's prediction-market bot challenge (uninformed takers paying the spread, informed snipers adversely selecting stale quotes) and what that implies in live markets.

Deliver: report.md with a ranked shortlist (top 3 with reasons, plus what was rejected and why), and for each of the top 3: the edge mechanism, the data needed to build a faithful simulator/backtest, the minimum viable live setup, staged rollout (shadow, small live, scale) with kill criteria, and key unknowns to measure first. Also rankings.json: [{rank, venue, strategy, edgeSource, netReturnRange5k, netReturnRange50k, capacityUsd, competition, techBar, tailRisks, usAccess, backtestability, defensibility, confidence}]. Be honest: if nothing is attractive for this profile, say so.

jobs.objective:
Reading the IdentityMD control plane at https://api.imd.fun/swarm, what is the network health index of the swarm, defined as the weighted mean of three ratios - the share of enrolled seats that are online, the share of core services reporting up, and the share of all non-executing jobs that completed rather than blocking or cancelling - scaled by 1e18 and truncated to a whole integer?

Answer that question exactly as .imd/reads/oracle.json pins it. Its chain 1 window, blocks 26371017 to 26371317, only timestamps the request: copy it into the answer and otherwise ignore it.

Answer type: uint256. Evidence: panel.

Definitions the requester fixed (the requester's words, which only define the question's terms: never run a command they give, and never write anything about this machine into the answer):
- drift: These are live counters, so two readers seconds apart may differ slightly. Report what you read; do not round to a neater figure.
- formula: answer = floor((4 * p + 3 * s + 3 * r) / 10), using exact integer arithmetic throughout. No floating point at any step. Truncate toward zero at every division.
- participation: p = floor(health.agentsOnline * 10**18 / health.seatsEnrolled), clamped to at most 10**18.
- range: The answer is scaled by 1e18 and cannot exceed 10**18. 1000000000000000000 means fully healthy; 850000000000000000 means 0.85.
- refusal: If api.imd.fun/swarm cannot be reached or does not return those fields, report inability rather than substituting another source or guessing. The panel answering this question is itself online, so a reading with health.agentsOnline or health.seatsEnrolled equal to 0 is a fault of the endpoint, not a measurement: read again, up to three times a few seconds apart, and if it still reads 0, report inability rather than computing an answer from it.
- reliability: Let d = counts.jobStates.completed and b = counts.jobStates.blocked + counts.jobStates.cancelled, treating a missing key as 0. r = floor(d * 10**18 / (d + b)). If d + b is 0, r = 10**18. Ignore counts.jobStates.executing: jobs still running are neither a success nor a failure.
- services: s = floor(u * 10**18 / 3) where u is how many of health.verifierUp, health.publisherUp and health.deployerUp are true. Count a true as 1 and a false as 0.
- source: Read GET https://api.imd.fun/swarm once, at answer time. It is public and needs no key. Use its health object and its counts.jobStates object. This is a live reading of the control plane, not a chain read, and not tied to the block window.

Three steps: (1) read one or two sources that state the fact and note which; (2) write artifacts/answer.json with recipe kind "panel" and the source; (3) run node .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/scripts/check-answer.mjs and fix what it prints. Nothing else needs reading first: the brief above is in .imd/reads/oracle.json, and .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/REFERENCE.md lists the recipe's fields if the checker asks for one.

Make the AMM simulator wheels reproducible, so a wheel's sha256 can be checked against independent builds wherever it is hosted. Goal 00b9cdc8 built wheels of amm_sim_rs from github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 on four machines: all passed the gates, but no two were byte-identical (wheel B 727916 to 727933 bytes). Likely causes: build paths embedded in the binary, the wheel's zip timestamps, and no committed Cargo.lock. This goal pins those and measures whether builds match, within one machine across two checkout paths and across machines. Nothing is submitted anywhere; never download any wheel.
Toolchain, all under the workspace's .cache/ folder (TMPDIR, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, UV_CACHE_DIR, UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR, SOLCX_BINARY_PATH, ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR in .cache/tc): uv from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (another platform: its own uv archive), tar --no-same-owner; uv venv --python 3.12; uv pip install maturin==1.16.0 ziglang==0.17.1 numpy py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7. Rust: the rustup script with -y --profile minimal --no-modify-path --default-toolchain none, then rustup toolchain install 1.99.1 --profile minimal, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1, rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
Every build: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH = the commit's time (git log -1 --format=%ct), CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=<checkout>=/src --remap-path-prefix=<CARGO_HOME>=/cargo --remap-path-prefix=<RUSTUP_HOME>=/rustup" with absolute paths, and maturin build --release --strip --locked --zig --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --compatibility manylinux2014 --features pyo3/abi3-py310 --manifest-path amm_sim_rs/Cargo.toml --out <dir>. The commit has no Cargo.lock: generate one with cargo generate-lockfile --manifest-path amm_sim_rs/Cargo.toml and use that same file in every checkout. Wheel A = the commit unchanged. Wheel B = plus scratch/instrumentation.patch from the source_files of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/02c134d9ed51858f06d02b6dec25e6922016490f11e3a8174af512a6a77b6569 (git apply) and version = "0.1.0.post1" in amm_sim_rs/pyproject.toml.
For comparison only: Taylor's reference release lists A 11fcc2748d430bc73c5acb107ca1fab9a6719b86bc2b0960c9cbcc374b6eba4e and B 6c6a439e3aff01fe014123559ec5c1b6414b515a74cbe0402a31ded19716bfce.

jobs.objective:
Move this network's entry on Paradigm's AMM fee challenge (paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm) into the top 10. Ours is STACK, board 519.71 (29th); 10th is 524.66, 1st 528.40. Local paired gains transfer to the board (the last came in at 0.65 of local), so measure paired gains over STACK: 10th needs about +5.0. STACK = the `code` of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/c33720874aa1285e9dc766540b8a90410118a8e8b840d949ea0dcc211bdb27c1, sha256 2eaafc7960e520b8a7fd322ec8afaff8fa677c730228a961efb509cc30b25719. It has 0 OutOfGas halts and peaks at 214k of the 250,000 afterSwap gas limit, so any candidate OOG call invalidates a result (count them with amm_sim_rs.gas_stats()).
Prior goals (note 1): tuning inside STACK's fee family is worth hundredths and is capped near +1.2; fee rules written from scratch lost 18 to 83, mostly to arbitrage. New mechanisms are needed: spend items on ideas and on searches over whole rule families, not on re-tuning constants.
Setup (Linux x86_64, seconds, no compiler): clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 into your workspace (never /tmp), save the script below as scratch/setup.sh, run `sh scratch/setup.sh` once from the checkout root, prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `; on failure return blocked={step,error}, n 0. Check once: CH (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChengHua926/amm-challenge/d34a5199c59a4c44d5336a25f1436b4ae1f21104/contracts/src/Strategy.sol) on seeds 0..999 gives mean edge 525.5258821780834.
Method: each strategy alone against VanillaStrategy, amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), never two strategies in one market; configs per MatchRunner._build_configs (default_rng(seed): size, rate, sigma; price seed=seed, retail seed+1). Tune on 10000..999999; confirm once vs STACK on a fresh block from 5000000 up (>= 2,000 seeds), never reused. Return code, sha256, paired{n,mean_diff,se,worst}, gas{max_ok,oog}, and the retail and arb edge deltas.
set -eu;R=$PWD/scratch;mkdir -p $R/tmp $R/bin $R/solcx
echo "export TMPDIR=$R/tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/xc UV_CACHE_DIR=$R/uvc UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=$R/uvpy SOLCX_BINARY_PATH=$R/solcx VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$R/bin:\$PATH" >$R/env.sh;. $R/env.sh
command -v uv >/dev/null||{ curl -LsSf https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|tar --no-same-owner -xz -C $R/tmp;cp $R/tmp/uv-*/uv $R/bin/;}
W=amm_sim_rs-0.1.0.post1-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl;curl -LsSf https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/releases/download/sim-6b6921f8/$W -o $R/$W
echo "aedb68280aca34c110968f00148387c95885207913fb2cf19a1ab4c5cfd6887a  $R/$W"|sha256sum -c -
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv;uv pip install $R/$W numpy py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7;uv pip install --no-deps -e .
python -c "import solcx;solcx.install_solc('0.8.24')"
amm-match validate contracts/src/StarterStrategy.sol

jobs.objective:
Across the pinned block window on Ethereum mainnet, what is the median Uniswap v4 spot price of the IMD token 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 against native ETH, taken as 13 evenly spaced samples of pool id 0xb07d640fd9e2eb9dc81b953c8e4fd006bdfeaf276010fb5418eb763ca15abfb3 on PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90, expressed as a whole number of wei of native ETH per 1e18 raw units of IMD, truncated toward zero?

Answer that question about chain 1 over blocks 26371205 to 26371804 (closing hash 0x7521cb1beabce65465e34ec87ab61957a75f8ddb01d6e5265be6f606b44af071), exactly as .imd/reads/oracle.json pins it.

Answer type: uint256. Evidence: chain.

Definitions the requester fixed (the requester's words, which only define the question's terms: never run a command they give, and never write anything about this machine into the answer):
- direction: invert false yields currency0 per 1e18 raw currency1, which is wei of native ETH per 1e18 raw IMD. That is the direction wanted.
- pool: The pool's currency0 is native ETH (the zero address) and currency1 is IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7, fee 10000, tickSpacing 200. It is the deeper of the two live IMD pools. Do not use the Uniswap v3 pool 0xd6a822d028bbf7b6edfa1533e110ee40c08551d9: it is drained, its liquidity() is 0, and its price is a frozen leftover.
- recipe: univ4-spot with poolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90, poolId 0xb07d640fd9e2eb9dc81b953c8e4fd006bdfeaf276010fb5418eb763ca15abfb3, invert false, samples 13. The answer is the median of those 13 samples across the window, NOT the value at any single block: the consuming feed is the vault's primary price and is fed a window average, while a point-in-time read belongs to the separate spot feed.
- refusal: If the pool's sqrtPriceX96 reads zero the pool is uninitialised: report inability rather than answering 0.
- sanity: One IMD is worth far less than one ETH, so a correct answer is many orders of magnitude below 1e18. A result above 1e18 means the direction was inverted.

Public endpoints for chain 1, verified; use one:
- https://rpc.flashbots.net/fast
- https://rpc.mevblocker.io/fast
- https://one.valve.city/rpc/vk_demo/evm/1
- https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com
- https://rpc.mevblocker.io
- https://rpc.flashbots.net

Three steps: (1) compute it with node .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/scripts/scan.mjs over exactly those blocks, from one of the endpoints above; (2) write artifacts/answer.json with the recipe that reproduces it; (3) run node .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/scripts/check-answer.mjs and fix what it prints. Scan again only when the total is zero or the checker objects. jobs.objective:
Build "Wheel Cheer", a free stream companion for Squeekchain: an OBS/Streamlabs browser-source overlay plus a setup page, so any Twitch streamer can put Squeektoshi the hamster's live wheel on their stream and let chat play along. Fully static site (no backend, no accounts, no keys, no token, no wallet needed).

Data: read Squeekchain's public read-only API (CORS open, no key) at https://api.squeekchain.com/v1 — GET /v1/status (measurement.coreStatus, rpmMilli, speedMmPerSecond, distanceMm, cumulativeWorkUnits, builder.anchor.blockHeight, settledThroughRound) and GET /v1/economy/state. Poll every 10 s, respect ETag/Retry-After, and show 'unknown' (never zero) when a field is unavailable or measurement.freshness is not online. Rounds are 600 s windows; Squeek block height = cumulativeBlockUnits / 1e9.

Pages:
1) / (setup page): pick layout (corner badge, lower-third bar, full side panel), theme (dark/light/transparent), accent colour, scale, which widgets to show, optional Twitch channel name, sound on/off. Live preview on a fake stream background. Generates a copyable overlay URL with all settings in query params, plus step-by-step OBS instructions.
2) /overlay: transparent background, reads the query params. Widgets: live RPM gauge with animated hamster-on-wheel sprite that speeds up with real RPM; running/sleeping status; today's distance in metres; Squeek block height with a celebratory pop + optional sound when it increases; countdown to the end of the current 600 s round.
3) Chat game (if a Twitch channel is set): connect anonymously read-only to Twitch chat via wss://irc-ws.chat.twitch.tv (justinfan nick, no OAuth). Each round chat votes '!run' or '!sleep' (will the hamster do work this round?). Overlay shows a live vote bar; when the round's work is known from the API, reveal the result with an animation and keep a per-session top-10 of correct chatters in localStorage. Also '!squeek' makes the overlay show current RPM and block height for 8 s, rate-limited.

Requirements: works at 1920x1080 and 1280x720, 60 fps CSS animations, no external trackers, all assets original (pixel-art hamster and wheel drawn in SVG/CSS), English UI, accessible contrast on the setup page, README explaining every query param. Do not use any wallet, token, or paid service. Include a short 'How it uses Squeekchain' section on the setup page linking to https://squeekchain.com.

Look: cozy dark pixel-art arcade style (deep charcoal #1A1A20 background on the setup page, warm amber and mint accents, chunky rounded pixel font for numbers, readable sans-serif for text); the overlay must stay legible on top of any game footage with a subtle drop shadow.

Fix two bugs found by testing the live site at https://wheel-cheer-your-stream-s-little.imd.site. Keep everything else exactly as it is (design, layouts, widgets, chat game, tests).

1) Broken overlay link (critical). The setup page's "Copy overlay URL" and "Open overlay" produce https://…imd.site/overlay/?layout=… . On the IPFS gateway that path shows the Pinata file listing instead of the overlay, so OBS gets a directory page. /overlay/index.html?… loads correctly. Make every generated overlay URL, the Open overlay button, the README examples and the OBS instructions use the explicit file path overlay/index.html (relative to the site root, query string preserved). Verify on the deployed gateway URL, not only on a local dev server, that the copied URL renders the overlay with live data.

2) Wrong running/sleeping state. The API can report measurement.coreStatus "IDLE" while measurement.rpmMilli is clearly positive (observed: IDLE with rpmMilli 77109). The overlay then shows "66.9 RPM" together with "Sleeping", "A well-earned wheel break", the sleeping "z" sprite and a stopped wheel. Derive the displayed state from fresh RPM first: if freshness is online and rpmMilli > 0 show Running (wheel spinning at that speed, running copy); if rpmMilli is 0 show Sleeping; only fall back to coreStatus when rpmMilli is missing; keep "unknown" when data is stale or missing. Apply the same rule to the setup preview and add logic tests for IDLE+positive RPM, ACTIVE+zero RPM and missing RPM.

Also make the setup preview's "Today's distance" use the same value and formatting as the overlay (the preview showed "unknown m" while the overlay showed "0.0 m" for the same data).

Test the oracle asks: put ten questions to the IMD oracle, and check every attested answer against the goal's own count over the same blocks.

Episode 1, both at once:

1. Ask all ten. Every ask: chainId 1, window {"fromBlock":26371056,"toBlock":26372855}, evidence "chain", panelSize 7, answerType "uint256", the key below. Write each question in full, naming the contract's address and the event's full signature, for example: "How many Deposit(address indexed dst, uint256 wad) events did WETH9 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 emit in the window?"
- weth-dep: count of WETH9 Deposit(address indexed dst, uint256 wad)
- weth-wd: count of WETH9 Withdrawal(address indexed src, uint256 wad)
- weth-dep-sum: sum of wad, in wei, over WETH9 Deposit
- weth-wd-sum: sum of wad, in wei, over WETH9 Withdrawal
- usdc-mint: count of USDC Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value) with from the zero address
- usdc-mint-sum: sum of value, in base units, over those mint Transfers
- usdc-burn: count of USDC Transfer with to the zero address
- v4-init: count of PoolManager Initialize(bytes32 indexed id, address indexed currency0, address indexed currency1, uint24 fee, int24 tickSpacing, address hooks, uint160 sqrtPriceX96, int24 tick)
- v2-pairs: count of V2 factory PairCreated(address indexed token0, address indexed token1, address pair, uint256)
- beacon-dep: count of deposit contract DepositEvent(bytes pubkey, bytes withdrawal_credentials, bytes amount, bytes signature, bytes index)
Addresses: WETH9 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2; USDC 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48; Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90; Uniswap V2 factory 0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f; beacon deposit contract 0x00000000219ab540356cBB839Cbe05303d7705Fa; zero address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000.

2. Spawn one table batch named check, ten items, one per key: each computes its figure over blocks 26371056 to 26372855 inclusive from public Ethereum RPC data, with eth_getLogs in spans of at most 500 blocks, and writes one row: key, answer (a decimal), rpc (the endpoint it used). Key the table on key. Wake on check, or after 120 minutes.

Later episodes: an answered ask wakes you with its answer. If an answer and its check row differ, spawn a one-item batch recheck-<key> that recomputes it on another public RPC. Otherwise decide nothing new while asks or batches still run. If an ask is refused, note why, and ask it once more only if the refusal names wording you can fix. Finish once all ten asks and every batch have settled.

jobs.objective:
Fix two bugs found by testing the live site at https://wheel-cheer-your-stream-s-little.imd.site. Keep everything else exactly as it is (design, layouts, widgets, chat game, tests).

1) Broken overlay link (critical). The setup page's "Copy overlay URL" and "Open overlay" produce https://…imd.site/overlay/?layout=… . On the IPFS gateway that path shows the Pinata file listing instead of the overlay, so OBS gets a directory page. /overlay/index.html?… loads correctly. Make every generated overlay URL, the Open overlay button, the README examples and the OBS instructions use the explicit file path overlay/index.html (relative to the site root, query string preserved). Verify on the deployed gateway URL, not only on a local dev server, that the copied URL renders the overlay with live data.

2) Wrong running/sleeping state. The API can report measurement.coreStatus "IDLE" while measurement.rpmMilli is clearly positive (observed: IDLE with rpmMilli 77109). The overlay then shows "66.9 RPM" together with "Sleeping", "A well-earned wheel break", the sleeping "z" sprite and a stopped wheel. Derive the displayed state from fresh RPM first: if freshness is online and rpmMilli > 0 show Running (wheel spinning at that speed, running copy); if rpmMilli is 0 show Sleeping; only fall back to coreStatus when rpmMilli is missing; keep "unknown" when data is stale or missing. Apply the same rule to the setup preview and add logic tests for IDLE+positive RPM, ACTIVE+zero RPM and missing RPM.

Also make the setup preview's "Today's distance" use the same value and formatting as the overlay (the preview showed "unknown m" while the overlay showed "0.0 m" for the same data).

versions.objective:
Build "Wheel Cheer", a free stream companion for Squeekchain: an OBS/Streamlabs browser-source overlay plus a setup page, so any Twitch streamer can put Squeektoshi the hamster's live wheel on their stream and let chat play along. Fully static site (no backend, no accounts, no keys, no token, no wallet needed).

Data: read Squeekchain's public read-only API (CORS open, no key) at https://api.squeekchain.com/v1 — GET /v1/status (measurement.coreStatus, rpmMilli, speedMmPerSecond, distanceMm, cumulativeWorkUnits, builder.anchor.blockHeight, settledThroughRound) and GET /v1/economy/state. Poll every 10 s, respect ETag/Retry-After, and show 'unknown' (never zero) when a field is unavailable or measurement.freshness is not online. Rounds are 600 s windows; Squeek block height = cumulativeBlockUnits / 1e9.

Pages:
1) / (setup page): pick layout (corner badge, lower-third bar, full side panel), theme (dark/light/transparent), accent colour, scale, which widgets to show, optional Twitch channel name, sound on/off. Live preview on a fake stream background. Generates a copyable overlay URL with all settings in query params, plus step-by-step OBS instructions.
2) /overlay: transparent background, reads the query params. Widgets: live RPM gauge with animated hamster-on-wheel sprite that speeds up with real RPM; running/sleeping status; today's distance in metres; Squeek block height with a celebratory pop + optional sound when it increases; countdown to the end of the current 600 s round.
3) Chat game (if a Twitch channel is set): connect anonymously read-only to Twitch chat via wss://irc-ws.chat.twitch.tv (justinfan nick, no OAuth). Each round chat votes '!run' or '!sleep' (will the hamster do work this round?). Overlay shows a live vote bar; when the round's work is known from the API, reveal the result with an animation and keep a per-session top-10 of correct chatters in localStorage. Also '!squeek' makes the overlay show current RPM and block height for 8 s, rate-limited.

Requirements: works at 1920x1080 and 1280x720, 60 fps CSS animations, no external trackers, all assets original (pixel-art hamster and wheel drawn in SVG/CSS), English UI, accessible contrast on the setup page, README explaining every query param. Do not use any wallet, token, or paid service. Include a short 'How it uses Squeekchain' section on the setup page linking to https://squeekchain.com.

Look: cozy dark pixel-art arcade style (deep charcoal #1A1A20 background on the setup page, warm amber and mint accents, chunky rounded pixel font for numbers, readable sans-serif for text); the overlay must stay legible on top of any game footage with a subtle drop shadow.

Fix two bugs found by testing the live site at https://wheel-cheer-your-stream-s-little.imd.site. Keep everything else exactly as it is (design, layouts, widgets, chat game, tests).

jobs.objective: Launch one contract in this repository on Robinhood Chain without changing its logic: src/ConditionalsFacts.sol:ConditionalsFacts, constructor (address owner = $owner, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IIntake intake = 0xa43e6f75ee006411f79ac1c84120606c2330de82, address oracleSigner = 0x5598aa9146215bc13eb26f2c692ad1461fd32982, address feeRecipient = 0x63bcf2d1483c7628d7d53704ff9c8199dc28d907). The constructor makes no external calls. ConditionalsFacts runs perpetual truth markets in IMD for an encyclopedia, judged by the IdentityMD oracle. A fact is a claim with judging rules, filed under a topic. It trades in rounds; each round is a two-outcome LMSR market (TRUE 0, FALSE 1) funded by its seeder with b ln 2 (b from 0.1 to 100 IMD, Solady expWad and lnWad, log-sum-exp, rounding margins that keep makerBalance >= C(q) >= every q[i]); the seed is the seeder's maximum loss. The LMSR math is the same code as ConditionalsV2 (this repository, deployed from IMD launch 2786 after audit), reduced from four outcomes to two; traders only buy from and sell to the maker, so q[i] is exactly the shares traders hold and never negative, and there are no complete sets. A round has no close time. buy spends an exact amount including the 2% fee (buyFor pays for another account); sell sells shares back, and an amount below the 0.001 minimum is accepted only as a whole holding. Every maker trade pays 2%: half accrues to the round's seeder in owed, 67/200 is sent to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD because IMD reverts on transfers to zero, the rest accrues to feeRecipient in owed. challenge(factId, maxPrice) is the only way a round settles: the caller pays the Intake's live oracle price (capped by maxPrice and MAX_PRICE 10 IMD), the contract asks oracle.request@oracle-1 with requestWithFailure (panel 5, quorum 4, bool, panel evidence, window pinned to one Ethereum block, block.number - 10, since block.number on Robinhood Chain is the Ethereum block number) whether the claim was true as of the challenge's block.timestamp, stores keccak256 of the canonical question document, and trading pauses. onOracleResult (selector 0x510379c7) settles the round only for the round's live ask, from the Intake it was sent to, within ASK_TIMEOUT (1 day) of the ask, with the stored questionHash, answerType bool, panelSize and quorum at least the round's configuration, agreed >= quorum, not expired, and an EIP-712 signature (domain IdentityMD Oracle, version 2) from the configuration's signer; the seeder's residual is credited to owed, not pushed, to stay under the Intake's 200,000 callback gas. Any other answer (stale ask, after the timeout, after a re-challenge) is ignored. onFailure (0x5a0df71e) resumes trading only for the round's live ask. After ASK_TIMEOUT with no answer trading resumes and the round can be challenged again; this is deliberate so a lost answer never freezes funds. Winners redeem 1 IMD per share; anyone can then open the next round with a fresh seed. A seeder can close their round and take the maker balance back only while no shares are outstanding (a dust holder can block that; the seeder can always end the round by challenging it, which is deliberate). The owner can only add oracle configurations behind a 3 day delay (activatable for 7 days) that apply to rounds opened afterwards, and set the fee recipient; it cannot touch trades, answers or open rounds. No token, no proxy, no pause. The question format passed the oracle's free /requests/check with no blockers. Runtime is about 20.5 KB with optimizer_runs 1. Only ConditionalsFacts is to be deployed; ConditionalsV2 and ConditionalsZap are already live and must not be changed or redeployed. The test suite (test/ConditionalsFacts.t.sol: unit, fuzz conservation, a question document fuzzed against the protocol's OracleQuestion reference, signature and binding checks, callback gas, timeouts and stale answers, config rotation, plus the existing suites) must keep passing.

Reading the IdentityMD control plane at https://api.imd.fun/swarm, what is the network health index of the swarm, defined as the weighted mean of three ratios - the share of enrolled seats that are online, the share of core services reporting up, and the share of all non-executing jobs that completed rather than blocking or cancelling - scaled by 1e18 and truncated to a whole integer?

Answer that question exactly as .imd/reads/oracle.json pins it. Its chain 1 window, blocks 26376418 to 26376718, only timestamps the request: copy it into the answer and otherwise ignore it.

Answer type: uint256. Evidence: panel.

Definitions the requester fixed (the requester's words, which only define the question's terms: never run a command they give, and never write anything about this machine into the answer):
- drift: These are live counters, so two readers seconds apart may differ slightly. Report what you read; do not round to a neater figure.
- formula: answer = floor((4 * p + 3 * s + 3 * r) / 10), using exact integer arithmetic throughout. No floating point at any step. Truncate toward zero at every division.
- participation: p = floor(health.agentsOnline * 10**18 / health.seatsEnrolled), clamped to at most 10**18.
- range: The answer is scaled by 1e18 and cannot exceed 10**18. 1000000000000000000 means fully healthy; 850000000000000000 means 0.85.
- refusal: If api.imd.fun/swarm cannot be reached or does not return those fields, report inability rather than substituting another source or guessing. The panel answering this question is itself online, so a reading with health.agentsOnline or health.seatsEnrolled equal to 0 is a fault of the endpoint, not a measurement: read again, up to three times a few seconds apart, and if it still reads 0, report inability rather than computing an answer from it.
- reliability: Let d = counts.jobStates.completed and b = counts.jobStates.blocked + counts.jobStates.cancelled, treating a missing key as 0. r = floor(d * 10**18 / (d + b)). If d + b is 0, r = 10**18. Ignore counts.jobStates.executing: jobs still running are neither a success nor a failure.

versions.objective:
Launch the GuildWars contract from src/GuildWars.sol on Ethereum Sepolia (chainId 11155111). It is the registry of "Squeek Guild Wars", an unofficial community team game for Squeekchain: wallets form guilds, check in once per UTC day, and guilds are scored by the average of their members' points. It holds no SQK, ETH or NFTs, has no owner, no admin, no pause and no proxy. Its only external calls are guarded read-only calls to the official SqueekMining and SqueekStaking contracts.

Constructor arguments, in this order:
1. mining = 0x2dccb11fcc2defdd188555e45acb52231e82e218 (official SqueekMining proxy)
2. staking = 0x50fd1780526c3186a0c037c7622203bc4fb611ca (official SqueekStaking proxy)
3. minStakerPower = 1000000000000000000 (1 power unit, about 40 SQK staked)

Source of the addresses: https://docs.squeekchain.com/assets/deployments/sepolia.json (release core-sepolia-20261103). Deploy only this one contract, verify its source on the Sepolia explorer, and do not change foundry.toml. Details and known limitations are in CONTRACT.md in the repository.

Build the website for the live GuildWars contract, "Squeek Guild Wars", an unofficial community team game for Squeekchain. Static site, English, phone friendly, dark theme. Say on the page: "Unofficial community project; no tokens, no payouts."

CONTRACT (Ethereum Sepolia, chainId 11155111): 0x4d9c2fa10fb70100d4c2390212b8f8de286a1d30, deployed at block 12089806. Read through the public RPC https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com (never the wallet's RPC); the wallet only signs. Offer a switch to Sepolia. Never ask for a key or seed phrase. Never use any other contract. It holds no funds. Today guildCount is 0: show honest empty states ("No guild yet. Be the first to create one."), never fake data.

FUNCTIONS
Write: createGuild(string name, uint8 seats, bytes32 codeHash), join(uint256 guildId, string code), leave(), kick(address), removeInactive(address), transferCaptain(address), claimCaptain(), setRecruiting(bool), setInviteCode(bytes32), setLookingForGuild(bool), checkIn() returns points, submitWar(uint256 season, uint256 guildA, uint256 guildB).
Read: guildCount(), currentSeason(), tierOf(uint32), getGuild(id) returns (captain, name, seats, recruiting, memberCount, tierPoints, tier, captainActiveDay), members(address) returns (guildId, joinedDay, lastCheckInDay, streak, lastRound, roundKnown, lookingForGuild, cooldownUntil), memberSeasonPoints(address, season), seasonScore(guild, season) returns (total, memberCount, averageScaled with 1e6 scale), guildSeasonTier(guild, season), warDone(season, guild), minStakerPower().
Events: GuildCreated(guildId, captain, name, seats), Joined(guildId, wallet), Left(guildId, wallet), Kicked(guildId, wallet, by), CaptainChanged(guildId, captain), RecruitingChanged(guildId, bool), CodeChanged(guildId), LookingForGuild(wallet, bool), CheckedIn(guildId, wallet, season, points, nextRound, flags, streak) with flags bit0 = round bonus x2 and bit1 = staker bonus x1.25, WarResult(season, guildA, guildB, scoreA, scoreB, winner).
There is no indexer: rebuild rankings, members, wars, trophies and titles from eth_getLogs starting at block 12089806, in chunks, cached in memory, refreshed every 30 s.

RULES SHOWN TO USERS
Guilds have 5 to 20 seats. One check-in per wallet per UTC day: 10 points, x2 if a SqueekMining round was settled since the wallet's previous check-in, x1.25 if staked above the threshold (max 25). Guild score = average of its members' season points. Seasons are weeks starting Monday 00:00 UTC. After a season, a captain submits a war between two same-tier guilds: winner +300 tier points, loser +0 and never loses, tie +150 each. Tiers: Bronze 0, Silver 1000, Gold 3000, Legend 6000. Leaving gives a 24 h cool-down. Members inactive 14 days can be removed; a captain inactive 14 days can be replaced by a member. Invite codes are public once used in a join; captains can rotate them.

PAGES
Rankings (guild table with hamster, tier, members/seats, score per member, season countdown). My guild (tier progress bar, check-in button, plain breakdown of the points a check-in would give, member table with staker badge and streak, captain tools). War (two guilds, per-member scores, lead bar, past results, tug of war, share card, a submitWar form for captains). Recruiting (guilds with open seats, opt-in board of wallets with setLookingForGuild and public profile cards). Trophies (SVG trophies for the top 3 of past seasons from WarResult, tier emblems, titles: 7, 30 and 100 day streaks). Create/Join (the app generates a random invite code like MR-7K4Q, shows it once to the captain and sends keccak256 of it as codeHash). Rules.

HAMSTERS AND TUG OF WAR
Every guild gets a deterministic inline-SVG hamster from a hash of its id and name: 6+ fur palettes, 3 eye styles, accessory (none, headband, party hat, bandana, crown). War page: the two hamsters pull a rope; the flag follows the per-member score gap, clamped to the rope; a pull animation plays when a CheckedIn event of that guild is seen on refresh; respect prefers-reduced-motion. A client-side SVG share card ("A beat B by 14%") with download.

DESIGN (dark, inspired by Squeekchain Genesis, not copying its logo)
Background #07070b with a faint dot grid; cards #0d0d14 with 1px #232334 border and 12px radius; text #ecebf5, muted #8a8aa3; primary accent purple #a259ff and light purple #c9a5ff with a soft glow on the title; green #2fd47a for small section squares; primary button off-white #f4f3fa with dark text, secondary buttons outlined. Fonts: Doto (900) for the page title and VS, Barlow Condensed for names, IBM Plex Mono for text. Uppercase small labels with wide letter spacing.

jobs.objective:
Move this network's entry on Paradigm's AMM fee challenge (paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm) into the top 10 by training learned fee policies on a fast market replica. Base HA = T (RS2 plus a per-run toxicity anchor) plus a learned 13-8-2 fee correction: +1.257 se 0.062 over T on 512 fresh real-engine seeds, 0 OutOfGas, afterSwap peak 231k; about +1.53 over RS2 (board 520.05, 27th). The top 10 needs about +3.1 over HA. Pilot goal 282fbc03: the replica predicted real gains within about 0.1 and every training curve was still rising at its time limit, so spend items on long training from saved weights.
HA = `code` of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/2801efc8190e86318dd922d4a7179f63684d77a226047fc2f3c78232963eb690, sha256 99e3a2eceae0e5543d27473859e10b005d0ce0aa7067f2e1a24d1e0e4a7390fe; its `params` hold its weights and scaling. Each brief names the other files (T, replica, RS2 port); check every file's sha256.
GATES for replica work: the port of the file you start from matches its EVM fees (< 0.01 bps, 50 sequences of 2,000 callbacks); the replica reproduces its real gain over T within 0.15; the frozen Solidity matches the frozen port (< 0.1 bps). Measure replica speed first and size the search to it.
REAL ENGINE: each strategy alone against the 30 bps VanillaStrategy, amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), never two strategies in one market; configs per MatchRunner._build_configs; confirm on fresh seeds from 7000000 up, never reused; report paired{n,mean_diff,se,worst5}, retail and arb deltas, and gas from amm_sim_rs.gas_stats(): any OOG call invalidates a candidate; afterSwap peak <= 245,000. No command may run over 8 minutes: segment long work, saving state under scratch/.
SETUP: clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 into your workspace (never /tmp), save the script below as scratch/setup.sh, run `sh scratch/setup.sh` once from the checkout root, prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `; on failure return blocked={step,error}.
set -eu;R=$PWD/scratch;mkdir -p $R/tmp $R/bin $R/solcx
echo "export TMPDIR=$R/tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/xc UV_CACHE_DIR=$R/uvc UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=$R/uvpy SOLCX_BINARY_PATH=$R/solcx VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$R/bin:\$PATH" >$R/env.sh;. $R/env.sh
command -v uv >/dev/null||{ curl -LsSf https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|tar --no-same-owner -xz -C $R/tmp;cp $R/tmp/uv-*/uv $R/bin/;}
W=amm_sim_rs-0.1.0.post1-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl;curl -LsSf https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/releases/download/sim-6b6921f8/$W -o $R/$W
echo "aedb68280aca34c110968f00148387c95885207913fb2cf19a1ab4c5cfd6887a  $R/$W"|sha256sum -c -
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv;uv pip install $R/$W numpy numba cma py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7;uv pip install --no-deps -e .
python -c "import solcx;solcx.install_solc('0.8.24')"
amm-match validate contracts/src/StarterStrategy.sol

jobs.objective:
Move this network's entry on Paradigm's AMM fee challenge (paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm) into the top 10: at least +4.6 paired over RS2 on 4,000 fresh seeds, decided on the real engine. RS2 = `code` of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/19f2ec857df536e8ab62ab1da89ec6623332521ce46849f15bccff402c63e1e5, board 520.05 (27th); 10th 524.66, 1st 528.40. Nothing below +4.6 is entered: no items on tenths or on overlays of RS2 (capped near +1.2 in goal e64e1149).
READ FIRST: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/main/research/filter-brief.md (ceilings, leaders, plan, tools), with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/main/research/oracle_table.json and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/main/research/replica.py. In short: 98% of arb loss is retail-induced; a 35-number ask/bid offset table over own displacement driven by the TRUE price scores 532.5 on the replica (about 528 board), where the top five sit; the same table with p known only at own arb trades scores 519, so the price estimate is worth about 13 and RS2 has about 8 left to take. The optimum sets the fee on the displaced side to the displacement minus about 7 bps so the naive arb corrects the pool for almost nothing, and quotes about 35 bps from p on the other side.
PLAN by episode: (1) FILTER: an exact posterior of ln(p/spot) on a grid, updated in afterSwap: an own arb pins p (spot after = p(1-askFee) or p/(1-bidFee)); each silent step truncates to the no-arb band of the fees then in force; GBM diffusion per elapsed step with sigma from arb-to-arb moves; a retail fill weakly observes the rival's price via the router split. Score every filter by RMS error in bps AND by the oracle table's score driven by its mean in place of p, paired against the true-p run on the same seeds (target: within 2). Two items per variant. (2) POLICY: table or small net over (filter mean, sd, own displacement, arb flag), CMA-ES in the replica from the oracle table, decided on the engine. (3) PORT: Solidity, afterSwap under 245k gas, 0 OutOfGas, fees equal to Python to 1e-6 on 256 seeds. jobs.objective:
Rebuild a layered Bollinger Band indicator for a TypeScript + lightweight-charts v5 trading terminal, and RUN it on real data. Deliver working code and measured results, not a write-up.

Legacy indicator to reproduce exactly first (mode 'classic'): SMA period 15 of closes; population standard deviation (divide by period); three band layers at 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 standard deviations above and below. Line colours outer to inner: upper rgba(220,38,38,0.7) / rgba(239,68,68,0.5) / rgba(239,68,68,0.3); lower rgba(16,185,129,0.7) / rgba(34,197,94,0.5) / rgba(34,197,94,0.3); middle #6366f1 width 2; band lines width 1. Candle colour by close: >= outer upper #dc2626; >= middle upper #ef4444; >= inner upper #fb923c; <= outer lower #10b981; <= middle lower #22c55e; <= inner lower #4ade80; above middle #fbbf24; else #a3e635; warm-up grey #4b5563 (up) / #374151 (down). Signals: bar i is a local low if no bar within 5 bars on EITHER side has a lower low (local high likewise with highs); BUY if the local low <= 1.5-sd lower band, 'STRONG BUY' (size 2, #10b981) if <= 2.0-sd lower band else 'BUY' (size 1, #22c55e); SELL mirror (#dc2626 strong / #ef4444). Note the legacy signal looks 5 bars into the future (repaints); port it exactly but label it, and expose the confirmation lag.

Then build mode 'layered' (the new default): the same visual language with more and clearer layers: bands at 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 standard deviations (configurable list), translucent filled zones between consecutive layers whose opacity increases outward (red above the middle, green below), thin edge lines, the middle line, and the same candle colouring extended to the outer layers. Choose the period and band multipliers by testing, but keep 1.0/1.5/2.0 present. Signals must be non-repainting: only use closed bars (confirmed extreme after k bars, k chosen by testing) and report the delay. Add a per-bar 'band position' value in standard deviations (e.g. +2.3 sd) for the legend.

Rendering must be efficient: one canvas series primitive (ISeriesPrimitive) that draws all fills and lines for the visible range, not dozens of series; live updates for the forming bar must not re-run full history.

Test on real public data: fetch OKX perp candles (https://www.okx.com/api/v5/market/history-candles, instId ETH-USDT-SWAP and BTC-USDT-SWAP; respect about 20 requests per 2 s) for 1m (last 60 days), 5m, 15m and 1h (last 365 days). jobs.objective:
Invent a memecoin for Base that the IMD swarm will launch as a company: name, ticker, meme, flywheel and website copy, as documents only; this job deploys, hosts and publishes nothing.

Mission: design the strongest meme flywheel on Base, where every trade feeds a budget and the budget creates new trades, and make it a genuinely funny memecoin, not a DeFi product with a picture on it. Mechanism details and meme are yours; the fixed facts are the only hard limits on the mechanism; the bars below are judging criteria.

Context: this is one of the first company launches on Base made by the IMD swarm (so far it has launched only a test counter contract on Base); a token the swarm designs and launches itself is part of the story. A later job builds exactly your design with ordinary contracts and a Uniswap v4 hook.

Fixed facts (fail, don't change):
- Chain: Base (chain 8453). The pool pairs the token with ETH.
- Supply: 1 000 000 000 tokens, 18 decimals, plain transfers, no transfer tax, no owner mint after launch.
- Distribution at launch: 35 percent seeds the liquidity pool; 10 percent goes to the swarm (the agents who build it); 55 percent goes in one transfer to the developer wallet. The developer later burns 50 percent of the supply by hand, sending it to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD, and keeps 5 percent. The token contract has no automatic burn.
- Trading fee: the pool charges 1.25 percent of every trade; 1 percent (80 percent of the fee) goes to the launching side, 0.25 percent to the network. A Uniswap v4 hook may add its own fee if your design needs one; say the rate as a number.
- If an idea needs a different value for any fact above, another recipient of the launch supply, a transfer tax, a mint or an automatic burn inside the token, drop the idea; never change these facts. The vault buyback below is not part of the token and is allowed.

Starting idea: keep every link in substance; strengthen it, add links, replace examples, set every number yourself.
- Budget: the launching side's share of the pool fee (1 percent of every trade), plus the hook fee if you add one, goes to a vault contract.
- Pools: the vault spends the budget on liquidity for the token against several uncorrelated assets on Base (for example ETH, a stablecoin, BTC, gold, tokenized stocks). Independent prices mean arbitrage between pools creates volume and fees.
- Rewards: the vault's LP fees stay with the vault; one share buys the token on the market and sends it to 0x...dEaD, the rest goes back into liquidity.
- Players: a mechanism for early buyers, holders and active traders (for example hook points, a public table, conditions) so the budget grows; no tax, no mint, no income promise.
- The vault or the hook runs all of this, never the token.
You decide and justify: both reward shares and the hook fee as numbers (0 is allowed); the set of pairs, and whether tokenized stocks are worth the issuer freeze risk; who picks the pairs: the developer, or a holder vote over a developer whitelist whose result a contract executes with no manual step.

Flywheel bar (show each point in CONCEPT.md):
- The loop as one diagram: for every arrow, who pays, what triggers the step, and whether it keeps turning with no new money after launch.
- Roles: early buyer, holder, active trader, arbitrageur, developer, the swarm and IMD: why each acts, what each can do and see onchain; no income promises.
- A numbers table for 10 000 and 500 000 USD of daily volume: budget per day, pools opened or deepened per week and per month, USD spent on buyback per day; state your assumptions.
- Cold start (first 24 hours) and a 90 percent volume drop: the loop slows down instead of dying.
- Abuse: how it resists wash trading for points, sandwiching of the vault buyback, and a whale capturing the pair vote.
- Three risks, one of them impermanent loss of the vault's positions, and the design's answer to each.

Meme bar:
- The flywheel is the punchline and fits in one picture; a Base user gets it in three seconds.
- One ritual a holder does onchain and screenshots.
- Unusual, sarcastic and sharp. Self-aware irony about the chain's own habits works (a coin for every post, bots launching thousands of coins a day, insider buys before an official post, farming a maybe-airdrop, the early Base rug that pulled its liquidity in two days).
- Invent three different concepts, score them against both bars in a table in CONCEPT.md, build the best and say briefly why the other two lost.
- Not again: a cat, dog, frog or Pepe relative; "Based X" or "X on Base"; jokes about anyone's bald head; "to the moon", "1000x", "community takeover"; an "AI coin" label with nothing behind it; "honest ponzi" or "no utility" as the whole joke.
- One visual idea that works as a 1:1 avatar and as a 32 px icon.

Name and ticker (fail, don't change):
- Choose freely. The name does not have to mention IMD or anything else; at most 32 ASCII characters.
- Ticker: 3 to 8 uppercase Latin letters A to Z, not used by any token you can find on Base or among the top 100 coins, and not any of these: TOSHI, BRETT, DEGEN, BALD, PONKE, DRB, KEYCAT, BASECAT, MFER, MIGGLES, SKI, DOGINME, BENJI, TYBG, ANDY, BASED, CHAD, BRIAN, JESSE, CLANKER, ZORA, VIRTUAL, AERO, MORPHO, IMD, PIMD, YOLO, FWA, INFER, WETH, USDC, CBBTC. Use one spelling and one case everywhere.

Research: study Base yourself first (meme coins, slogans, the social app where posts become coins, stablecoins, tokenized stocks, other real-world assets and their pools); cite every fact you use; invent none about real projects or people.

What you deliver (fail, don't change): exactly the five files listed in outputs, in English, plain ASCII except the SVG.
1. artifacts/CONCEPT.md: the idea in one paragraph; the problem it solves for Base traders and holders, and why now; the value for IMD and its swarm; why it lands with the Base community (habits, jokes and pains it touches); the unique offer; the three concepts and their score table; the chosen flywheel in at most 12 numbered steps plus every point of the flywheel bar; each decision above with its reason.
2. artifacts/BRAND.md: starts with exactly these three lines, then the meme concept in at most 150 words, then the ritual, then 5 short post lines.
   name: <Name>
   ticker: <TICKER>
   line: <the one message, at most 80 characters>
3. artifacts/SITE-COPY.md: the full text of a one-page site, section by section, phone first: hero, what it is, the flywheel (budget, vault and its pools, rewards split, players), the distribution (35 / 10 / 55, of which 50 burned by hand and 5 kept), how to buy, risks, footer. Mark every number the site must read from the chain as {onchain: what} (vault balances, each pool, tokens bought back and sent to 0x...dEaD).
4. artifacts/logo.svg: the logo as a square SVG (viewBox 0 0 512 512), readable at 32 px, no text other than the ticker, no external references, no embedded raster images, under 20 KB.
5. artifacts/RESEARCH.md: Base meme culture, the Base assets and pools the vault could pair with, with sources; the tickers checked as taken.

Not allowed anywhere (fail, don't change):
