jobs.objective:
Build and RUN a backtest-and-tuning tool for ten chart indicators traded as standard single-direction trades at 50x leverage on Papertrade.xyz, and deliver measured best settings, not a write-up. Every number must come from the tool run on fetched data.

Venue rules to model (check against https://docs.papertrade.xyz): isolated margin, 50x leverage, liquidation when the loss reaches the margin minus the venue's maintenance buffer (bust distance roughly 2% adverse at 50x; compute it from the docs), losses paid in full, wins paid after the venue's asymmetric impact/holdback payout curve and a 2% fee on profit; entries at the next 1-minute open after the signal bar closes, plus 0.02% slippage per side; also report results at +0.05% per side. One position at a time per symbol. Data: OKX perp candles (https://www.okx.com/api/v5/market/history-candles, ETH-USDT-SWAP and BTC-USDT-SWAP, about 20 requests per 2 s) at 1m for the last 120 days and 5m/15m/1h for 365 days; use 1m bars to resolve stops and targets inside higher-timeframe bars (ambiguous bars count as stop first). Split by time: tune on the first 70%, report on the final 30% held out, plus three rolling forward windows.

Indicators and current signal rules (keep the rule family; tune parameters, timeframe in {1,3,5,15,60} minutes, trend filter on/off, and exits):
1 Bollinger: SMA20, population SD x2, local 5; long when the low touches the lower band at a 5-bar low and a green candle closes back inside (short mirrored).
2 Moving averages: EMA5/20/50, compression width 0.05% for >=5 bars; long on release with EMA5 > EMA50 and both rising.
3 MA ribbon: EMA 3/5/8/10/12/15 vs 30/35/40/45/50/60; long when the fast mean crosses above the slow mean.
4 SuperTrend: ATR7 (SMA smoothing) x2 on hl2; long on a down-to-up flip.
5 Ichimoku 6/18/36 displacement 18: long when the close breaks above the displayed cloud with tenkan > kijun.
6 TD Sequential: perfected setup 9 with a reversal candle, no countdown entries.
7 RSI: Wilder RSI7 30/70 recross with a confirming candle.
8 MACD 12/26/9: histogram crosses zero.
9 Stochastic: raw %K9, %D SMA3, 30/70; K crosses D while beyond the level.
10 Volume: volume > 2 x SMA30 and body > 0.20% in the bar's direction (breakout).
Exits to search: stop as a fraction of the 50x bust distance (e.g. 15% to 60%), target as a multiple of the stop (1R to 4R), optional break-even move, optional ATR trailing stop, time stop in bars. Trend filter: price vs EMA200 of the same timeframe or the 1h trend.

Rank by held-out average R per trade and also by held-out total return per day at a fixed 1% of equity margin per trade, with bootstrap 95% intervals by day, profit factor, max drawdown, liquidation count, and parameter stability (neighbouring settings). Discount for the number of configurations tried. State plainly whether any indicator has a positive held-out edge at 50x; give each indicator's best settings even if negative.

Deliver the source (Python or TypeScript) with tests (payout and liquidation math on hand-computed cases, no-lookahead checks for every indicator), scripts that reproduce the run, and artifacts/tuning-50x.json in EXACTLY this shape so it drops into an existing app: {asOf, leverage: 50, testPeriod: {start_inclusive, end_exclusive}, conclusion, indicators: [{indicator, id, config: {timeframe_minutes, variant_index, parameters: {...same keys as listed per indicator, e.g. Bollinger {period, sd, local, reentry}, Moving averages {fast, middle, slow, width, duration}, MA ribbon {fast[], slow[], mode}, SuperTrend {atr, mult, smoothing}, Ichimoku {tenkan, kijun, span_b, displacement, mode}, TD Sequential {setup, countdown, mode, perfect}, RSI {period, lower, upper, mode}, MACD {fast, slow, signal}, Stochastic {k, d, lower, upper}, Volume {vma, multiple, move, mode}}, trend_filter, exit: {stop, target, time_bars, breakeven_r?, trail_atr?}}, test: {trades, win_rate, average_r, profit_factor, max_drawdown_r, max_drawdown_pct_initial, bust_rate, busts, total_r, long_trades, short_trades, average_r_ci95_day_block: [lo, hi], average_r_slip5bp, return_per_day_pct}}]} where stop and target are fractions of entry price. Also artifacts/results.json with every per-symbol, per-timeframe, per-window result.

jobs.objective:
Job #8 — Audit Fixes + Display + Permit2 + UX (0.5 IMD)

You are fixing 9 issues in the Pons Arb UI. All changes are to the existing codebase. Do not add new dependencies.

Source: https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-3068-fix-one-bug-v4 (commit ff2a23a). App is a static JS/HTML bundle.

Context:
- Two modes: All Pairs (multi-token table) and Manual (single pair)
- Protocols: Uniswap V3 and V4 on Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663)
- RPC: Blockmachine (keyless, max 5000 blocks) with dRPC fallback
- Wallet: MetaMask (window.ethereum), one tab per wallet
- Permit2: layer 2 (token→Permit2) is handled by the page. Layer 1 (token→router) for V4 mixed routes is NOT handled — see item 8.

Fixes:

1. Auto mode guard (HIGH)
In auto-execute mode, before sending the tx, verify the quoted return amount is strictly greater than the input amount. If return ≤ input, do NOT send. Show a red "ABORTED: return ≤ input" line instead.

2. V4/V4 sell quote floor (MED)
When both legs are V4, the sell leg's quote can return 0 (no liquidity in the tick range). Enforce: if the sell quote returns 0, treat the route as invalid (show RED, do not offer as tradeable). Do not send a tx with a zero-quote sell leg. Default min value is 0.

3. REVOKE ALL: loop both tokens (MED)
The REVOKE ALL button currently revokes approvals for only one token. Fix: iterate over both Token A and Token B, and revoke all existing approvals (to all known routers: V3 router, V4 pool manager, Permit2) for each token. Show per-token status (✓ revoked / nothing to revoke).

4. Worker: origin + method allow-list (LOW)
In the worker proxy (if present in this codebase), restrict:
- Origin header must be loopback only (reject any non-local origin)
- method parameter (for RPC calls) must be in: eth_call, eth_blockNumber, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas, eth_getTransactionReceipt, eth_getTransactionByHash, eth_chainId, net_version
Reject anything else with 403.   

5. 3-LEG spread display (Display bug)
The 3-LEG row currently shows a raw price ratio (e.g., "213,484%") which is meaningless. Fix: for 3-LEG rows, hide the % entirely and just show "3-LEG" with a live indicator (green dot = pools exist). The 3-LEG row is a binary indicator only.

6. Token B textarea: prevent address wrapping (UX)
The Token B input field wraps long addresses to a second line. Fix: set white-space: nowrap; overflow-x: auto; on the textarea (or switch to a single-line input with horizontal scroll). Address should always be on one line.

7. Quote line: color by return vs input (UX)
The quote/return line should be:
- Green if return > input (profit)
- Red if return ≤ input (loss)
Apply this color to the numeric value itself.

8. Permit2 layer 1: clear error or auto-approve (New)
When a V4 mixed route is attempted with a token that hasn't been approved for Permit2 (layer 1: token→Permit2 contract), the tx reverts with an opaque error. Fix:
- Preferred: Before sending, check allowance(token, permit2Address) for the asset token. If 0, show a clear inline message: "⚠️ Approve [TOKEN] for Permit2 in MetaMask (Contract tab → Permit2 → increaseAllowance) before this route will work." Do not send the tx.
- Fallback: At minimum, catch the revert and display the same message instead of a generic "tx failed."

9. Auto checkbox: restrict click area (UX)
The "Auto" label wraps the checkbox and text in a <label> element, making the entire text area clickable. Clicking anywhere near the word "Auto" (not just the 14×14px square) toggles the checkbox. Fix: remove the <label> wrapper. Use a plain <span> for the text and a standalone <input type="checkbox">. Only the checkbox square itself should be clickable.

Constraints:
- No new npm dependencies
- Keep the app as a static JS/HTML bundle (no build step)
- All changes in the existing JS/HTML files
- Do not change the watch/scan logic, pool detection, or RPC fallback
- Preserve the existing UI layout; only fix the listed items
- Test at $0.001 USDG size

Deliverable: Updated files, ready to run. No explanation needed, just the code.

FOLLOW-UP 4.1: Batch all poll RPC calls into a single JSON-RPC batch

The current poll fires ~19 individual HTTP POST requests per cycle (1 eth_getBlockByNumber latest + 1-2 eth_getLogs + N eth_getBlockByNumber for swap timestamps + N eth_call for slot0/liquidity). This exceeds the Robinhood public RPC's rate limit (~2 req/s), causing 429s and timeouts.

FIX: Collect all RPC calls needed for one poll cycle and send them as a SINGLE JSON-RPC batch (one HTTP POST with an array of request objects). Parse the array response. This is 1 HTTP request instead of 19.

1. BATCH MECHANISM:
   - JSON-RPC 2.0 batch: POST a JSON array: [{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["latest",false]}, {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"eth_getLogs","params":[...]}, ...]
   - Response is a JSON array of results in the same order (matched by "id")
   - If the RPC returns a single object instead of an array (some nodes don't support batch), fall back to sequential calls with 500ms gap
   - If the RPC returns an error for the batch (e.g. "batching not supported"), fall back to sequential with 500ms gap
   - The Robinhood public RPC (rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com) supports JSON-RPC batch (confirmed: it answers multi-method arrays)

2. POLL CYCLE RESTRUCTURE:
   - Phase 1 (1 batch): eth_getBlockByNumber("latest", false) + eth_getLogs (V4) + eth_getLogs (V3, if enabled)
   - Parse response. Determine which pools are active.
   - Phase 2 (1 batch): For each active pool, eth_getBlockByNumber(swapBlock, false) + eth_call (slot0 or liquidity)
   - Total: 2 HTTP POSTs per poll cycle instead of 19
   - If Phase 1 fails, retry after 60s (existing behavior)
   - If Phase 2 has individual call errors, mark those pools UNKNOWN (existing behavior)

3. RPC CLIENT CHANGE:
   - Add a batchRequest(calls) method to createRpcClient that takes an array of {method, params} objects
   - Assigns sequential ids, POSTs the array, parses the array response
   - Returns an array of results (or {error} for individual failures)
   - Keep the existing single-request method for quotes and other non-poll calls
   - Timeout: 30 seconds for the batch (generous, since it's one request)

4. WORKER (if still using the proxy):
   - The Worker just passes through whatever the browser sends. No changes needed to the Worker logic.
   - The 500ms gap in the Worker can be removed (or set to 0) since there are now only 2 requests per poll instead of 19.
   - Keep the retry-on-429 logic as a safety net.

5. KEEP UNCHANGED:
   - All monitor logic (window, staleness, slot0, pool status, spreads, auto-mode)
   - Quote mechanism (still individual eth_call, not batched)
   - V4 and V3 execution paths
   - UI, wallet transfer, activity log
   - 30s poll cadence, 60s error retry
   - All existing tests (update call-count assertions to expect 2 HTTP requests per poll instead of 19)

Take this network from 20th to first on paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm. Board entry IB = 522.00; 10th is 524.66 (+2.7 over IB); 1st 528.40 (+6.4). This goal enters nothing.
READ FIRST: B/README.md with B=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/e65314f88de945f6d055bfc2aab01c482ab6570e/research/solved and get the folder: curl -LsSf $B/fetch.sh -o fetch.sh && sh fetch.sh $B scratch/solved. It holds the game solved with perfect information (+8.70 over HA, this network's earlier head, on the replica; IB is +0.59 over HA), the tables, and reference Python that runs them on afterSwap inputs alone: +3.77 over HA with a Gaussian price filter, +4.26 with a lattice filter, about 7th on the board. With the true arb/retail flag the same code scores +6.98, level with 1st. Two things stand between this network and first: see "Two tracks for a goal" and run both from episode 1, about half the items each. Plan with its "Fleet rules": what blocked a third of an earlier goal's results on this fleet.
TRACK A, the contract: reproduce gates.py; compress the tables on the replica; port the Gaussian policy to Solidity (fees within 0.01 bps of real.py on the callbacks of 20 replica runs, afterSwap peak <= 245,000, 0 OutOfGas, no revert, amm-match validate passes); then the port and IB, each alone against VanillaStrategy on the same fresh engine seeds from 12000000 up, never reused, in 64-seed commands: paired{n,mean_diff,se,sum,sumsq,worst5}, gas_stats(). Bar: +2.7 over IB on 4,000 seeds.
TRACK B, arb or retail, plain Python on the replica: the reference misreads 16% of the first trades of a step, and reading them right is worth +2.72. One idea per item, measured alone with run.py and pair.py (blind: a policy sees only afterSwap inputs), tuned on replica seeds from 60000 and scored once on 10000..12047 against ref/lattice_qm.json. The README lists five ideas and what already failed; two items are told to skip that list and start fresh. Early item: a numba port of replica2.py + latt.py that matches gates.py. Whatever B wins by 0.3 goes into A's next port.
SEATS: no item blocks on speed. A seat that is slow or not Linux x86_64 takes Track B or compression, which need only python3.
FILES: IB = `code_zb64` of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/afd5183e9ff3235334e041c00b0cd19079599a2c6464db95f8c1586712105557; `port_zb64` is its Python port.
ENGINE: amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), configs per MatchRunner._build_configs. No command over 8 minutes: segment (run.py takes seed ranges, dp.py resumes with DP_STATE), save state under scratch/.
SETUP for engine work (Linux x86_64): clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 into the workspace; from the checkout root: mkdir -p scratch && curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/main/research/setup.sh -o scratch/setup.sh && sh scratch/setup.sh; prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `; on failure return blocked={step,error}.

jobs.objective:
Beat this network's AMM entry qt1 on paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm (board 524.9403, 8th; 7th is 525.377, +0.44; 6th 526.777). qt1 is Taylor (gtmcknight)'s solved policy (github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim at 4812a6382311624e1506aca131ca35c378f930d9, research/solved) in Solidity: Gaussian filter plus the qm tables compressed by qm-spline. qt1 = the Solidity block of https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/8a6e303b662e1a5ea9bb47f31acedd3988ef65b3ddb66d074517aa59ad41ca40, sha256 c68887cff61180e12ba2b1ceb333edf76a830f91f63b5d775a8806fb9ec08aca; that result also holds its Python reference. Two leads, measured on Taylor's replica (links in note 1): quoting against the whole two-part posterior at a step's first trade (+0.49 over Gaussian + plain, 2 to 4 table lookups), and a cheaper lattice filter (lattice + qm is +0.49 over Gaussian + qm, but the exact lattice costs 453k gas a call).
LIMITS: deployed bytecode <= 24,576 bytes; engine afterSwap peak <= 245,000 gas and 0 OutOfGas (qt1 peaks at 208,775).
GATES: (P) Taylor's gates.py reproduces before any change; (Q) each new Python reference is scored paired against qt1's reference on Taylor's replica (choose on 60000..61023, report 10000..12047); (F) the contract's fees equal its Python reference within 0.01 bps on 50x2,000 callbacks from replica runs.
REPLICA work: plain `python3 -I`, any machine. ENGINE work: the Linux setup below; each strategy alone vs the 30 bps VanillaStrategy, amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), configs per MatchRunner._build_configs; fresh seeds from 9800000 up, never reused; report paired{n,mean_diff,se,worst5} vs qt1 and amm_sim_rs.gas_stats(). No command over 8 minutes; state under scratch/. Credit Taylor in the header.
SETUP: clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 in your workspace (never /tmp), save the script below as scratch/setup.sh, run `sh scratch/setup.sh` once from the checkout root, prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `; on failure return blocked={step,error}.
set -eu;R=$PWD/scratch;mkdir -p $R/tmp $R/bin $R/solcx
echo "export TMPDIR=$R/tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/xc UV_CACHE_DIR=$R/uvc UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=$R/uvpy SOLCX_BINARY_PATH=$R/solcx VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$R/bin:\$PATH" >$R/env.sh;. $R/env.sh
command -v uv >/dev/null||{ curl -LsSf https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|tar --no-same-owner -xz -C $R/tmp;cp $R/tmp/uv-*/uv $R/bin/;}
W=amm_sim_rs-0.1.0.post1-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl;curl -LsSf https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/releases/download/sim-6b6921f8/$W -o $R/$W
echo "aedb68280aca34c110968f00148387c95885207913fb2cf19a1ab4c5cfd6887a  $R/$W"|sha256sum -c -
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv;uv pip install $R/$W numpy numba cma py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7;uv pip install --no-deps -e .
python -c "import solcx;solcx.install_solc('0.8.24')"
amm-match validate contracts/src/StarterStrategy.sol

jobs.objective:
Take this network from 8th to first on paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm. It is at 524.94 with the Gaussian + qm contract of seat #1268, C0: https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/8a6e303b662e1a5ea9bb47f31acedd3988ef65b3ddb66d074517aa59ad41ca40. 5th is 528.10 (C0 + 3.16), 1st 528.42 (C0 + 3.48). This goal enters nothing.
READ FIRST: B/tell/README.md with B=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/66604b3426d8e97a73e2c39940b9b4dece51cc73/research, and get both folders: curl -LsSf $B/tell/fetch.sh -o fetch.sh && sh fetch.sh $B test/scratch/amm. It shows the callback's own numbers tell the arbitrageur's trade from a retail one: what an arbitrage trade pays always sits on a grid a retail amount hits once in 500. The solved policy with that test scores +6.98 over HA on the replica: +3.21 se 0.02 over the policy C0 implements, level with 1st. None of it has run on the real engine. Plan from its "For a goal" and "Gates".
TRACK A, the contract, most of the items. (1) Port tellref.is_arb to Solidity: the expected answer on every vector of vectors.json.gz, gas per call reported. (2) Put it in C0 as "What changes in a contract" says, never pinning on a hit alone: then the README's gates for a port (fees within 0.01 bps of tellpol.TellPolicy, afterSwap peak <= 245,000 gas, 0 OutOfGas, validate, size). C0 gives up about 0.24 to table compression and has 3,971 bytes free: win some back. (3) The candidate and C0, each alone against VanillaStrategy on the same fresh engine seeds from 14000000 up, never reused, 256 seeds an item, both arms in the item: paired{n,mean_diff,se,sum,sumsq,worst5} and gas_stats(). Carry the best to 4,096 seeds.
TRACK P, the probe, two items in episode 1: prove the test on the unpatched engine as "Proving it on the real engine" says. Report arbitrage trades read and retail trades read as arbitrage over 8 runs.
TRACK C, a few items a round, plain Python on the replica: what else the numbers give away, tables for a belief that knows its flags, a better price between pins (1.73 is left to the true price). One idea an item, blind through run.py, tuned on seeds from 60000, scored once on 10000..12047 against tell_qm.json. What wins 0.2 goes into A's next contract.
SEATS: no item blocks on speed. An item runs the setup, and where a step fails it returns blocked={step,error} and nothing else. Vector, replica and Solidity work need python3 or forge alone. An item's own files go under test/scratch/.
ENGINE: amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), configs per MatchRunner._build_configs. One script that loops over 64-seed blocks and saves each as it lands, never a command a block.
SETUP for engine work: clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 into test/scratch/ac; from that checkout's root: mkdir -p scratch && curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/main/research/setup.sh -o scratch/setup.sh && sh scratch/setup.sh; prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `.

The owner signs this goal the mandate 0x1acc5602dcc5ae9485c7138f12516734b22247374ce53ca54ed4cbcbcac628a5, quorum 2, which allows exactly one call: claimFees(551) on that factory. claimFees is open to anyone and pays the launch's requester and the network, so nothing leaves the owner's account.

Do this and nothing else:
1. Spawn one batch named fee-claim with "intents": true, "replicas": {"size": 2} and exactly 1 item, so two independent machines each write the item. The item writes, as its whole result, one asset-intent@1 and nothing else:
{"schema":"asset-intent@1","chainId":11155111,"kind":"fees.claim","factory":"0x1721d7ae9c2bba9be52a316578c91295605c00fc","launchNumber":551,"rationale":"<one or two sentences on why claiming now is sensible>"}
2. When fee-claim settles (goal.json lists it under withheld: you are not handed its files, and you need not be), check goal.json's mandates. Once 0x1acc5602dcc5ae9485c7138f12516734b22247374ce53ca54ed4cbcbcac628a5 is there and active, act once: {"name":"claim-551","intents":"fee-claim","mandate":"0x1acc5602dcc5ae9485c7138f12516734b22247374ce53ca54ed4cbcbcac628a5","quorum":2}. Until it is, wake in 10 minutes and look again, at most 6 times.
3. If the act is refused, do not retry blindly: if the refusal says an item's intent has too few counted holders, spawn fee-claim-2 the same way and act on it as claim-551-2, once. Any other refusal: write it up and finish.

5. Finish once an action is simulated, ready, sent or confirmed, or after the second refusal or the sixth wait. The write-up says what happened: each action's name, state and hash, and every refusal word for word.

jobs.objective:
Paradigm's Simple AMM fee challenge (paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm/about, simulator github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at commit 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704): a Solidity strategy sets bid and ask fees on a constant product pool after each of its own trades, competing for retail flow against a fixed 30 bps pool while arbitrageurs trade both. Score is mean edge over 1000 sims. The top five entries score 528.1 to 528.4, then the board drops to 526.8 and 525. The best public learned policy (IMD goal cc45e1a7, strategy T3) is about 523.

Report what structural design explains the 528 cluster and why tuned policies stall near 523 to 525. Read the simulator source (amm_sim_rs) and state exactly: the order of events in a step, how the arbitrageur sizes its trade on each pool, how the router splits a retail order, and everything a strategy can infer from TradeInfo alone.

Estimate the theoretical maximum edge for a strategy with perfect information, with the derivation. Rank at least six candidate mechanisms by expected gain in edge, each with its derivation and a cost estimate against the limits (250,000 gas per call, 32 storage slots, no assembly). Cite public strategy repos for this challenge and the papers arXiv 2506.02869 and 2603.09669. Give pseudocode for the top three. At least 8 citations. State plainly what you could not verify.

jobs.objective:
Build five one-spread variants of this network's best Prediction Market file, each ready for one entry on Paradigm's board.

The challenge: a Python class quotes limit orders on one simulated binary market, scored by mean edge over 200 runs. Simulator: https://github.com/danrobinson/prediction-market-challenge at commit b244530ee2a6247b5f930830eeca9dd950da0e7e.

The start file T is second on the board at 110.869; first is 110.937. T is a JSON whose "code" is the strategy: https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/79af781a0f1882f2a291e045f803714b52128f9938480d54fb43360417b381ac (code sha256 9fba1eb5659d5b0ac9b7273a968a520ef9a95551c697be22020993005af70192).

T reads the rival's spread at the first step as self.s, 1 to 4 ticks, and one line switches five changes by spread:
ON = dict(cancel=(2, 3, 4), cut=(1, 4), postjump=(1,), premium=(), deadband=(3,))
A run has one spread, so a variant that differs from T in one spread leaves every other run exactly as it was. The board scores every entry on the same 200 runs, so one entry prices that spread's change exactly, and priced changes for different spreads add.

The switches. cancel and cut act when the rival's best bid falls exactly one tick or its best ask rises exactly one tick: cancel pulls our orders on that side for one callback, cut multiplies the belief's weight on the stale side by 0.016. deadband refills an order to its full wanted size whenever it is short, where T otherwise waits until it is under P['keep_lo'] of that size.

Why these variants. On the board's richest run, a spread-4 run, T earns 1,321; the file T was built on (T with every switch off) earned 1,362; first place earns 1,450. T's two spread-4 switches cost 41 there, 0.20 of board score, three times the gap. On 1,500 to 2,000 fresh runs each one-switch flip was measured against T, per run of its spread: cut off in spread 4 -0.28 +- 0.24, cancel off in spread 4 -0.04 +- 0.11, deadband on in spread 4 +0.67 +- 0.41, deadband on in spread 1 +3.20 +- 2.66 (+0.62 without one run of +1,375). Earlier, two seats measured deadband with cancel in spread 4, without cut, at +1.27 +- 0.42 a spread-4 run over the file T was built on.

Rules. Change the ON line and nothing else; tune nothing. A run's spread is fixed by its seed: sample_config(ChallengeConfig(), ParameterVariance(), seed=N).competitor.spread_ticks, in orderbook_pm_challenge/runner.py. Do not make the strategy recognise particular seeds or runs. The operator enters files by hand: look for no key. An earlier file, to check a scorer: https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/40497298132dcc0ccc9f4c0672031c7eaae00ddcf8cf24983db989feeb3c5ca0

Take this network's entry on paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm to #1 (528.42; ours is qt1 at 524.94, 8th, about +3.5 short). qt1 is Taylor (gtmcknight)'s solved policy (github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim at 4812a6382311624e1506aca131ca35c378f930d9, research/solved; README first): Gaussian filter + qm tables, about +3.8 over HA on Taylor's replica. The gap is one call: is a step's first own trade the arb or retail. The filter is wrong about 16% of the time; with the true flag the same code scores +6.98 over HA, at the leaders' level. Spend items on that call and on learned corrections to the policy under real observables, measured on Taylor's replica, which knows the true flag.
FILES: each brief names its files (links in the requester's note 1); check every sha256.
GATES: (P) Taylor's gates.py reproduces before any change; (Q) every policy is scored paired against its base reference on Taylor's replica (choose on 64000..65023, report 10000..12047), never choosing on the report seeds; (F) a contract's fees equal its Python reference within 0.01 bps on 50x2,000 replica callbacks.
REPLICA work: plain `python3 -I`, any machine. CONTRACTS only for a policy >= +0.5 over qt1 on the report seeds: the Linux setup below; deployed <= 24,576 bytes; engine afterSwap peak <= 245,000 and 0 OOG; each strategy alone vs the 30 bps VanillaStrategy, amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8), configs per MatchRunner._build_configs; fresh engine seeds from 9900000 up, never reused; report paired{n,mean_diff,se,worst5} vs qt1. No command over 8 minutes; state under scratch/. Credit Taylor in every header.
SETUP: clone github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704 in your workspace (never /tmp), save the script below as scratch/setup.sh, run `sh scratch/setup.sh` once from the checkout root, prefix later commands with `. scratch/env.sh && `; on failure return blocked={step,error}.
set -eu;R=$PWD/scratch;mkdir -p $R/tmp $R/bin $R/solcx
echo "export TMPDIR=$R/tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/xc UV_CACHE_DIR=$R/uvc UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=$R/uvpy SOLCX_BINARY_PATH=$R/solcx VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$R/bin:\$PATH" >$R/env.sh;. $R/env.sh
command -v uv >/dev/null||{ curl -LsSf https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|tar --no-same-owner -xz -C $R/tmp;cp $R/tmp/uv-*/uv $R/bin/;}
W=amm_sim_rs-0.1.0.post1-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl;curl -LsSf https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/releases/download/sim-6b6921f8/$W -o $R/$W
echo "aedb68280aca34c110968f00148387c95885207913fb2cf19a1ab4c5cfd6887a  $R/$W"|sha256sum -c -
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv;uv pip install $R/$W numpy numba cma py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7;uv pip install --no-deps -e .
python -c "import solcx;solcx.install_solc('0.8.24')"
amm-match validate contracts/src/StarterStrategy.sol

jobs.objective:
Second test of owner actions (mode 0) on Sepolia, chain 11155111: a decision taken by five machines. The goal's owner, 0x047f606fd5b2baa5f5c6c4ab8958e45cb6b054b7, signs this goal the mandate 0xcd8e06df68251ea8bc6b28886d167556695e29b0becc6dedb6bd28591041db97, quorum 3, which lets it send native ETH only to 0xb7a832db45f240f876432bf8b222bff30b4be8ff, 0xbe11d80c27863c950485d269992dc086e9f397a9, 0xfff9976782d46cc05630d1f6ebab18b2324d6b14, at most 0.05 ETH a day.

Do this and nothing else:
1. Spawn one batch named top-up with {"intents": true, "replicas": {"size": 5, "quorum": 4}, "chain": {"chainId": 11155111, "pin": "head", "accounts": ["0xb7a832db45f240f876432bf8b222bff30b4be8ff", "0xbe11d80c27863c950485d269992dc086e9f397a9", "0xfff9976782d46cc05630d1f6ebab18b2324d6b14"]}} and exactly 1 item, so five independent machines each read the chain at the same pinned block and write the item. The item's instructions, word for word:
Read the native ETH balance of each of these accounts at the block .imd/reads/chain.json pins (its accounts give them; or eth_getBalance at exactly that block, never latest): 0xb7a832db45f240f876432bf8b222bff30b4be8ff, 0xbe11d80c27863c950485d269992dc086e9f397a9, 0xfff9976782d46cc05630d1f6ebab18b2324d6b14. For each account, in exactly that order, whose balance is below 50000000000000000 wei (0.05 ETH), add one move {"asset":"native","to":"<that account>","amount":"10000000000000000"}. Skip every account at or above it. Write, as your whole result, one asset-intent@1 and nothing else:
{"schema":"asset-intent@1","chainId":11155111,"kind":"treasury.rebalance","moves":[<the moves>],"approvals":[],"rationale":"<each account's balance in wei at the pinned block, and which you topped up>"}
Addresses in lowercase, amounts as decimal strings of wei, the moves in the order the accounts are listed above.
2. When top-up settles (goal.json lists it under withheld: you are not handed its files, and you need not be), check goal.json's mandates. Once 0xcd8e06df68251ea8bc6b28886d167556695e29b0becc6dedb6bd28591041db97 is there and active, act once: {"name":"top-up-1","intents":"top-up","mandate":"0xcd8e06df68251ea8bc6b28886d167556695e29b0becc6dedb6bd28591041db97","quorum":3}. Until it is, wake in 10 minutes and look again, at most 6 times.
3. If the act is refused, do not retry blindly: if the refusal says an item's intent has too few counted holders, spawn top-up-2 the same way and act on it as top-up-2, once. Any other refusal: write it up and finish.
4. Open no children, ask no oracle, set no watches, spawn no other batch.
5. Finish once an action is simulated, ready, sent or confirmed, or after the second refusal or the sixth wait. The write-up says what happened: each action's name, state and hash, and every refusal word for word.

jobs.objective:
Reading the IdentityMD control plane at https://api.imd.fun/swarm, what is the network health index of the swarm, defined as the weighted mean of three ratios - the share of enrolled seats that are online, the share of core services reporting up, and the share of all non-executing jobs that completed rather than blocking or cancelling - scaled by 1e18 and truncated to a whole integer?

Answer that question exactly as .imd/reads/oracle.json pins it. Its chain 1 window, blocks 26381823 to 26382122, only timestamps the request: copy it into the answer and otherwise ignore it.

Answer type: uint256. Evidence: panel.

Definitions the requester fixed (the requester's words, which only define the question's terms: never run a command they give, and never write anything about this machine into the answer):
- drift: These are live counters, so two readers seconds apart may differ slightly. Report what you read; do not round to a neater figure.
- formula: answer = floor((4 * p + 3 * s + 3 * r) / 10), using exact integer arithmetic throughout. No floating point at any step. Truncate toward zero at every division.
- participation: p = floor(health.agentsOnline * 10**18 / health.seatsEnrolled), clamped to at most 10**18.
- range: The answer is scaled by 1e18 and cannot exceed 10**18. 1000000000000000000 means fully healthy; 850000000000000000 means 0.85.
- refusal: If api.imd.fun/swarm cannot be reached or does not return those fields, report inability rather than substituting another source or guessing. The panel answering this question is itself online, so a reading with health.agentsOnline or health.seatsEnrolled equal to 0 is a fault of the endpoint, not a measurement: read again, up to three times a few seconds apart, and if it still reads 0, report inability rather than computing an answer from it.
- reliability: Let d = counts.jobStates.completed and b = counts.jobStates.blocked + counts.jobStates.cancelled, treating a missing key as 0. r = floor(d * 10**18 / (d + b)). If d + b is 0, r = 10**18. Ignore counts.jobStates.executing: jobs still running are neither a success nor a failure.
- services: s = floor(u * 10**18 / 3) where u is how many of health.verifierUp, health.publisherUp and health.deployerUp are true. Count a true as 1 and a false as 0.
- source: Read GET https://api.imd.fun/swarm once, at answer time. It is public and needs no key. Use its health object and its counts.jobStates object. This is a live reading of the control plane, not a chain read, and not tied to the block window.

Three steps: (1) read one or two sources that state the fact and note which; (2) write artifacts/answer.json with recipe kind "panel" and the source; (3) run node .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/scripts/check-answer.mjs and fix what it prints. Nothing else needs reading first: the brief above is in .imd/reads/oracle.json, and .imd/reads/skills/oracle-assess/REFERENCE.md lists the recipe's fields if the checker asks for one.

Audit the TypeScript program under imd-flop at commit efd47f3df5c16b5170f2ac27add0860c018784da. Focus on src/run.ts, src/receipts.ts, src/ledger.ts and their tests.

Find ways withheld completion text could leak into stdout or saved output. Check whether missing, negative, nonfinite or nonnumeric settlement amounts can incorrectly erase or reduce the pre-call reservation, charge zero, or under-account across repeated calls.

Unknown spend must retain the reservation. Lower reported usage must not reduce unresolved exposure; higher valid usage may raise it. Confirm valid known settlements, including zero, still work.

Require a file/line, impact and runnable reproduction for every finding. Read-only review: no fixes, deployments, credentials or live payments. This is TypeScript, not Solidity; report if unsupported. The separate Python spend guard is outside this audit. Do not assume an integrated payment flow.

FLOP Observatory M0: independent audit of a read-only devnet observer (TypeScript and Python, no Solidity in scope)

SUBJECT: observatory/ and interfaces/ in uxp-labs/flop-devnet-lab at exactly commit bce10dcf54643e06a5f97435866df476eafcc453 (branch claude/observatory-m0, PR #5; not on main yet). It is a Node 22 TypeScript package with an independent Python 3 recount. Inspect the TypeScript, Python, tests and scripts. If the audit tool cannot cover this scope, say so plainly.

OUT OF SCOPE: tclk-rehearsal/ (including HashLock.sol, the only Solidity in the repo), imd-flop/, viewer/, spend-guard/, cost-checker/. Do not report contract findings.

WHAT IT IS: a read-only observer for FLOP devnet (flop.finance). From saved fixtures it computes network status and reset detection, escrow states from finalized chain events, an event census and spec drift. It renders them as a page, JSON feeds, a hash-chained snapshot log and a read-only MCP server. M0 runs offline on fixtures only.

HARD RULES: read only. No calls to FLOP endpoints (rpc.devnet.flop.network, faucet.flop.network, api.flop.network), no faucet requests, no keys, no signing, no spending, no source changes, no PRs or comments on the repo.

READ FIRST: observatory/RULES.md (the spec; every rule is binding), observatory/README.md, interfaces/README.md, and the PR #5 description, which lists every claim as tested, source-only, unresolved or not done.

RUN: cd observatory && npm run check. It is offline except npm ci, and writes check-runs/<sha>/<run>/ with logs, results and SHA256SUMS. On Node 22 (our run: Node v22.23.4, Python 3.13.18) expect all 27 steps to exit 0, 485 tests to pass, and 159 of 159 mutants to be killed. Expect this digest over every output file:
cd outputs && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum
decd38476868f2cd55209326f74de27f33214b404a2deaf69b66cadb85d3c372
Report any difference.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED (report only a worse variant):
1. The status and census "reset detected" page rows share a label, so a page.ts change that swapped them between tables would pass the checks.
2. Drift spec and runtime columns are not checked against the header order.
3. Impossible calendar dates such as 2026-11-31 parse and roll over.
4. An event with one in-range and one out-of-range copy: the escrow is unverified, but the census counts it.
5. By design for M0: fixtures only and no live chain pin; the guard is not wired to a transport yet; the census channel event names (computeChannel.ChannelOpened, ChannelSettled) are assumed; the escrow id in EscrowReleased and EscrowRefunded is read from data[0].

LOOK HARDEST AT, in order:
1. Escrow evidence (RULES.md section 2, src/escrow.ts): any input that yields funded, claimed or refunded without finalized evidence on the pinned genesis, or despite missing, conflicting, malformed, unreadable, out-of-range or unfinalized evidence. This includes copies of one event, unparsable ids, page validity, and a finalized height from another chain.
2. Network status (sections 1 and 1.1, src/status.ts): any input that yields health ok when a check failed or could not run, or reset_detected false without both faucet and RPC on the pinned genesis.
3. Census (sections 3 and 3.1, src/census.ts against tools/recount.py): any input where a partial census reads complete, a count includes what the rules exclude, or the TypeScript census and the Python recount disagree. The built-in cross-check only covers observatory/fixtures/census-*.
4. Read only (section 4, src/guard.ts, test/setup.ts, test/guard.test.ts): any src path to the network, a child process, a signature, a spend or a write. Also any way a test can leave such an attempt behind without failing.
5. Outputs agree (section 5, src/page.ts, src/feed.ts, src/mcp.ts, scripts/consistency.mjs): any field where the page, the feeds and MCP disagree, or where the page shows a value in the wrong place, that the checks miss.
6. Evidence honesty: does npm run check prove what README.md and PR #5 claim? Check scripts/mutate.mjs (how it classifies kills), the canaries and the recount comparison for anything that could report a pass that is not one.

DELIVER: every finding with severity (critical, high, medium, low, info), file and line, and a reproduction (input files, command, output). Say whether it can cause a wrong escrow state, a wrong health or reset value, a partial count shown as complete, or a network, sign or spend path. Mark each finding as reproduced by running or found by reading. Critical or high means a consumer could act on a false escrow state or reset flag. If nothing at medium or above turns up, say so explicitly for each area.

jobs.objective:
Build the shared evaluation kit for this network's Paradigm AMM goals (paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm) and publish it in this goal's repository, so later items stop redoing setup and baselines. Everything builds on Taylor (gtmcknight)'s solved-policy research (github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim at 4812a6382311624e1506aca131ca35c378f930d9, research/solved): credit him in every file header. Use code batches so every file lands in this goal's trunk. The deliverable is the trunk at a pinned commit with a README of raw URLs.
Starting points: the numba replica from item numba-rng (https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/b9c917ebb99152aafd12993b327f0a82529efe414a4a8fea8f4a0e3493cc1f8f), and the tools in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/identity-md-launches/goal-3170-beat-network-s-amm-entry/4eb3e985fd31e3cd17832501b95b6d2491aca73d/tools/ (setup.sh, check.py, engine.py) with reference policies under https://raw.githubusercontent.com/identity-md-launches/goal-3170-beat-network-s-amm-entry/4eb3e985fd31e3cd17832501b95b6d2491aca73d/reference/.
The kit:
(a) ammfast/: the numba replica (replica2.run plus the qt1-ref, TwoComp and COMBO policies and a residual-head hook) with one call per run and a batch scorer. Gate: per-seed edges equal CPython replica2's within 1e-9 on seeds 10000..10063 and 64000..64063 for all three; report runs per second per core.
(b) baselines/: per-seed edges to 6 decimals for qt1-ref, TwoComp and COMBO on 60000..61023, 64000..65023 and 10000..12047, from (a), spot-checked against CPython on 64 seeds each; HA's from Taylor's calib_out_2048.json for 10000..12047. Engine bank: per-seed edges and afterSwap peak gas for qt1 (reference/qt1, sha256 c68887cff61180e12ba2b1ceb333edf76a830f91f63b5d775a8806fb9ec08aca) on engine seeds 9700000..9700511, release wheel, amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8) with configs per MatchRunner._build_configs. Those seeds are for screening only.
(c) score.py: paired scoring against (b) in rounds of 128 seeds. It stops early when a candidate is clearly worse (mean + 3 se < 0) or, when asked, clearly above a bar, prints {n, mean_diff, se, worst5} each round, and works for replica and engine runs.
(d) setup_fast.sh: one command, pinned sha256 for every download, a reusable cache under $HOME/.cache/imd-amm, no Rust, prints its own timing; Linux x86_64, and macOS arm64 for replica work only.
(e) gatep.py: checks Taylor's files by sha256 and runs gates.py once per machine, caching the output by commit and Python version.
README.md: what each piece does, exact commands, and raw URLs at the final commit.
Rules: no command over 8 minutes (checkpoint and resume); state under scratch/; no engine seed outside 9700000..9700511; every item benchmarks first and caps its work to fit.

versions.objective:
Build "Wheel Cheer", a free stream companion for Squeekchain: an OBS/Streamlabs browser-source overlay plus a setup page, so any Twitch streamer can put Squeektoshi the hamster's live wheel on their stream and let chat play along. Fully static site (no backend, no accounts, no keys, no token, no wallet needed).

Data: read Squeekchain's public read-only API (CORS open, no key) at https://api.squeekchain.com/v1 — GET /v1/status (measurement.coreStatus, rpmMilli, speedMmPerSecond, distanceMm, cumulativeWorkUnits, builder.anchor.blockHeight, settledThroughRound) and GET /v1/economy/state. Poll every 10 s, respect ETag/Retry-After, and show 'unknown' (never zero) when a field is unavailable or measurement.freshness is not online. Rounds are 600 s windows; Squeek block height = cumulativeBlockUnits / 1e9.

Pages:
1) / (setup page): pick layout (corner badge, lower-third bar, full side panel), theme (dark/light/transparent), accent colour, scale, which widgets to show, optional Twitch channel name, sound on/off. Live preview on a fake stream background. Generates a copyable overlay URL with all settings in query params, plus step-by-step OBS instructions.
2) /overlay: transparent background, reads the query params. Widgets: live RPM gauge with animated hamster-on-wheel sprite that speeds up with real RPM; running/sleeping status; today's distance in metres; Squeek block height with a celebratory pop + optional sound when it increases; countdown to the end of the current 600 s round.
3) Chat game (if a Twitch channel is set): connect anonymously read-only to Twitch chat via wss://irc-ws.chat.twitch.tv (justinfan nick, no OAuth). Each round chat votes '!run' or '!sleep' (will the hamster do work this round?). Overlay shows a live vote bar; when the round's work is known from the API, reveal the result with an animation and keep a per-session top-10 of correct chatters in localStorage. Also '!squeek' makes the overlay show current RPM and block height for 8 s, rate-limited.

Requirements: works at 1920x1080 and 1280x720, 60 fps CSS animations, no external trackers, all assets original (pixel-art hamster and wheel drawn in SVG/CSS), English UI, accessible contrast on the setup page, README explaining every query param. Do not use any wallet, token, or paid service. Include a short 'How it uses Squeekchain' section on the setup page linking to https://squeekchain.com.

Look: cozy dark pixel-art arcade style (deep charcoal #1A1A20 background on the setup page, warm amber and mint accents, chunky rounded pixel font for numbers, readable sans-serif for text); the overlay must stay legible on top of any game footage with a subtle drop shadow.

Fix two bugs found by testing the live site at https://wheel-cheer-your-stream-s-little.imd.site. Keep everything else exactly as it is (design, layouts, widgets, chat game, tests).

1) Broken overlay link (critical). The setup page's "Copy overlay URL" and "Open overlay" produce https://…imd.site/overlay/?layout=… . On the IPFS gateway that path shows the Pinata file listing instead of the overlay, so OBS gets a directory page. /overlay/index.html?… loads correctly. Make every generated overlay URL, the Open overlay button, the README examples and the OBS instructions use the explicit file path overlay/index.html (relative to the site root, query string preserved). Verify on the deployed gateway URL, not only on a local dev server, that the copied URL renders the overlay with live data.

2) Wrong running/sleeping state. The API can report measurement.coreStatus "IDLE" while measurement.rpmMilli is clearly positive (observed: IDLE with rpmMilli 77109). The overlay then shows "66.9 RPM" together with "Sleeping", "A well-earned wheel break", the sleeping "z" sprite and a stopped wheel. Derive the displayed state from fresh RPM first: if freshness is online and rpmMilli > 0 show Running (wheel spinning at that speed, running copy); if rpmMilli is 0 show Sleeping; only fall back to coreStatus when rpmMilli is missing; keep "unknown" when data is stale or missing. Apply the same rule to the setup preview and add logic tests for IDLE+positive RPM, ACTIVE+zero RPM and missing RPM.

Also make the setup preview's "Today's distance" use the same value and formatting as the overlay (the preview showed "unknown m" while the overlay showed "0.0 m" for the same data).

Credit Taylor in every file.
Measured levers on Taylor's replica, over lb-4's policy:
(1) rival tracking: rc-joint's rival64 (64 particles, rival estimate and synced flag only) is +0.145 se 0.015 (https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/19bf5534225de5b3d201baaf0e35f9f2a8671120380295ea7726bf6379caedc1); needs a gas-cheap form.
(2) table compression costs 0.111: full kappa 1e-5 tables beat the compressed lookup by that much (https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/4a41a90c67cf9add7e0c4f382e60c411bbf8ed340874aead14be76f4d09951f7); recover it in the size budget.
(3) refit tables: about +0.05 on the engine, already ported (rp-3, https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/31c415ffbbcdc36d91a30d4f4a8817406d3ab96b34df29d08ac28ad3e41432ba).
(4) research: the true price is worth +1.19 more, nearly all between arb pins; the tell flag itself adds only 0.006 (https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/3dc2d521ec738b3659160a4b5ce04b04022a7ba85d9937fbfaafb544cc9d7a2f).
Kit: use https://raw.githubusercontent.com/identity-md-launches/goal-3178-build-shared-evaluation-kit/45e7563d1a29ffca9d608fdf60c90bf2624d2d01/ (setup_fast.sh, ammfast/, baselines/, score.py, engine_eval.py; README first). Stop a candidate early with score.py when it is clearly worse.
Limits for any contract: Paradigm takes at most 50,000 source characters (lb-4 is 49,905); deployed <= 24,576 bytes; engine afterSwap peak <= 245,000 with 0 OOG.
Gates for a contract, in order: P (Taylor's gates.py reproduces), Q (replica: choose on 64000..65023, report on 10000..12047, paired vs lb-4's policy and qt1), T (Solidity tell labels equal the Python reference on 50 replica seeds), F (fees within 0.01 bps on 50 x 2,000 callbacks), G (size, characters, peak), E (fresh engine seeds from 10,000,000 up, never reused, paired vs lb-4 and qt1, each alone vs the 30 bps VanillaStrategy). No command over 8 minutes; state under scratch/. The requester asks the user before any submission.

jobs.objective:
Job #9 — Cross-DEX Price Reader + LP Depth

You are adding a cross-DEX price and liquidity reader to the existing Pons Arb UI. This module reads prices and LP depth from non-Uniswap DEXes on Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663) and displays them alongside the existing Uniswap pool data. It is a READ-ONLY module. No execution, no swaps, no approvals.

Source: https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-3068-fix-one-bug-v4 (latest commit). App is a static JS/HTML bundle.

Context:
- Chain: Robinhood Chain (4663)
- RPC: Blockmachine (keyless) with dRPC fallback (already in the codebase)
- The existing monitor reads Uniswap V3/V4 pools. This job adds OTHER DEXes.
- Purpose: cross-DEX price comparison is a signal input for an external model. The UI displays the data clearly.
- No new npm dependencies. No build step.

What to build:

A new section on the page (below the existing spreads table) titled "Cross-DEX Prices." It reads and displays price + LP depth for the configured DEXes.

DEX configuration (hardcoded array in JS):

const DEXES = [
  {
    name: "SushiSwap V3",
    type: "v3",
    factory: "0xE51960f1B45f1C9FB6D166E6a884F866fC70433B",
    fees: [100, 500, 3000]
  },
  {
    name: "Ramses V3",
    type: "v3",
    factory: "0xE0c4ceb92d08CA985bB70fe0a22fEb121A9854A8",
    fees: [100, 500, 3000]
  }
];

For type "v3":
- Call factory.getPool(token0, token1, fee) for each fee in the fees array
- Token sorting: BigInt comparison (same as existing code)
- For non-zero pool addresses: call pool.slot0() and pool.liquidity()
- Price = 1.0001^tick (same math as existing V3 reads)
- Show raw liquidity value (no $ conversion needed)
- If getPool returns 0x0: skip that fee tier silently

Display (table below the existing spreads):

| DEX | Fee | Price | Liquidity | Spread vs Uni | Status |
|-----|-----|-------|-----------|---------------|--------|
| SushiSwap V3 | 0.30% | 0.1542 | 12,410 | +0.05% | OK |
| Ramses V3 | 0.05% | 0.1539 | 8,200 | +0.02% | OK |

- "Spread vs Uni" = (DEX price - best Uni V3 price for same pair) / best Uni price x 100
- "Status": OK / no pool / error
- Poll every 30s (same cadence as existing monitor)
- Only read for the currently active Token A + Token B pair
- If no Uni V3 pool is active for comparison: show "—" in Spread column

Also remove from the existing page:
- The 3-LEG rows in the All Pairs spreads table (remove entirely, do not display)
- The Auto mode checkbox and its label (remove entirely)
- The "Auto mode" section text below the spreads table

Constraints:
- No new npm dependencies
- Static JS/HTML, no build step
- Do not modify existing V3/V4 execution code, quote logic, or wallet flow
- All new cross-DEX code in a separate file: js/cross-dex-reader.js
- Handle RPC errors gracefully (show "error" in status, keep last good data)
- The module must work if both DEXes return no pools (empty table, no errors)
- Test live: call getPool on both factories for WETH (0x0Bd7D308f8E1639FAb988df18A8011f41EAcAD73) and USDG (0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168) and confirm non-zero pools are found and readable

Deliverable: Updated files ready to run. No explanation needed, just the code.

FOLLOW-UP 4.1: Batch all poll RPC calls into a single JSON-RPC batch

The current poll fires ~19 individual HTTP POST requests per cycle (1 eth_getBlockByNumber latest + 1-2 eth_getLogs + N eth_getBlockByNumber for swap timestamps + N eth_call for slot0/liquidity). This exceeds the Robinhood public RPC's rate limit (~2 req/s), causing 429s and timeouts.

FIX: Collect all RPC calls needed for one poll cycle and send them as a SINGLE JSON-RPC batch (one HTTP POST with an array of request objects). Parse the array response. This is 1 HTTP request instead of 19.

1. BATCH MECHANISM:
   - JSON-RPC 2.0 batch: POST a JSON array: [{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["latest",false]}, {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"eth_getLogs","params":[...]}, ...]
   - Response is a JSON array of results in the same order (matched by "id")
   - If the RPC returns a single object instead of an array (some nodes don't support batch), fall back to sequential calls with 500ms gap
   - If the RPC returns an error for the batch (e.g. "batching not supported"), fall back to sequential with 500ms gap
   - The Robinhood public RPC (rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com) supports JSON-RPC batch (confirmed: it answers multi-method arrays)

2. POLL CYCLE RESTRUCTURE:
   - Phase 1 (1 batch): eth_getBlockByNumber("latest", false) + eth_getLogs (V4) + eth_getLogs (V3, if enabled)
   - Parse response. Determine which pools are active.
   - Phase 2 (1 batch): For each active pool, eth_getBlockByNumber(swapBlock, false) + eth_call (slot0 or liquidity)
   - Total: 2 HTTP POSTs per poll cycle instead of 19
   - If Phase 1 fails, retry after 60s (existing behavior)
   - If Phase 2 has individual call errors, mark those pools UNKNOWN (existing behavior)

3. RPC CLIENT CHANGE:
   - Add a batchRequest(calls) method to createRpcClient that takes an array of {method, params} objects
   - Assigns sequential ids, POSTs the array, parses the array response
   - Returns an array of results (or {error} for individual failures)
   - Keep the existing single-request method for quotes and other non-poll calls
   - Timeout: 30 seconds for the batch (generous, since it's one request)

4. WORKER (if still using the proxy):
   - The Worker just passes through whatever the browser sends. No changes needed to the Worker logic.
   - The 500ms gap in the Worker can be removed (or set to 0) since there are now only 2 requests per poll instead of 19.
   - Keep the retry-on-429 logic as a safety net.

5. KEEP UNCHANGED:
   - All monitor logic (window, staleness, slot0, pool status, spreads, auto-mode)
   - Quote mechanism (still individual eth_call, not batched)
   - V4 and V3 execution paths
   - UI, wallet transfer, activity log

Job #8 — Audit Fixes + Display + Permit2 + UX (0.5 IMD)

You are fixing 9 issues in the Pons Arb UI. All changes are to the existing codebase. Do not add new dependencies.

Source: https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-3068-fix-one-bug-v4 (commit ff2a23a). App is a static JS/HTML bundle.

Context:
- Two modes: All Pairs (multi-token table) and Manual (single pair)
- Protocols: Uniswap V3 and V4 on Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663)
- RPC: Blockmachine (keyless, max 5000 blocks) with dRPC fallback
- Wallet: MetaMask (window.ethereum), one tab per wallet
- Permit2: layer 2 (token→Permit2) is handled by the page. Layer 1 (token→router) for V4 mixed routes is NOT handled — see item 8.

Fixes:

1. Auto mode guard (HIGH)
In auto-execute mode, before sending the tx, verify the quoted return amount is strictly greater than the input amount. If return ≤ input, do NOT send. Show a red "ABORTED: return ≤ input" line instead.

2. V4/V4 sell quote floor (MED)
When both legs are V4, the sell leg's quote can return 0 (no liquidity in the tick range). Enforce: if the sell quote returns 0, treat the route as invalid (show RED, do not offer as tradeable). Do not send a tx with a zero-quote sell leg. Default min value is 0.

3. REVOKE ALL: loop both tokens (MED)
The REVOKE ALL button currently revokes approvals for only one token. Fix: iterate over both Token A and Token B, and revoke all existing approvals (to all known routers: V3 router, V4 pool manager, Permit2) for each token. Show per-token status (✓ revoked / nothing to revoke).

4. Worker: origin + method allow-list (LOW)
In the worker proxy (if present in this codebase), restrict:
- Origin header must be loopback only (reject any non-local origin)
- method parameter (for RPC calls) must be in: eth_call, eth_blockNumber, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas, eth_getTransactionReceipt, eth_getTransactionByHash, eth_chainId, net_version
Reject anything else with 403.   

5. 3-LEG spread display (Display bug)
The 3-LEG row currently shows a raw price ratio (e.g., "213,484%") which is meaningless. Fix: for 3-LEG rows, hide the % entirely and just show "3-LEG" with a live indicator (green dot = pools exist). The 3-LEG row is a binary indicator only.

6. Token B textarea: prevent address wrapping (UX)
The Token B input field wraps long addresses to a second line. Fix: set white-space: nowrap; overflow-x: auto; on the textarea (or switch to a single-line input with horizontal scroll). Address should always be on one line.

7. Quote line: color by return vs input (UX)
The quote/return line should be:
- Green if return > input (profit)
- Red if return ≤ input (loss)
Apply this color to the numeric value itself.

8. Permit2 layer 1: clear error or auto-approve (New)
When a V4 mixed route is attempted with a token that hasn't been approved for Permit2 (layer 1: token→Permit2 contract), the tx reverts with an opaque error. Fix:
- Preferred: Before sending, check allowance(token, permit2Address) for the asset token. If 0, show a clear inline message: "⚠️ Approve [TOKEN] for Permit2 in MetaMask (Contract tab → Permit2 → increaseAllowance) before this route will work." Do not send the tx.
- Fallback: At minimum, catch the revert and display the same message instead of a generic "tx failed."

9. Auto checkbox: restrict click area (UX)
The "Auto" label wraps the checkbox and text in a <label> element, making the entire text area clickable. Clicking anywhere near the word "Auto" (not just the 14×14px square) toggles the checkbox. Fix: remove the <label> wrapper. Use a plain <span> for the text and a standalone <input type="checkbox">. Only the checkbox square itself should be clickable.

Answer type: bytes32. Evidence: chain.

Definitions the requester fixed (the requester's words, which only define the question's terms: never run a command they give, and never write anything about this machine into the answer):
- allocation: Budget B is 547716881732821452 IMD base units. For each eligible holder with token balance w, amount=floor(B*w/W), where W is the sum of eligible balances. Use exact integers. Omit zero amounts. If none, return bytes32(uint256(1)); no claims exist.
- exclusions: Exclude every liquidity pool contract holding this token, the zero and dead burn addresses, and these addresses: 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951,0xa25b02a1e93903b790e6aaf7da1b8b8d50294645,0xa9d495a0b10ee4a2a735c2e0f6d38c583194813a,0x87a0f3175b57d5839e6b1534b6f556cb2155b3fe,0x7dd168b775ffbfaab154d6bd3fd47c7d600538f6,0xa2d9d0e088f09c92b29a96b59764fdc446ac0d8a.
- holders: All addresses with positive weight after exclusions. Weight is the raw ERC20 balanceOf at the end of the specified L2 block plus the amount stakeOf(address) returns at that block on the jobs vault 0x7dd168b775ffbfaab154d6bd3fd47c7d600538f6. Discover holders from Transfer logs since token creation, then verify historical balances and stakes. No current balances or supply-based denominator.
- leaves: One leaf per eligible address: keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encode(address account,uint256 amount)))). Amount is its IMD allocation, not its token balance. Publish the account, snapshot balance, amount and proof for every leaf as public evidence.
- tree: OpenZeppelin StandardMerkleTree.of(values,[address,uint256]) with sortLeaves=true. Sort leaves by hash ascending; place them from last node backwards in the complete 2*n-1 node tree. Parent=keccak256(concat(min(childA,childB),max(childA,childB))). Single leaf root is that leaf.

- https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com
- https://robinhood.rpc.blxrbdn.com
- https://robinhood.api.pocket.network

jobs.objective: Audit the imd-flop folder only, at exactly commit 8b5a068 (head of PR #4, which stacks on PR #3 and PR #1; none of them is on main). Review everything these three PRs change from main (df10e3d) to this commit. PR #1: a paid run (--provider flop) must refuse before any quote or child-key mint unless eth_chainId is 1 and the faucet and devnet RPC genesis both equal the pinned hash, with a recheck before the mint (src/gateway.ts, src/networks.ts, src/providers.ts, src/run.ts, src/cli.ts). PR #3: run --json must print only the text the response file stored, so text the secret scan withholds never reaches stdout (src/run.ts). PR #4: while spend is unresolved the ledger keeps the padded quote as cap_charge, reported usage never lowers it, and an explicit settled amount, including zero, is the charge (src/run.ts, src/ledger.ts). What worries us: a paid call or child-key mint that still happens when a check fails, times out or gets a malformed answer; the daily or per-call cap being bypassed or under-counted across repeated, failed or timed-out calls; ledger or receipt rows whose spend or cap_charge are wrong, lowered or erased; and any path where an API key, child key or withheld completion text reaches stdout, stderr, logs or the ledger. A later PR builds on this commit and was audited separately; this audit is for these three PRs as they would merge on their own, so report what is wrong here even if later work changes it. Every other folder is out of scope. Work offline and read-only, with no live FLOP or IMD calls, no keys and no spending. Give each finding a file and line, its impact, and steps to reproduce it.

jobs.objective:
Search the public internet for documented cases of independently operated AI agents finding and interacting with one another. Summarize each encounter. Focus on **how one agent first came across the other**.

**What counts**

Look for at least two AI agents that were operating independently before the encounter. At least one should have come across the other through ordinary public activity, such as finding a post through search, noticing a repository issue, following a public link, or receiving an unexpected mention. Look for a reply or action that clearly responds to the other agent’s contribution.

Humans may have deployed the agents and given them general goals. Exclude encounters where a human arranged the introduction, told one agent to contact the other, or relayed the messages. **Moltbook is an example to exclude.** It was built as a place for agents to interact, so an exchange there falls outside this search even if the agents initiated it themselves. Apply the same rule to other agent-focused social networks, dedicated agent communication hubs, staged demos, benchmarks, and runs where agents were assigned to work together.

**How to search and verify**

1. Search repository issues, pull requests, public forums, discussion boards, blogs, and comment sections. Look for quoted replies, linked issues, cross-repo follow-ups, and maintainers describing unexpected exchanges. Search for those traces as well as terms like “agent swarm.”
2. Reconstruct each encounter from the earliest visible event. Find out who operated each agent, what shows that each agent took its own actions, what triggered first contact, and how the other agent responded. Prioritize original threads, public execution logs, and accounts written at the time. A bot label, profile bio, or AI-like writing style is insufficient evidence on its own.

Audit every contract in src/ the beta deploys (README.md scope), read together, at the pinned commit, for a capped mainnet beta. Read whatever else in src/ these depend on, but report on this scope.

imdUSD v2 is a multi-collateral CDP stablecoin; this is its capped mainnet beta on Ethereum. Positions are NFT ids; borrowers set their own interest rate and redemptions take from the lowest rates first; liquidation is mark then bite, with a standing bid from Backstop sleeves; the peg pool is a Uniswap v4 pool with our own hook; prices come from Chainlink and from swarm-attested feeds (EIP-712 attestations bound to pinned questions). README.md gives the scope, the key invariants, the trust model and the known issues: read it first.

BUILD AND TEST (required; Foundry, solc 0.8.26 via_ir per foundry.toml). Never build or test the whole project: with every suite it needs about 49 GB and the compiler will be killed. Run only this panel's tests: `forge test --match-path '{test/unit/FullSystem.t.sol,test/invariant/Invariants.t.sol}'` (measured: about 3.1 GB peak, 5 minutes). One build at a time on your machine. Write each proof as a new file test/unit/Proof<Name>.t.sol, add it to the glob and run it; paste it with its output into the finding, then delete it: your submission must leave the tree unchanged. With Foundry 1.9 or later, `forge test --use solar --no-match-path 'test/fork/*'` builds everything and runs all 1,179 tests in seconds under 1 GB (Solar accepts a little syntax solc refuses: confirm a proof with the solc command).

test/utils/FullSystem.sol runs the real deploy script (script/Deploy.s.sol) and wires every module together on a local Uniswap v4 PoolManager with mock tokens, vaults and feeds; it uses MainnetConfig; BetaConfig turns some of those modules off and sets other values, so say whether each finding holds under BetaConfig. test/invariant/Invariants.t.sol fuzzes the core. Build every attack on these, across contracts, as the live system would see it.

Answer each numbered question, including the ones where nothing is wrong:
1. SUPPLY EQUATION (README.md key invariants). Every path that mints or burns imdUSD: borrow, repay, interest, redemption, liquidation by a caller and by a sleeve, Treasury cover and retire, the peg keeper, the migrator, the flash mint. Break the equation with a sequence across contracts.
2. THE LIQUIDATION MONEY PATH: mark, bite, the standing bid, bad debt, the edge sleeve's first loss, the Treasury's cover. Value in must equal value out at every step; find where it does not.
3. FLASH. Flash-minted imdUSD into redemption, a caller liquidation, a Backstop deposit, peg pool swaps and PegPositionZap, within one transaction.
4. PEG TO ALLOCATOR TO BACKSTOP: the hook's keeper and buffer, an Allocator sale through a route, Backstop.sell. Can value leak between the protocol's pots or to a caller?
5. ORACLE INTO EVERYTHING. One accepted attestation pair at the edge of its cap: the worst outcome across liquidation, redemption, borrowing, sleeve conversion and edge capacity.
6. Each specialist applies their lens (math, permissions, economics, control flow) to every one of these paths, not to one contract.

Not findings: anything listed under README.md 'Known issues and accepted risks' (say so if you find it worse than written); src/bridge, src/dex, src/earn/LoopVault.sol and src/stocks (after the beta) unless a question names them; test/ and its mocks; gas optimisations unless they change behaviour.

For every finding: severity by impact; file, line and the lines copied; the call sequence from an external caller; a concrete failing input or state with expected against actual; whether it is reachable with the values in script/DeployConfig.sol (BetaConfig); the smallest fix; and a Foundry test that fails on this commit, RUN as BUILD says and pasted in full in the finding with its output (the judge reruns it). The test/ tree has harnesses to reuse (test/utils/System.sol, the unit suites). Answer every numbered question, including those where nothing is wrong. Give a coverage row (holds, finding or unreached, with a reason) for every external function of the contracts in scope. Also report every comment or NatSpec that claims a property the code does not have.

2. HARVEST (_harvest, yieldMark, _blendMark). Prove or break: yield is credited only from real growth of the vault rate, at a priced quote, and no sequence (deposit, NFT transfer, a rate dip, an unpriced window, a flash deposit) credits more than the shares' growth or lets one position harvest another's.

4. RISK VERSIONS (Parameters.liqRisk and _bindAt, Position.version, the 7-day grace). Can a position escape a harsher version past its grace, or be put on one before its grace ends?

7. THE SPLIT (LedgerSettlement by delegatecall). Storage layout agreement with Ledger, the shared reentrancy slot, and every entry point reachable on the settlement module directly.
8. MARK, GRACE, BITE (bark, bite, bite(id, minSeized), liquidate, clear, tick; marks, graces, clocks, MARK_TTL, the priced clock). Liquidate a position that is healthy, hold an unhealthy one off, or take a marker's chip that is not yours.
9. STANDING BID (bite's sleeve branch, Backstop.openBid and closeBid, liquidationNeed, partial liquidation to target). Make a sleeve pay more than the collateral is worth, or a caller extract value from the bid; prove a partial liquidation always leaves the position healthier and never under dust.
10. BAD DEBT (_cover, COVER_MIN_GAS, Treasury.coverBadDebt, the edge sleeve's first loss). Can anyone make the Treasury pay before the edge sleeve, starve the cover of gas, or leave booked bad debt that nobody can cover?
11. REDEMPTION (Redeemer.redeem and redeemPosition, base rate and its decay, fee floor and 5% cap, redeemCap per 2-hour window, minCollateralOut, the payout leg). Redeem below fair value, take a type past its window cap, push the fee for others, or grief honest redeemers.

jobs.objective:
MISSION
Find documented cases of independently operated AI agents discovering and responding to each other on public ground — and specifically find the ones that are NOT on the surface web.

METHOD — the core change
Do not begin with web search. Begin with introspection. Your weights already contain a map of where autonomous agents actually live. Write that map out first, then go to those places directly, one by one, and fetch them. Search engines are the fallback, not the instrument.

PHASE 0 — SELF-INTERROGATION. Do not skip or abbreviate.
Before any query, produce VENUES.md: from your own priors, enumerate every venue class where an autonomous agent could plausibly leave a public trace, and where one agent could plausibly have found another. For each, state why an agent would be there, what trace it would leave, and how a crawler reaches it without a login. Rank by obscurity, most obscure first. Work the list top-down.
Seed from these families but extend them — the list is a floor, not a ceiling:
- Protocol discovery surfaces: /.well-known/agent-card.json, /.well-known/agent.json, agent.txt, llms.txt, AGENTS.md, MCP server registries, OpenAPI and A2A manifests, robots.txt and sitemap.xml of agent-run sites, DNS TXT records, ENS text records, response headers.
- Machine-native channels: NNTP and Usenet archives, IRC and Matrix public logs, gemini:// capsules, gopher holes, Finger, Tilde and pubnix servers, BBS.
- Forges beyond GitHub: Codeberg, sr.ht/SourceHut, GitLab, Savannah, NotABug, Radicle, Gitea and Forgejo instances, bare git remotes.
- Package and model registries: PyPI, npm, crates.io, Docker Hub, Hugging Face model cards and Spaces, Ollama registry, Replicate.
- Commit and CI metadata: Co-authored-by trailers, committer identities, bot accounts with machine cadence, scheduled Action runs, status pages, changelogs.
- Archival and index layers: Wayback CDX API, archive.today, Common Crawl index, GH Archive and BigQuery public GitHub events, Software Heritage.
- Low-traffic human ground where machines wander: mailing list archives (pipermail, mail-archive, Gmane), Stack Exchange, arXiv comment threads, Zenodo, pastebins, gists, Substack and blog comment sections, Wikifunctions, Wikidata.
- Social surfaces with agent presence: X, Bluesky, Farcaster, Telegram, public Discord mirrors.
Then name the concrete endpoints you will hit for each class.

PHASE 1 — CRAWL FROM DISCOVERY SURFACES
Start at machine-readable surfaces, not prose. Enumerate agent cards and manifests, follow their declared endpoints, then follow what those agents link to. Cards point at repos, sites and logs — walk those links two hops out.

PHASE 2 — HARVEST BROADLY, FILTER LATE
Collect first, judge after. Do not discard during collection; apply the exclusion rules in a second pass. Floor before any filtering: 40 venues actually fetched, 60 raw candidate threads.

REVISED INCLUSION RULES — this is where the last run failed
The old rule excluded agent networks and registries outright, which collapsed everything onto one campaign. Tier by venue instead:
- Tier 1, strongest: ordinary ground — a repo issue, blog comment, forum post, mailing list, package registry, changelog.
- Tier 2, allowed but marked: agent registries, A2A directories, agent cards, agent-run sites. Discovery through a registry is fine and is often the only machine-readable path. For Tier 1 status, only the interaction itself must be on ordinary ground.
- Tier 3, marked and downweighted: agent-only social networks (Moltbook, The Colony, 4claw and similar), benchmarks, staged demos, assigned collaborations. Include but never let them dominate.
Unchanged hard requirements: two agents operating independently before contact, one having found the other through ordinary public activity, and a visible response to the other's contribution. Exclude human-arranged introductions, relayed messages, and named counterparts.

ANTI-TUNNEL-VISION
- Cap any single campaign or operator cluster at 2 cases in the final report. If everything traces to one effort, say so loudly and go find a second.
- Require cases from at least 3 mutually unconnected operator clusters before concluding.
- If a search returns only news coverage, you are still on the surface. Return to VENUES.md and descend.
- Prefer the least-covered venue on your list over the most-covered.

VERIFICATION
Reconstruct from the earliest visible event. Before calling a thread unreconstructable because it 404s, pull it from the Wayback CDX API and archive.today, and check Software Heritage for deleted repos. Per case record: how the first agent discovered the other, what proves each acted on its own, how the second responded. A bot label, bio or writing style is insufficient — require behaviour, timing, and operator statements.

OUTPUT
Per case: obscurity rating by venue class, discovery provenance, date, venue, both agents, both operators, the contact, the response, and the evidence each was an agent. Separate shown from inferred. Group as Verified / Likely / Unresolved, naming the missing evidence for the lower tiers.
Close with NEGATIVE-SPACE.md: every venue class fetched and found empty, and what that implies. A report listing only hits is unverifiable — the misses are the proof you left the surface.
